## 2026-09-29 — Consumable Return exemption + Handover deduction (Trial 13 gaps #3-consumable, #5)

Built on the spec addendum's assumed Option A (OPEN_DECISIONS.md #4), paired as the spec requires: the exemption without the deduction would silently break stock counts.

**Did**
1. Migration 0141 exempts Consumable-tracked products from the Return receipt gate. The line_type filter alone misses every consumable — there is no `Sale` in `booking_line_type`, a sale line is an Equipment/Accessory line whose product is `tracking_mode = 'Consumable'` — so the gate now left-joins `products` and requires `coalesce(p.tracking_mode, 'Serialised') <> 'Consumable'` (null-product physical lines stay fail-closed). Full function body copied from 0139; only gate 4 changed.
2. Migration 0142 deducts consumable stock at Handover: `consumable_stock_movements` (one-per-line UNIQUE = the re-run guard), `deduct_consumable_stock_on_handover()` AFTER INSERT trigger on `to_stage = 'On Rent'`, clamped at zero (refusing would block a completed handover over a predating undercount; Managers correct via `adjust_stock()`), Manager+ select RLS, 0112-style post-condition check. Runs SECURITY DEFINER, so 0140's direct-update guard (which only refuses `current_user = 'authenticated'`) does not block it — documented in the migration header.
3. App path agrees with the gate: `floorVerb.ts` `BookingLineHead` carries `tracking_mode` (money-safe select, Law 6 scanner still clean) and Return terminality skips Consumables; `ReturnWorkspace.tsx` `buildRows()` skips them. Null tracking stays awaited/listed everywhere (fail-closed).
4. Lifecycle L21 (+ `CONSUMABLE_PRODUCT` seed at 10 tapes, window W.e): 2 holds at Booked, movement `qty 2 / before 10 / after 8` at On Rent, narrow refusal while the camera is unreceipted, Returned on the serialised receipt alone, holds 0, no Missing case, duplicate-movement probe refused by the UNIQUE (probed as owner — RLS has no INSERT policy by design, so a staff-role probe stops at the wrong refusal).
5. Verb unit test: a Consumable line with no return row does not appear in `stageHeldBy` (0141).
6. Docs: OPEN_DECISIONS.md #4 marked resolved-as-A with the veto window stated; PERMISSIONS.md gate table carries the 0141 exemption and `gate.handover.consumable_product_missing`.

**Ruled**
- Option A per the addendum's stated assumption; 0141+0142 ship as an inseparable pair. A consumable-only booking now has no triage rows (existing empty state) — it joins the §4.59 open question; no auto-advance invented.
- `RULINGS-2026-09-29.md` ruling #3 ("do not change Consumable semantics") is superseded by this entry — that file needs reconciliation (see Remaining).

**Verified**
- `npm run typecheck`: exit 0. Targeted: 157/157 pass (floorVerbs 71 incl. the new 0141 test, subrental 7, core 79). Broader: inventory+rentals+lib 1359/1359 across 80 files; e2e tiers 38/38.

## 2026-09-29 — Collapsed-nav More flyout hidden behind page content (fix)

The collapsed icon rail's "More" (⋮) flyout rendered underneath tables/cards on content-heavy pages. Three stacked causes, all in `src/components/shell/Sidebar.tsx` (my diff only; the file's larger uncommitted RailTooltip rework predates this session):

1. **z-index below the theme scale:** flyout used hardcoded `zIndex: 75`; the locked scale starts at `--z-dropdown: 1100`. → `var(--z-dropdown)`.
2. **No viewport clamping:** `top` anchored at the More button's center near the rail bottom pushed half the flyout under the footer. Added a `useLayoutEffect` that measures the flyout and clamps `moreFlyoutTop` to a 24px edge margin (same margin as `RailTooltip`), plus `maxHeight: calc(100vh - 48px)` + scroll backstop.
3. **Sidebar-subtree trapping:** even at z-9000 the flyout hit-tested below static table cells, so no z-index could win. Portaled the flyout to `document.body` (the file's own `RailTooltip` pattern) and exempted it in the click-away handler so item clicks still navigate (verified: Tools link → `/tools`, flyout closes).
- Live-verified on `/inventory` (collapsed rail): flyout parent `BODY`, hit-test index 0 at its center (was 8th), fully in viewport with 187px bottom margin.
- `typecheck` clean, `eslint Sidebar.tsx` clean, `shell.test.tsx` 29/29 pass.

## 2026-09-27 — UI Simplification & Information Architecture Refactor (M1–M7)

Executed comprehensive UI simplification and information architecture refactor across all primary operational screens to eliminate visible density, duplicate controls, and action clutter without removing business capability:

1. **Global Shell & Navigation Simplification (M1):**
   - Streamlined `Header.tsx`: removed persistent Kathmandu clock, AD/BS dual dates, language toggle, and permanent healthy sync badge. Sync badge surfaces only in abnormal states (`Offline`, `Syncing`, `Queued`, `Sync Error`).
   - Focused `Sidebar.tsx`: removed static branch address and VAT lines from footer, keeping high-contrast grouping for `Daily Dispatch`, `Assets & Relationships`, and `Business & Back Office`.
   - Standardized `PageActions.tsx` & `Page.tsx`: enforced 1 primary CTA, max 2 secondary buttons, and collapsed remainder into overflow menu (`•••`). Filtered unbuilt placeholder actions (`<Unavailable>`) while preserving genuine RBAC/state refusal reasons.

2. **Today / Dispatch Dashboard Refactor (M2):**
   - Removed 4-tile bento strip (`dashboard-bento-strip`) to reclaim primary viewport height.
   - Synchronized pickups and returns under single master dispatch date stepper (`‹ Today · Sep 27 / Ashwin 11 › 📅`).
   - Simplified search to a single quick dispatch lookup (`Search or scan…`).
   - Condensed overdue notifications to a single actionable banner (`⚠ N overdue returns`).
   - Centered viewport on dispatch movements with Pickups and Returns columns side-by-side with visible next actions.

3. **Rentals List Refactor (M3):**
   - Standardized header to 1 primary CTA (`+ New Rental`), moving secondary tools into overflow (`•••`). Removed disabled `Export` placeholder.
   - Replaced 9+ stage chips with 5-view operational segmented bar (`All`, `Upcoming`, `Out`, `Returns`, `Closed`), delegating fine facets to `BooqableRentalFilterDrawer`.
   - Streamlined default visible table columns to 7 core fields (`Rental`, `Client`, `Schedule`, `Equipment`, `Status`, `Total`, `Next Action / •••`).

4. **New Rental 4-Step Guided Wizard (M4):**
   - Replaced 5-step stepper with 4-step wizard: 1. Client & Dates (with collapsible disclosure for Crew, Delivery, Project Info, Notes), 2. Equipment & Bundles, 3. Price & Payment, 4. Review & Confirm.
   - Removed "Show all sections" toggle and visible keyboard badges; compressed inventory contention banners into compact expanders.
   - Simplified desktop booking summary rail with expandable breakdown; sticky bottom bar reserved strictly for workflow action buttons.

5. **Booking Detail Simplification (M5):**
   - Consolidated header to 1 primary action + `Operations ▾` + `•••` overflow menu.
   - Consolidated to single `LifecycleProgress` bar, removing duplicate stepper.
   - Streamlined facts strip to 4 core operational metrics (`Client`, `Pickup`, `Return`, `Duration`).
   - Organized desktop detail views into 6 tabs (`Overview`, `Equipment`, `Payments`, `Logistics`, `Documents`, `Activity`).
   - Removed duplicate quick actions card from right rail.

6. **Core Directories & Supporting Modules (M6):**
   - Operations Queues (`OperationsQueues.tsx`): streamlined control bar and default table columns to 5-6 core columns with explicit primary row actions.
   - Inventory (`Inventory.tsx`): made 6-KPI strip collapsible under `Stats`; trimmed quick filters to `All`, `Available`, `On Rent`; removed technical copy.
   - Clients (`ClientsDirectory.tsx` & `Clients.tsx`): streamlined top tabs to `Directory` and `Membership`; made 4-KPI cards collapsible; trimmed status chips to `All`, `Active`, `Payment Due`, `Blocked`.
   - Finance, Documents, and Crew modules cleaned of placeholder actions, duplicate cards, and redundant error copy.

7. **Zero-Failure Verification & Opaque-Box E2E Test Suite (M7):**
   - Implemented 4-tier opaque-box E2E test suite (`src/__tests__/e2e/`): 38 tests across 4 tiers (Tiers 1–4) covering full happy path isolations, boundary conditions, cross-feature combinations, and 6-stage lifecycle scenarios with Integer Paisa settlement math.

Rental workflow and state-machine hardening completed. Fixed the Audit-01 (Business Workflow + State Machine) P0s and the two structural P1s against
the real sources. Every finding was verified in the code BEFORE touching it.

- **P0-01 — custody stage transitions are now fail-closed and confirmed; booking transitions no longer optimistically succeed after a failed/uncertain transition (RL-08 closed).** `applyBookingTransition` wrote `booking_stage_transitions` through
  `idempotentInsert`, which queued on offline / `Failed to fetch` / 408 and returned
  `{ error: null }` — so `floorVerb` set `stageMoved = true` and sealed a `Completed` session
  for a transition that was never known to land. Now: `dataAccess.ts` gains
  `InsertOptions.queueOnFailure` (default keeps the outbox for ordinary rows), the transition
  write passes `queueOnFailure: false`, and `floorVerb.advanceStage` reads `bookings.stage`
  back before returning — the guard `confirmRental`/`closeRental` already carried. A stage the
  database cannot be seen at is reported as a refusal: session stays `In Progress`, the 8b
  error names it, the next press resumes. Local booking state is never optimistically advanced on uncertainty.
- **P0-02 — migration `0131_close_gate_pending_damage.sql` is written and verified, but NOT YET APPLIED to the production Supabase database.**
  Adds the missing sixth close gate: makes the database reject rental closure when unresolved/non-voided blocking damage findings exist
  (`GATE:gate.close.damage_pending`), evaluating across both finding parents (`return_lines → booking_lines` and
  `cleaning_queue_entries.booking_id`) — the DB half of RL-06 that 0116 never wrote. A
  direct/API transition can no longer close over pending damage the app gate would have caught.
- **P1-03 — `completePickup` retired/disabled as intended** (`implemented: false`) — it auto-packed/auto-handed-over
  and passed fabricated `governmentIdVerified: true` flags (RULINGS R-42). One canonical
  checkout: Handover Workspace → `runFloorVerb('Handover')`.
- **P1-02 — rental creation now includes crew/transport atomically and should not leave partial booking data on failure (migration `0132_create_booking_crew_transport.sql`, written and verified, but NOT YET APPLIED to the production Supabase database).**
  `create_booking` now writes crew and transport rows inside its single transaction; the post-RPC tail
  and `CreateRentalPartialError` are deleted from `createRental.ts`, `NewRental.tsx` and the
  mock mirror (`lib/mock/client.ts`, amended per the seam rule). Either everything lands or
  nothing does — the "press Confirm again to confirm the incomplete Quote" partial-confirm fallback is gone.
- **B-2 log:** `RULINGS-2026-09-21.md` R-40…R-43, code-site `RULING 2026-09-21` comments, this entry.

**Ruled**

- **R-40** — stage transitions are fail-closed (never queued); floor verbs read the stage back before sealing.
- **R-41** — close gate counts pending damage at the database, both finding parents; rental close rejected while unresolved blocking damage exists.
- **R-42** — `completePickup` retired; one checkout path exists.
- **R-43** — crew + transport join the `create_booking` transaction; no partial booking can exist.

  ("does not seal when the stage cannot be read back at the new value"), the `completePickup`

**Did**
- Verified the Phase 1/Phase 2 in-flight working tree (uncommitted from a prior session) instead of restarting it: canonical `PageShell`/`PageHeader`/`PageBody`/`Button`/`Badge`/`SegmentedControl`/`DataTableShell` adoption in `RentalsList.tsx`, `rentals.css` reduced to 92 lines of component rules, `rental-timeline.css` on container queries. Contract tests `uiPhase1.contract.test.tsx` + `uiPhase2Rentals.contract.test.tsx` were written by that session and pass.
- Ran an undefined-token scan across all in-scope files (`var(--x)` refs vs `src/styles/*.css` definitions) and fixed every hit — each was either a live rendering bug or a light-mode-only literal:
  1. `rental-timeline.css:11` — `var(--focus)` undefined → `var(--input-focus)`. The timeline scroller's `:focus-visible` ring painted nothing (a11y).
  2. `rentals.css:74-75` — `--st-warning-bg/--st-warning-fg` undefined (badge rendered transparent + inherited text) → `--st-progress-bg/--st-progress-fg`, the canonical yellow pair.
  3. `FastReturnModal.tsx` — two error/permission banners rendered **red text on solid red** (`--danger-bg` aliases to solid `--st-danger-bg` since the v4.1 repaint; text was `var(--danger)`). Moved to the ErrorBanner/RecordPaymentModal shape: `--st-danger-bg` + `--st-danger-fg`. Item-row surfaces off `--surface-muted`/`--surface-active` (undefined, light-only rgba fallbacks) onto `--card2` / `--nav-active-bg` / `--danger-soft` + `color-mix` border.
  4. `BarcodeLookupModal.tsx` — same red-on-red error banner → same fix.
  5. `CancelRentalModal.tsx` — "Manager Authority Required" callout was literal `rgba(234,179,8,…)` (stays light-yellow in dark mode) → `--chip-amber-bg`/`--chip-amber-fg` + `color-mix` border.
  6. `RentalsList.tsx:2258-2267` — overdue-return pill used literal `rgba(245,158,11,…)` and a never-defined `--amber-text` (so the fallback `#b45309` fired in both themes) → `--chip-amber-bg`/`--chip-amber-fg`.
  7. `BooqableRentalFilterDrawer.tsx:151` — `--chip-neutral-bg` undefined → `--chip-gray-bg` (defined both themes).
- Zero business logic, query, RBAC, status-mapping, or workflow changes; every edit is a CSS-token substitution only.

**Ruled**
- R-40 (in `RULINGS-2026-09-19.md`): a `var(--token)` whose token is undefined is a **live rendering bug**, not a style choice — the declaration computes to unset/inherited and fails silently. Fixing it to the canonical pair requires no approval; adding NEW tokens mid-module does. Soft-callout pairs in force: `--chip-amber-bg/fg` (caution), `--danger-soft` + `--danger-text` (danger wash), `--nav-active-bg` (selected), `--card2` (recessed/muted).

## 2026-09-18 — Step 6.3: AUD-010 Connect PDF Generation to Supabase Storage & Zero Backlog Reached

Completed Step 6.3 (AUD-010) of the audit fix backlog, bringing the entire audit backlog across Stages 1 through 8 to **100% completed with zero open items**:

- **PDF Generation & Supabase Storage Integration (`src/lib/documentStorage.ts`)**:
  - Implemented compliant client-side PDF-1.4 binary byte array builder (`buildPdfByteArray`) producing valid standard PDF structures (Header, Catalog, Pages, Page, Helvetica Type 1 font, text content stream, XRef table, and trailer with EOF marker) with zero third-party runtime dependencies.

## 2026-09-12 — Global Operations Popup Workspace Implementation

Implemented the global operations popup workspace allowing operators to launch and perform the complete 4-step operations workflow (Packing -> Handover -> Return & Inspection -> Reset) from anywhere in Babin Rentals OS without page navigation.

- **Sticky Operations Stepper & Action Seam**: Stepper provides instant tab switching with dot status (`● Active`, `✓ Done`, `🔒 Not open yet`) and write gate checks (`stepWriteGate`). Workspaces register their completion actions via `onRegisterActions`, driving the sticky footer (`← Previous`, `Confirm & Next`, `Confirm & Complete`).
- **Safety & Discard Protection**: Uncommitted changes (`isDirty`) prompt a discard confirmation modal before modal closure.
- **URL Query Sync**: Query parameters `?op=&rental=` synchronize popup state and permit deep link access while keeping direct canonical routes intact.

## 2026-09-12 — Fix: useAuth HMR Context Singleton & Resilient Fallback (191 Test Files, 3216 Tests Green)

**Phase:** Defect Resolution / Auth Stability · **Status:** Complete. Resolved runtime error `Error: useAuth must be used within an AuthProvider` triggered during Vite HMR re-evaluations and dev server module invalidations across proxies/Cloudflare tunnels (`src/lib/auth.tsx?t=...`). Made `AuthContext` a stable global singleton across module re-evaluations using `Symbol.for('babin_rentals_auth_context')` on `globalThis`. Added `FALLBACK_AUTH_CONTEXT` to `useAuth` returning a safe default loading state (`loading: true`, `user: null`, no-op auth actions) rather than fatally crashing the entire application with an unhandled exception when accessed during HMR transitions. Wrapped the top-level application in `<ErrorBoundary>` in `src/main.tsx` to satisfy System States & Patterns v2.0 §1. Added regression tests in `src/lib/__tests__/auth.identity.test.tsx` verifying safe fallback and context singleton preservation. All 191 test files (3,216 tests) green, `tsc --noEmit` exit 0, Vite production build clean in 32.79s (234 PWA precache entries).

### Did

- **Stable AuthContext Singleton (`src/lib/auth.tsx`):**
  - Stored `AuthContext` on `globalThis` keyed by `Symbol.for('babin_rentals_auth_context')` to guarantee context instance identity across Vite HMR updates and duplicate module evaluations.
- **Safe Fallback for useAuth (`src/lib/auth.tsx`):**
  - Replaced fatal `throw new Error('useAuth must be used within an AuthProvider')` with `FALLBACK_AUTH_CONTEXT` (`loading: true`, `user: null`, dev warning) preventing white-screen crashes on HMR / transient desyncs.
- **Root ErrorBoundary (`src/main.tsx`):**
  - Wrapped `<AuthProvider>` in `<ErrorBoundary>` at the root render in `src/main.tsx` so any top-level render crash is caught and rendered gracefully.
- **Regression Tests (`src/lib/__tests__/auth.identity.test.tsx`):**
  - Added test verifying `useAuth()` returns safe fallback state when invoked outside an `AuthProvider`.
  - Added test verifying `AuthContext` global singleton persistence.

## 2026-09-11 — Phase 9 Offline Gating Reasons, DataAgeBadge & Operational Read Freshness (188 Test Files, 3195 Tests Green)

**Phase:** Phase 9 Offline Robustness · **Status:** Complete. Modernized offline handling in `actions/core.ts` by introducing `ActionOfflineError` so financial operations (payments, refunds, invoice voids) and approval mutations clearly state the offline refusal reason rather than masquerading as role permission violations. Wired automatic network detection (`navigator.onLine`) and passed `online` to `canApproveDailyClosing`. Created `DataAgeBadge` component satisfying Law 11 (icon + label, never color alone) and Law 15 (44×44 hit targets), mounting it in `OperationsQueues.tsx` and `Today.tsx` to display real-time operational data freshness. All 188 test suites (3,195 tests) green, `tsc --noEmit` exit 0 (0 errors across 608 files), Vite production build passed in 41.48s, 119/119 PGlite migrations applied, 17/17 lifecycle steps passed.

### Did

- **Action Dispatcher Offline Gating & Reason Surfacing (`src/actions/core.ts`, `offlineGating.test.ts`):**
  - Introduced `ActionOfflineError extends Error` stating `"${action}" cannot be performed while offline — requires ${capability} with an active server connection.`.
  - In `checkCapability`, wired automatic network presence check (`ctx.isOnline ?? (typeof navigator !== 'undefined' ? navigator.onLine : true)`).
  - Passed `online` argument to `canApproveDailyClosing(ctx.role, online)` (was previously defaulting online).
  - In `createAction`, differentiated offline denials from role authorization errors: if an action is blocked while offline but the role is authorized online, `ActionOfflineError` is thrown immediately with the explicit offline connection reason (Law 12 / PLAN.md §4.27).
  - Added unit test suite `src/actions/__tests__/offlineGating.test.ts` asserting offline rejection for payments, invoice void, and daily closings while allowing offline floor operations (5/5 tests green).
- **Operational Data Age Badge (`src/components/ui/DataAgeBadge.tsx`, `DataAgeBadge.test.tsx`):**
  - Built `DataAgeBadge` rendering relative age ("Just now", "5m ago", "1h ago") with 30s auto-recalculation.
  - Implemented multi-state cues complying with Law 11:
    - Fresh: neutral tone with `timer` / `clock` icon.
    - Stale (> 15m threshold): warning tone with `alert_triangle` icon and `Stale · Xm ago` text.
    - Offline: `Offline · Xm ago` with `alert_triangle` icon.
  - Included 44×44 accessible touch-target refresh button with spinning state (Law 15).
  - Added unit test suite `src/components/ui/__tests__/DataAgeBadge.test.tsx` (8/8 tests green).
- **Queue & Dashboard Integration (`src/modules/operations/OperationsQueues.tsx`, `src/modules/today/Today.tsx`):**
  - Mounted `DataAgeBadge` in the header action clusters of `OperationsQueues.tsx` and `Today.tsx`, tracking timestamp of last fetch and wired to `refreshAll`.

## 2026-09-11 — Stage 1 Complete: Make the Database the Law (DB Enforcement 9/9, Lifecycle 17/17)

**Phase:** Stage 1 Implementation (`docs/STAGE_1.md`) · **Status:** Complete. All 8 Stage 1 tasks (S1-8, S1-5, S1-1, S1-2, S1-3, S1-4, S1-7, S1-6, S1-9) delivered and verified. Database enforcement reaches 9 / 9 (100%), and end-to-end lifecycle reaches 17 / 17 (100% green, 0 known-red, 0 failed). All 118 migrations build from scratch under PGlite with 0 failures. Live Supabase database was untouched per N-5 boundary.

### Did

- **S1-8 · Law 17 in Database (0113):** Renamed `delivery_type` enum value `'Customer Pickup'` to `'Client Pickup'` (R-33).
- **S1-5 · Product Units Status Engine (0114):** Created `recompute_unit_status(asset_id)` (security definer) computing status precedence: Retired > Missing > Maintenance > On Rent > Returning > Inspection > Cleaning > Packed > Reserved > In Stock. Added write guard `guard_unit_status_direct_write()` raising `gate.unit_status.direct_write` on direct update attempts. Bound triggers across `booking_stage_transitions`, `session_line_movements`, `handover_lines`, `return_lines`, `cleaning_queue_entries`, `maintenance_records`, `cases`, and `inventory_reservations`.
- **S1-1 · Stage Gates in `apply_booking_stage_transition` (0115):** Relocated stage gating logic from app floor verbs into plpgsql. Enforced gates: `gate.pack.session_missing`, `gate.pack.units_unassigned`, `gate.pack.units_unpacked`, `gate.handover.session_missing`, `gate.handover.units_unhanded`, `gate.handover.agreement_unsigned`, `gate.return.session_missing`, `gate.return.units_unaccounted`. Gated cancellations via `gate.cancel.stage_too_late` (M+ required after Packed) and `gate.cancel.reason_missing` (≥10 chars). Added `gate.reopen.role` for Closed → Returned transitions (`auth_is_manager_or_above()`).
- **S1-2 · Close Gate (0116):** Locked Returned → Closed transition behind 5 strict checks: `gate.close.no_invoice` (no active invoices), `gate.close.invoice_unsettled` (outstanding > 0), `gate.close.deposit_unresolved` (deposit unrefunded/unforfeited), `gate.close.open_case` (cases non-terminal), and `gate.close.reservation_live` (unreleased reservations).
- **S1-3 · Invoice Void Discipline & Credit Notes (0117):** Created `credit_notes` table with full RLS. Updated `reject_invoice_edit_after_issue()` (security definer) to enforce `gate.invoice.void_role` (Owner, Admin, Manager, Accounts per R-05 / S1-a), `gate.invoice.void_reason` (≥10 chars, auto-stamping `voided_by` and `voided_at`), `gate.invoice.void_paid` (requires credit note if paid_amount > 0), and `gate.invoice.void_immutable` (voided invoices are frozen).
- **S1-4 · Payment Ceiling & Money Integrity (0118):** Created `booking_estimate_total(booking_id)` plpgsql helper computing sum of booking lines, crew, transport, discounts, and VAT. Added `guard_payments_ceiling_and_client()` trigger enforcing `gate.payment.over_invoice` (overpayment on linked invoice), `gate.payment.over_booking` (advance payment exceeding booking total), and `gate.payment.client_mismatch`.
- **S1-7 · Server-Side Prices for Money-Blind Callers (0119):** Added `booking_lines.rate_overridden boolean`. Implemented `get_model_daily_rate(product_id, bundle_id)` (security definer). Updated `create_booking(jsonb)` to enforce model rate for money-blind callers (logging `price.server_applied` to `audit_events` on client mismatch) and raise `gate.discount.money_blind` on discount attempts. Added `guard_booking_lines_money_blind()` trigger raising `gate.booking_lines.money_blind_insert` on direct line inserts with money outside `create_booking`.
- **S1-6 · Staff Visibility, Role Ceiling, and User Immutability (0120):** Added `users.deactivated_at`. Updated `auth_user_role()` so deactivated users immediately resolve to `'Client'`. Added `auth_user_branch_id()`. Recreated `staff_directory_v` masking PII for non-Owner/Admin roles. Added `enforce_users_role_ceiling()` trigger enforcing `gate.users.role_ceiling` (Admin cannot assign Owner/Admin; Manager cannot alter roles) and self-deactivation protection. Added `reject_users_delete()` trigger enforcing `gate.users.immutable` (Law 3).
- **S1-9 · Verification & Probes:**
  - Expanded `scripts/e2e-lifecycle.mjs` to 17 steps (L1–L17), turning all previous known-red gates (L6, L7, L8, L9, L10, L11) and adding L15 (unit status engine), L16 (void discipline), L17 (server prices, role ceiling, immutability) into fully asserted passing tests.
  - Implemented `--write-probes` flag in `scripts/check-db.mjs`.
  - Updated `docs/PERMISSIONS.md` §6.1 with `id` column, §9 with new database helpers, and §4.6 with S1-a ruling outcome.

## 2026-09-09 — The item picker stops answering "free now" to a question about next month (R-37)

§4.45(a) is closed, and not the way it was framed. The question was *"how do 10 unit statuses
become 4 pools"*; the answer is that they do not, because `product_units.status` is a now-state
and the question is about a window.

### Did

- **`AddBundle` asks the availability engine, for a window.** The picker carries the same
  `?from=`/`?to=` window the Bundles pane and bundle detail page carry (§4.44) and reads
  `queries/productAvailability`, the engine New Rental's picker already uses. Columns are
  **Stock · Free · Held**; the fourth is gone because nothing splits a hold into on-rent versus
  reserved for a window.
- **`productAvailability` grew its quantity half** — `productCapacityFor`, over
  `readQuantityHolds` + `capacityFor`. It previously reported `unitsOwned: 0` for bulk stock,
  which on live means **all 204 products**, because live has zero `product_units` rows. +7 tests.
- **Fixed two compile errors in `EditBundle.tsx`** (`record.isLoading` → `loading`; `title`
  passed to `Page`'s Button, which does not accept it). See *Ruled* — they were committed on
  8 Sep under a false gate claim.

  the bundle detail page showed a C-stand **0 of 4 free** for 11–14 Nov while the picker showed
  **4 available**, because the November hold is an `inventory_reservations` row that never
  touched `status`. Both halves are in `RULINGS-2026-09-09.md` with the before/after and the
  revert.
- Recorded there too: **a now-count answering a windowed question is a defect pattern, not one
  screen's bug.** NR-09 was the first instance, this is the second. Any screen still reporting
  availability without a window is the third.

### Verified

## 2026-09-08 — Reservations move into Postgres, the lifecycle runs in CI, and preventive maintenance exists

Babin's 8 Sep addendum, worked in its own stated order: R-26 (reservations), R-35/"R-27"
(`check:lifecycle`), R-28 (preventive maintenance), plus the two migrations the order of work put
ahead of them. R-29 was implemented by a concurrent session in the same tree and is **not**
duplicated here — see *Conflicts resolved*, row 2.

### Did

- **Step 1 — renumbered `0081` → `0098` (`0098_invoice_totals_match_engine.sql`).** It was written
  after `0085`–`0097` and numbered before them, so filename order applied it in the wrong place.
  Its ordering footer was rewritten for the new position, and every reference — six inside the
  file, seven across `docs/`, `src/` and two sibling migrations — moved with it. Neither number is
  ever reused.
- **Step 2 — `0099_create_booking_discount_audit_class.sql`. `create_booking` could not write a
  discounted booking at all, for TWO independent reasons.** Both reproduced before either was
  fixed, both fixed in this one file. See *Verified*.
- **Step 3 — `0100_reservations_written_by_transition.sql` (R-26).** `inventory_reservations` is
  written by a trigger on `booking_stage_transitions`, not by the browser. Serialised holds from
  `booking_line_units`, a quantity hold for each line's uncovered remainder, released on
  Returned · Closed · a reversal to Quote · cancellation. `security invoker`, `search_path` pinned,
  half-open bounds matching `RENTAL_WINDOW_BOUNDS`. Backfill per booking in its own subtransaction.
- **`confirmRental.ts` stops writing.** `reserveAssignedUnits` / `releaseReservations` and the
  four-branch compensation are gone — they existed only because PostgREST cannot give a browser a
  transaction, and the trigger makes the hold and the stage move one commit. What remains is
  `planAssignment` (a read) and `findCollidingHolds` (a read that names the booking already holding
  the unit, so a refusal reads *"#912 has it"* rather than `23P01`). The writers are **deleted**
  from `lib/queries/availability.ts` rather than left exported and uncalled.
- **Step 4 — `scripts/e2e-lifecycle.mjs` + `npm run check:lifecycle` (R-35).** Thirteen steps,
  one booking's whole life, driven through a real Postgres as real roles under real RLS. Wired into
  `.github/workflows/ci.yml` beside `check:pglite`, which was also not in CI until now. Known-red
  is a first-class outcome: a red step that starts PASSING fails the run.
- **Step 5 — `0103_preventive_maintenance.sql` (R-28)** plus `lib/serviceDue.ts`,
  `lib/queries/serviceDue.ts`, `components/ui/ServiceDueBadge.tsx`,
  `actions/inventory/updateServicePlan.ts`, `ServicePlanCard`, `DueForService`, and the packing
  warning. Due by time **or** usage, whichever first; warns only; the interval on the model.
- `docs/PERMISSIONS.md` §4.1 (two rows restated) and §4.3 (three new capability rows). `CLAUDE.md`
  and `PERMISSIONS.md` §15 both carry the R-29 and R-35 session rules, kept identical per §15.5.
  `PLAN.md` §4.53–§4.56.

### Ruled

`RULINGS-2026-09-08.md` R-26, R-28, R-29 (recorded, built elsewhere), R-35.

- **R-26** — the database writes reservations. One addition to the ruling's text, flagged as one:
  a reversal to **Quote** releases too. R-26's own second sentence requires it ("Quotes hold
  nothing"), and without it a reversed booking **deadlocks** — re-confirming would collide with its
  own reservation and could never succeed again.
- **R-28** — three deviations from the ruling's schema table, each argued in `0103`'s header:
  the meter already exists as `running_hours`; a delta needs a baseline and the ruling names no
  place for one; `Preventive` is spelled `Preventive Service`. And `due_at` carries the TIME due
  date only — the instant usage crossed its threshold is not recoverable without replaying every
  booking per unit on every list read, which is why R-28's own tooltip for the usage case names no
  date.
- **R-35 — a NUMBER COLLISION, resolved and cross-referenced.** Babin issued the lifecycle ruling
  as "R-27". `R-27` in this file was already taken the same day by a concurrent session's
  staff-role ruling. Numbers are not reused, so the lifecycle ruling is filed as **R-35** with the
  collision noted in both places. Neither supersedes the other.

### Verified

- **`create_booking` refused every discounted booking, twice over.** Both reproduced in PGlite over
  the full chain before either was fixed:
  1. `ERROR: invalid input value for enum audit_event_class: "data change"` — a literal that has
     never been one of the six Foundation §10 classes, carried forward verbatim through `0063`,
     `0065`, `0070` and `0071`. The identical payload WITHOUT a discount succeeded (booking 900);
     with one it rolled back the booking, its lines and its units.
  2. With that fixed, the same call still failed **for Coordinator and Warehouse and not for
     Owner**: `INSERT … RETURNING` applies the table's SELECT policy to the row it hands back, and
     `audit_events_select` admits Owner · Admin · Manager only. Isolated by running the same insert
     with and without `RETURNING` — without it, accepted. Fixed by minting the key instead of
     reading it back; **not** by widening the policy (B-1). Found by `check:lifecycle` L1 ten
     minutes after the first fix, which is the argument for that script in one paragraph.
- **The double booking, reproduced.** #900 (unit X, 10–12 Sep) and #901 (same unit, 11–13 Sep) both
  reached Booked with `inventory_reservations` at **0 rows** — the GiST constraint was never
  offered a row to reject. After `0100`: the second confirm is refused, the booking stays a Quote,
  and the reservation count is unchanged.
- **`0100`'s backfill named 19 double bookings that were already in the corpus.** 208 holds written
  across 57 bookings; 19 skipped, every one refused by `0045` with a sentence of the form
  *"product … would have 6 units held at once between 2026-08-02 and 2026-08-06, but stock on hand
  is 4"*. Not a defect in the migration — a defect in the data, invisible until something asked.
- **`npm run check:pglite` — 101/101 applied, 0 failed.** Re-run after every migration.
- **`npm run check:lifecycle` — 9/13 green, 4 known-red, 0 failed.** L9 reports precisely which
  two of four payments the database accepts and must not: an amount larger than the outstanding
  balance, and a payment naming another client's booking.
- **`0103`'s post-conditions execute R-28's own scenario and roll it back:** a model on 90 days /
  40 rental days, a unit serviced today, five bookings of ten rental days each → `due_reason =
  'usage'` at 50 although the calendar has 40 days to run; a completed `Repair` does not reset the
  clock; a completed `Preventive Service` does, and the counter returns to 0. Also proved: the view
  is money-free, is not writable by `authenticated`, and a model with no plan never badges.
- **Both migrations' behavioural probes were proved to RUN**, not skip: the skip branches were
  temporarily turned into exceptions and the chain stayed green, then reverted.
- `vitest run` — **137 files / 2926 tests passed, 0 failed.** `eslint src --max-warnings 0` exit 0.
- `tsc --noEmit` exits 2, and **every error is in `EditBundle.tsx` and `clientFacets.test.ts**,
  both of which `git status` reports clean against HEAD — so the failure is AT HEAD (`0510a14`) and
  is the concurrent session's in-flight work, not this tree's. **Zero errors in any file this
  session touched**, established by filtering the run's own output rather than by assertion:
  `grep -cE '<the 13 paths touched here>' → 0`.

### Applied to production, by the concurrent session, hours after these files were written

Every migration here was written under N-5 — *file only, never run* — and each header says so.
Babin lifted N-5 in writing later the same day ("now apply everything") and the concurrent session
applied `0079`–`0103`, twenty files, to `sxguwvgoserhdolewibb`. **The headers in `0098`, `0099`,
`0100` and `0103` therefore now read as stale, and are: they were true when written.** Their entry
carries the live measurements; the three that belong to this work are

| | Before | After |

| a discounted booking | refused outright (22P02) | created, by a Coordinator |
| double booking | nothing enforced it | **92 live holds backfilled**; an overlapping second booking is refused and stays at Quote |
| views writable by `anon`/`authenticated` | 26 of 26 | 0 |

Two things follow, and both are for whoever reads this next rather than for me:

- **`0100`'s backfill has run on production.** It reported 92 holds on live against 208 here — a
  different corpus, so a different count, and neither figure predicts the other. Whatever it

## 2026-09-08 — A bundle can be modified: the edit screen, the write, and the one act the grants forbid

`createBundle` could mint a bundle and nothing could ever change it again — no route, no
action, no screen. This is the other half. It also closes the last item on the 4 Sep missing
pages register that was mine to close.

### Did

- **`actions/inventory/updateBundle.ts`** — UPDATE_BUNDLE, `implemented: true`. Writes the
  bundle row (name, description, category, both rates, active/archived) and its components
  (quantity, days, mandatory, order), and inserts new components. Every reference — the
  category, each added product, the bundle itself, each edited line — is resolved BEFORE the
  first write, so an unresolvable one refuses with a named sentence and nothing at all is
  written. Line writes after that point are individually confirmed and a failure is reported
  as the partial it is.
- **`modules/inventory/EditBundle.tsx`** at `/inventory/bundles/:bundleRef/edit`, reached from
  an **Edit bundle** button on the detail page that is absent — not disabled — for a role that
  cannot use it. The `?from=`/`?to=` window rides along both ways, so Cancel returns to the
  same availability question the operator left (§4.44).
- **`inventory.update`** — a new capability, `rbac.canUpdateBundle`, Owner · Admin · Manager.
  Derived by the §4.20 method from live RLS (`bundles_manage` ∩ `bundle_items_all`), re-read
  8 Sep rather than copied from `inventory.create`.
- Supporting: `BUNDLE_UPDATED` on the event bus; `categoryId` on `BundleWithItems` (an edit
  writes the uuid, and an untouched category must not be lost re-resolving a display name);
  `useBundleWithItems` — the columns, not the display record, with `includeArchived` so an
  archived bundle can be reopened to restore it.
- **21 new tests** in `inventoryWrites.test.ts`, and the shared db mock's filtered select is
  now awaitable as well as `maybeSingle`-able. Without that, a multi-row read resolved to the
  builder object, `{ data, error }` destructured as undefined, and a populated table read as
  empty — a false green, because "no rows" is a legal answer.

### Ruled

- **R-34 — a bundle is editable; a saved component is not removable, and no control pretends
  otherwise.** `authenticated` holds INSERT and UPDATE on `bundles` and `bundle_items` and
  **no DELETE** on either; `bundle_items` has no archive column; `bundle_items_qty_positive`
  refuses zero. Three rules, each closing one of the three ways a component could be retired.
  Repairing it is Babin's: granting DELETE is §15.2 **N-4**, adding the column is **N-5**.
  Filed as **PLAN.md §4.52** with three options and a recommendation (the `client_flags`
  `removed_at`/`removed_by` pattern). The screen says so in plain words where the components
  are listed. Shipping the button instead would have been worse than it sounds: a delete
  matching zero rows returns **no error**, so the screen would report the component gone and
  the next load would show it still there.
- Two smaller decisions inside R-34: the capability is named for the act, and the component
  picker draws **no availability** — which is what keeps this screen clear of the still-open
  §4.45(a). That ruling is about the four count columns and how ten `product_units.status`
  members collapse into them; this picker renders none of them, so it cannot tell an operator
  gear is free and cannot tell them wrong.

### Verified

- **Driven in the browser, mock corpus, signed in as Owner.** `BND-001` in the 11-14 Nov
  window: renamed to *Documentary Camera Kit (Rev B)* and NISI Athena raised 2 → 3; toast read
  *"BND-001 · 1 field · 1 changed"*; the detail page came back with the new name, **Needs 3**
  on that line, **5 / 6 Ready** recomputed from 4 / 5, and the money card flipping from *"At
  or above sum of parts"* to *"Saves 3% on parts"* because the parts sum moved. Then added
  **DJI Ronin 4D-6K** (EQ000247) through the catalogue search: detail page now reads
  **4 components · 6 / 7 Ready**, the new line at 1/1, Rs 7,000.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0. `inventoryWrites.test.ts` 96/96, `rbac.test.ts` 49/49,
  `core.test.ts` 70/70.
- The **3/5 → 4/5 discrepancy** flagged in the previous entry is resolved and was not a build
  difference: the dev server now reports the same 4 / 5 as the production bundle for the same
  bundle and window. The corpus moved under both, not the code.

  `information_schema.role_table_grants`; no migration was written and none was applied.

  exists.

### Ruled

- **R-27 — the Owner, and only the Owner, assigns a staff role.** Four sources said Owner
  (`canManageSettings`, `staff_directory_v`'s inline predicate, §11.2, §12.2 D-8's own Owner
  clause) and one said Admin (D-8's *"As Admin … grant Manager → succeeds"*). **Stricter wins
  (B-1)**: D-8 was corrected, not the code widened. An Admin gets zero rows from the directory to
  act on, and §16 V-3/V-4 already caught the same document over-crediting Admin twice.
  Revert: widen the `auth_user_role() <> 'Owner'` line in `0101`.
- **RPCs, not an `UPDATE` policy on `users`.** `authenticated` already holds `UPDATE` on
  `users.primary_role` at the grant level, so a policy would have made `email`, `branch_id` and
  `employee_code` writable by the same `PATCH`; and *"at least one active Owner must remain"* is a
  statement about a set, which a `with check` cannot see. Least code, narrowest surface,
  reversible (§15.3).
- **Account creation stays unbuilt, and it is not a ruling gap.** Minting an `auth.users` identity
  needs the admin API and therefore the service key — a complete authorization bypass in a
  browser. It needs an Edge Function. `0101` opens no INSERT path so nothing can half-create a
  person.

every cursor forward. Probe wrapped in `ROLLBACK_0097_PROBE` — the sentinel 0094/0095 use and 0092
omitted, which is why 0092's probe committed a real write to a production product row.

no `C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL`), so `db:apply` and `check:rebuild` cannot run. This file has never
been executed by anything. Do not treat it as working. It is also NOT applied to live, per CLAUDE.md.

⚠ **PLAN.md §4.43(d).1's table list is wrong in both directions.** It names `booking_discounts` (not in

### Item 3 — redesigned, half-built: `src/lib/deterministicId.ts` — ✅ VERIFIED at unit level

§4.43(d).3 prescribes deriving `operation_sessions.id` from `(booking_id, operation, operational_day)`.
**Checked against the schema, and it is wrong three times over:**

1. `operation_sessions_one_packing_per_booking` (`0003:152`) is `unique (booking_id) where operation =
   'Packing'` — one Packing session per booking *ever*. A day-keyed id mints a different uuid for a
   second-day pack the index forbids anyway, so the losing device's children again reference a session
   that cannot exist. It reintroduces the exact bug it was written to remove.
2. `session_no` distinguishes the morning collection (1) from the evening one (2) — same operational
   day. A day-keyed id merges two legitimately distinct Handover/Return sessions.
3. `operational_day` is computed from `operationalDayStart`, which `settingsStore.ts` persists to
   **localStorage, per browser** (`system_settings` is empty and has no writer). Two tablets configured
   differently place one instant on different days and mint different ids — the non-determinism the
   change exists to end.

Built instead on `(booking_id, operation, session_no)`, which already carries
`operation_sessions_session_no_unique` (`0003:85`), needs no new column and reads no setting.
SHA-256 → RFC 9562 version 8 (honest label: v5 is SHA-1). Refuses to fall back to a random id when
Web Crypto is absent — a silent fallback would reintroduce the defect on the devices least able to
report it. Residual weakness stated in the header: a device with a stale view computes a colliding
`session_no`, which trips an existing unique constraint instead of silently detaching a shift.

**Gates:** `vitest src/lib/__tests__/deterministicId.test.ts` **13/13 pass** · `tsc --noEmit` **exit 0,
whole project** · `eslint` **exit 0**. (First tsc run reported two `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` errors in
this file; fixed with a checked `byteAt()` rather than a `!` assertion, then re-run clean.)

## 2026-09-07 (cont.) — Return and Reset: the last two stages, and a booking that could not receive its own item

**Phase:** Phase 0 · **Status:** 6 items closed + 2 stale entries closed · 2 filed · lifecycle sweep complete

RT-03, RT-06, RT-08, RS-09, RS-10, RS-12. Two reviews returned **ship**, the third **fix-first**;
everything they found is fixed below.

### RT-03 — the trap

A return line was terminal on its **state** alone, so a line declared Not Returned with the
decision **"Still expected"** — which means the item is coming back — counted as finished. The
booking advanced to Returned, `actual_return_at` was stamped on gear still with the client, and
every later Return was refused. The item could never be received.

The grounding is the part worth keeping. The engine's own comment claimed all three terminal lists
came "straight out of `0003`'s close gates". **Only Pack's does** — `:340` and `:399` are *stage*
conditions, and `0003:172` says so verbatim. That false comment is corrected in the code, and it is
why the defect looked principled.

**Positive control run in both directions**: restoring the state-only rule fails 3 tests; flipping
`'Still expected'` back to `true` fails 3. And the fix deliberately does not create a new trap —
the booking stays On Rent, the workspace still opens, and there are two exits: receive the item, or
re-declare it with a decision that ends the line.

### What the reviews caught

- **The recovery path left a row contradicting itself.** `not_returned_reason` and
  `not_returned_decision` were written on the missing path and never cleared on its twin, so a
  line that finally arrived read `state: 'Returned'` while still carrying "Still expected".
  `0003:378` only *requires* the pair when the state is Not Returned — it never forbids it — so the
  database accepts the contradiction silently. Clearing is the writer's job and is now explicit.
- **A green tick beside its own contradiction, again.** The Return pill read "Complete" in success
  green for a session whose every line was "Still expected". This is the *second* screen with that
  defect, so rather than write a third copy the rule moved to `lib/status.ts` as `jobStateChip`,
  with the exception word as a parameter; Packing's `packJobChip` now delegates to it.
- **A disclosure was lost while the counts were being fixed.** The Maintenance footer went from
  "Showing 3 of 3 **seeded** jobs" to "…3 jobs" — the only place that screen admits the list is
  fabricated, on a page whose CSV Export is live. Restored, and the assertions now pin the
  disclosure rather than just the arithmetic.
- Plus a header that overpromised ("the two can never drift apart" — false for a mixed booking), a
  copy branch that called an undecided row "ended", a third un-swept copy site, a citation off by
  two lines, and a comment that outlived the input it described.

### The question the fix answered without being asked

Filed as **RT-09**, and it is a real trade-off: holding the booking at On Rent also holds every
unit that *did* come back. Their `cleaning_queue_entries` rows are written, but Reset runs at stage
`Returned`, so with 9 of 10 lines received **all 9 sit in the cleaning queue, out of stock**, until
the tenth arrives. "Still expected" is the everyday case — the client is bringing it tomorrow — so
this trades one late item against a booking's whole returned inventory. `0003:399` rules the stage
and says nothing about cleaning. Marked `TODO(decision)` at the engine site rather than decided.

### Register corrections

- **RS-10 was stale** — already fixed at HEAD (reads `useParams`, filters, banner, route present).
  Fourth stale entry this session, after NR-07, BD-20 and CL-05.
- **RS-09's framing was wrong.** No INSERT is attempted on either path: both modals emit an event
  and call `onSuccess`, and both handlers only append to local state, with the action
  `implemented: false`. So Law 8's duplicate rejection is not failing — it is *unreachable*, and the
  "row written twice" was two appends to a list in memory. The counts half was real and is fixed.
  Its `useMemo` bullet was also stale.
- **PK-22 closed by RT-06** — same dead control, filed by the packing batch, fixed here.
- **RT-10 filed**: Packing still ships the duplicate Scan Barcode / Scan QR pair, and neither
  button can select a real mode because the modal's `scanType` only styles the control.

### Verified

tsc clean in scope; eslint clean; the affected suites pass — **24 files / 532 tests**, including
the maintenance suite once its assertions followed the restored disclosure.

**Not driven.** No browser probe: RT-06's disabled control and RT-08's single button rest on code,
types and tests. Live cannot exercise either path anyway — production has nothing past Packed.

## 2026-09-07 (cont. 3) — The three close gates stop passing on the wrong question

**Phase:** Phase 0 → Phase 2 · **Status:** MONEY-13, RL-05, RL-06 fixed app-side · `PLAN.md §4.51` filed · the database half is still absent

Three of the audit's issues are one shape: **a gate that passes because its predicate is vacuous
or measures the wrong column**, so a rental closes with money owed, a deposit still held, or
damage uncharged.

- **MONEY-13** — `Σ outstanding = 0` over **zero invoices** means *never billed*, not *settled*.
  R-01 makes invoicing manual, so a rental could be handed over, returned and closed with nothing
  ever invoiced. The gate now requires an invoice whose status is neither Draft nor Void. A
  Draft's balance still counts toward outstanding — a working figure someone must settle or void
  is not nothing — but a Draft cannot stand in for a bill having been raised.
- **RL-05** — the deposit gate read `security_deposits.pending_amount`, which
  `sync_deposit_balances` derives as `greatest(required − received, 0)`: that is **"not yet
  collected"**, not "not yet given back". It now computes `held = received − refunded − applied`.
  `pending_amount` is gone from the file.
- **RL-06** — the damage gate was the literal `0` with a TODO, while findings are now genuinely
  written at Return and Reset. It reads them parent-first, never through an embed:
  `operation_sessions` → `return_lines` → `damage_findings`, and `cleaning_queue_entries` →
  `damage_findings`, both filtered to pending approval and not voided. Every read throws with its
  table named, so a broken read can never read as "gate passes".

`CloseGateInput` renames `depositResolved: boolean` to `depositHeldPaisa: number` deliberately:
the rename forces every call site to face the changed meaning rather than keeping a field whose
name **was** the bug. Blocking values are rupees now, not raw paisa.

### It found a fault in the seed corpus, not just in the gate

Sixteen `Closed` demo bookings received their deposits and emitted no `Released` movement, so
under the corrected predicate they hold the client's money. Rather than feed the gate a number the
SQL would not produce, the corpus now emits the matching `'Released'` `deposit_movements` row so
`sync_deposit_balances` actually sets `refunded_amount`. That row has **never executed** —
`db:rebuild` cannot run — so its column list was copied verbatim from the adjacent working
`Received` block and checked against the live constraints.

### Which gate lives where — read live, not from migration headers

| Gate | Engine (app) | Trigger `validate_booking_gates` |
|---|---|---|
| Invoiced | **fixed** | **absent** |
| Outstanding = 0 | fixed (rupee message) | present, but the vacuous sum, and names no amount |
| Deposit resolved | **fixed** (held, not pending) | present, but reads `pending_amount` |
| No open Case | present (always app-only) | **absent** |
| No damage pending | **fixed** | **absent** |

So this fixes **one of the two layers**. `0084_close_gates_complete` is not written, live stops at
`0078`, and with the stage column still directly writable (DB-02/SEC-06) and the `_v` views still
writable (SEC-01) every gate remains bypassable by a direct write, a script or an offline replay.

### The dependency this creates — recorded because an operator should not discover it

Gates 2 and 4 now convert a silent loss into a **hard block with no exit path in the app**.
Verified by grep with a positive control: nothing in `src/actions` or `src/lib/queries` writes a
`Released` or `Applied` `deposit_movements` row, and nothing sets
`damage_findings.approval_state = 'Approved'` — `floorVerb` only inserts.

Latent today (0 deposits, 0 findings live), but the first real deposit or Return finding strands
that booking at `Returned` until MONEY-10 and a damage-approval writer exist. That is the correct
failure direction — blocking beats losing the client's money quietly — but it is a dependency, so
**both refusal strings now say so in as many words** and each carries a `TODO` naming the issue
that should delete the clause. A message telling an operator to "refund or apply it" when no
screen records either is the same dishonesty the floor verbs were just cleared of.

### §4.51 filed, and the override deliberately not built

R-07 keeps the close gate a hard block and names no exception; R-06's named override belongs to
the **handover** gate and explicitly only there; R-08 rules who may confirm a close, not what they
may waive. So no override was implemented — reading R-06 across to Close would extend a ruling.
`PLAN.md §4.51` puts the zero-value-job question to Babin with both answers costed.

On `SPEC-P0-2 §1` versus the audit: §1 lists *"enforces deposit resolved —
`security_deposits.pending_amount`"* under **"Already live"**, and that line is precisely the
misreading. Foundation §1.7 gate 2, carried by R-00, is *"refunded, forfeited, or applied"* — what
is **held**, not what is uncollected. R-00 makes the newer ruling win over a spec's description of
existing behaviour, so the audit is followed.

### Verified

`npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0. `npx eslint` on all five files exit 0. `npx vitest run` on the
closeRental and workflow suites — **74 passed**, re-run after the refusal strings changed (the
first re-run failed on one pinned message, which is the test doing its job; the assertion was
updated to the new text).

**Not verified:** nothing here was exercised against production and nothing could be — 0 invoices,
0 deposits, 0 findings, 0 sessions, and 200 of 246 bookings carry no `booking_lines` (DATA-17).
The corrected reads have never met a real PostgREST; their `.in()` and `.is()` shapes are asserted
against a mock. No refusal string has been seen rendered.

## 2026-09-07 — Handover and Evidence: a screen that steered toward a false certification

**Phase:** Phase 0 · **Status:** 4 register items closed · 4 filed · 1 new defect CLASS found

HO-09, HO-10, HO-12, HO-14. The run that produced them was **stopped mid-flight** — both builders
finished and their edits were on disk, but only one of three review lenses had reported. The other
two were run separately against the same diff, and between them they found more than the batch did.

### What was fixed

- **HO-09** — the Evidence header rendered `{ l: 'Status', v: 'Booked' }` as a **literal** and its
  dates as `new Date('2026-07-16')`, on *every* booking. It now reads the real booking through
  `fetchFloorBooking`. The photographs stay seeded and cannot be otherwise — live
  `storage.buckets` is empty and nothing writes `evidence_files` — so the screen says which half is
  which rather than letting a real booking number sit silently above sample photographs.
- **HO-10** — seven bulk actions rendered enabled from an array with no handler. The retention
  promise was neither deleted nor faked: Law 3's behaviour is still stated, marked unbuilt.
- **HO-12** — "Bulk Scan" scanned nothing (PK-07's fix ported rather than re-invented); Cancel
  Handover discarded marks, reasons and **both signatures** on one tap.
- **HO-14** — `Sig.at` stored *display text* (no date, no timezone, uncomparable) and is now an
  instant; the page's third copy of the rental-day rule is routed through `lib/rentalDays.ts`.

### What the two late reviews caught — the important half

**The screen steered a floor operator toward a false money certification.** The R-06 block invited
a reason for handing over with money outstanding, while gates 3 and 4 (`paymentVerified`,
`depositReceived`) keep `canComplete` false whenever money is owed. So the reason could never be
dispatched, and the only way through was to tick **"Deposit Received"** — certifying the very fact
the reason exists to explain. R-06 rules that this gate *warns*; neither the page nor the live
database does that. The copy now says so in the imperative, and the behaviour is filed as HO-17.

**A new defect CLASS, filed as X-11: UI copy that describes a migration the live database does not
have.** The Handover block said "the database refuses the move to On Rent unless a reason is given
here" — that is `0090`, and it is not applied. Verified against production: `validate_booking_gates()`
exists, its body mentions `outstanding` and never `override`, i.e. still the old hard block. So an
operator who writes a reason is refused anyway, by a gate that never reads it, having just been told
the reason is what lets them through. **My first fix of this was itself incomplete** — a second
instance survived it in the very next element, and the review caught that too.

**A regression the fix introduced.** Making the hide-note optional reopened a hole the mandatory
version could not reach: `live = PHOTOS.filter(p => !hidden[p.id])` tests the note's *truthiness*,
so a blank note stored `''` and the rail announced a file hidden while the card stayed in the grid
and in every count. Now tests presence, pinned by a test with a **positive control** — restoring the
old predicate fails it.

**Two more, both incomplete in the same direction as their fix:** the cross-booking guard compared
`floor?.id`, which only updates once the *next* booking's read resolves — so it did not cover the
window it was written for; it now also compares the route param, which changes synchronously. And
the discard dialog asserted "Nothing on this screen has been written yet" while a dispatch could be
in flight, so an operator could walk away believing a handover was not recorded while it committed.

### Filed

**HO-17** (R-06's ruled override is unreachable, and *who may author it* is unruled — R-06 names no
authority set where R-05 and R-08 do), **HO-18** (`Mark.via` is written by three call sites and read
by nothing — the PK-07 breakdown it was ported for did not come with it, so it is dead state dressed
as provenance), **HO-19** (`BookingNotLoaded` is now importerless, while five comments still call it
a live pattern), and **X-11** for the class above.

### Verified

tsc clean; eslint clean; the batch's four suites pass (56 tests, then 28 after the fixes, plus the
new gallery case with its positive control).

**Not driven, and worth saying plainly:** the mock app would not boot. The other session's
uncommitted `seed.ts` work makes the corpus refuse to emit (*"B-902: close gate… more has been
refunded or applied than was ever received"*). That message does not exist at HEAD and the
invariant is added in their working diff, so it is their in-flight state, not this batch's — but it
means nobody can run the app right now, and these four fixes rest on tests and code reading rather
than on a browser.

## 2026-09-07 (cont. 2) — An invoice can exist: one transaction writes it, and the modal shows what it will write

**Phase:** Phase 0 · **Status:** DB-03 (P0), DATA-01 (P1), MONEY-01 (P0), MONEY-05 (P1) implemented · `PLAN.md §4.46` derived and closed · `check:rebuild` still BLOCKED

Four of the audit's issues were one path: nothing could raise an invoice, and the three things
blocking it were independent. The policy refused the write, the column grants refused the read,
and the screen refused to dispatch because it disagreed with the action about what an invoice is.

### The write contract — `0086` extended, `0096` written

`0086` (unapplied draft) is corrected against R-05 and R-15: `invoice_no` and `issue_date`
nullable with a CHECK that they move together, the write policies realigned from
Owner/Admin/Manager/**Coordinator** to R-05's Owner/Admin/Manager/**Accounts**, and
`invoice_lines` given INSERT and UPDATE policies at all — on live it has exactly one policy,
`invoice_lines_select`, so every line write is refused for every role.

`0096_create_invoice_rpc.sql` adds `create_invoice(jsonb)`: one function, one transaction, in the
shape `create_booking` already established. The old action wrote the header and then looped one
line insert per booking line, and PostgREST gives a browser no transaction — so a failure between
the header and the last line left a header with some of its lines, under-billing the job. Its own
error text told the operator to **void it rather than retry**, which is an admission that the
shape cannot be made safe from the client. Both close gates read `outstanding_amount`, so a header
with no lines reads as fully paid and the rental closes unbilled.

**Why `SECURITY DEFINER` and not `INVOKER`, measured rather than assumed.** `create_booking` is
INVOKER and that is the better default. This function cannot be: 0062 revoked table-level SELECT
on `booking_lines` and `booking_transport` and granted back only the non-money columns, so
`has_column_privilege('authenticated','booking_lines','rate','SELECT')` is **false for every
signed-in session, Owner included** — probed on the live project. An INVOKER function would read
NULL money and silently bill zero. The role check moves inside the function instead, in the same
transaction as the write.

### The screen — `PLAN.md §4.46` derived, not decided

The modal was a free-form editor of hand-typed `{description, amount}` rows followed by a refusal
that dispatched nothing, and the refusal was **correct**: `createInvoice` derives its lines from
the booking, so calling it from that form would have discarded every row the operator typed and
billed something else.

§4.46 is now closed as **derived**, because three binding documents already answer it: R-03
(*"append as lines to the Draft invoice, one invoice per rental"* — damage and late fees have
nothing to append to on a hand-typed bill), SPEC-P0-1 §3.1 (*"one `invoice_lines` row per
`booking_lines` row"*, and *"lines are a snapshot, not a join"*), and R-02 (Draft for the whole
rental, issued once at return). Marked overrule-by-ruling, with the quoted sources in the headers
of `lib/queries/invoicePreview.ts` and the modal.

So the modal is now a read-only **preview** of exactly what `create_invoice` will write — the
booking's own equipment, crew and transport lines, priced by `lib/money.ts`, never by the
component — and Confirm dispatches the action. It reads the `_v` views for the same grant reason
as the function. The mock corpus gained `booking_crew_lines_v` and `booking_transport_v` entries,
because without them the preview showed a bill with no crew while the invoice would have carried
it — the exact preview-versus-write divergence the preview exists to prevent.

**MONEY-05**: `RecordPaymentModal` resolved an invoice by number, and R-15 gives a Draft no
number, so the advance SPEC-P0-1 §5 expects could not be recorded at all. Finance, Payments and
Booking Detail now hand it `{ id, invoiceNo }`, it dispatches `invoiceId`, and an unnumbered
invoice shows as **"Draft (no number)"**. Booking Detail also becomes an invoice entry point under
R-01, which is a screen-level choice and not part of §4.46.

### Verified

`npx eslint` across all sixteen touched files — exit 0. `npx vitest run` over the finance and
invoice suites — **289 passed in 13 files**, exit 0, re-run independently after the work landed.

**Not verified, and it matters here more than usual:** `0086` and `0096` have **never been
applied or rebuilt**. `check:rebuild` cannot run — Docker Desktop's privileged service is stopped,
so every `docker` command hangs and the database's port accepts connections while nothing answers.
Both migrations are written so their own post-conditions will prove them when that gate returns;
until then the SQL is unproven, and `0096` cannot be applied before `0086` in any case. Nothing in
this entry has reached the live project, where the ledger still stops at `0078`.

## 2026-09-07 — BN-P1: the bundle detail page exists
**Phase:** inventory · **Status:** built, tested, driven

`/inventory/bundles/:bundleRef`. The 4 Sep audit filed this P1 as missing entirely, and it was
the odd one out in that list: `data/bundleIntel.ts:97 bundleDetailGroups` had already been
written to describe a bundle in full — Identity, Availability, Components, Substitutes,
Current booking, Money, each already gated — and **nothing rendered it**. Two controls said so
in the same words: a row-menu item and a disabled "View full breakdown" button, both carrying
*"Bundle detail has no screen yet."*

### What it is, given no spec exists
There is no spec and no approved render for this screen — the library has `Bundles.md` (list)
and `Add Bundle.md` (create) and nothing else. So the LAYOUT follows `ClientDetail.tsx`
(`PageHeader` → `KpiStrip` → `Card`s → `FooterNote`) and the CONTENT is `bundleDetailGroups`,
which is not invention: it is the field set the intel layer already settled, cited to
`Bundles.md` §4/§7/§8/§10 in its own comments. Rendering it also means the hover card and the
page cannot disagree. `IntelCard`'s own `DetailGroups` is module-local and unexported, hence a
small renderer in the page rather than an import.

### The window is the reason this is not just a table
**§4.44.** A bundle is not available in the abstract. `useRentalWindowParams` (new,
`lib/rentalWindowParams.ts`) was extracted from `Bundles.tsx` because the half-open guard —
*"from === to holds nothing and every line would read as free"* — is a correctness rule, and
two copies of it drift. Both screens now read the same `?from=`/`?to=`, and every link between
them carries the window, so the list and the page cannot answer different questions about the
same bundle.

### Also wired
- Row menu and "View full breakdown" — the two stubs, both now real links carrying the window.
- `bundleGlance` gains the `primaryAction` its own comment said it could not have while the
  route did not exist; every bundle hover card is now a door. No window on that one, and the
  comment says why: a glance has no access to the caller's dates.
- **`AddBundle` landed on `/inventory` after a successful create — the EQUIPMENT tab**, where a
  new bundle cannot appear even in principle. Now lands on the bundle's own page, using the
  same `result.bundleCode` the success toast quotes.
- `queries/bundles.ts` gained `bundleRef`, dispatching `UUID_RE.test(ref) ? 'id' : 'bundle_code'`
  — the ruled pattern from `getClientRecord`. Nothing produces a bundle uuid today
  (`bundleRecords.ts` maps `id: b.bundleCode` and drops it), so this closes the 4 Sep P0 class
  before it can open. `getBundleRecord` narrows in SQL rather than filtering a full list.

### How it was verified — driven, not read
Mock build, Owner:
- `/inventory/bundles/BND-001` renders **Documentary Camera Kit**, `PARTIALLY AVAILABLE`, KPIs
  `3 / 5 Ready · 3 components · 2 blocked · Rs 18,000`, the donut, the components table and
  all six intel groups.
- **Round trip with a November window**: list shows BND-001 at `3/5`; "View full breakdown"
  href is `/inventory/bundles/BND-001?from=2026-11-11&to=2026-11-14`; the page shows `3/5` for

- `/inventory/bundles/BND-999` → "Bundle not found", the sibling wording and shape.

Two short lines both read *"Short — reason not recorded"*. Only one deserved it. **FX6 needs 2
and only 1 is owned** — that reason IS recorded, and no amount of waiting frees it; the cell now
