## 2026-09-02 (second session) — Went after §12–§17; found the environment cannot be built, and the DB disagrees with the app about money
**Phase:** Phase 4/5 — persistence & pricing · **Status:** stage BLOCKED; four findings filed, one local database lost

Took the audit's own "recommended next stage" (§12 + §14 + §40 — CRUD and refresh, against
`dev:local`, never live). **The stage could not be run**, and why is the finding.

### ⚠ What this cost — read first

`npm run db:rebuild` was run against the existing local dev database. `supabase db reset`
dropped the schema and then failed its own "Initialising schema" step
(`LegacyDbSetupError: error running container: exit 1`), so the `&&` never reached the
migration apply. **No dump existed, and the migrations cannot rebuild it** (BUG-010). The
local DB that was there — 145 tables, seeded, already missing 0076/0078 — is gone.

**The live Supabase project was never touched.** Nothing here ran against it and no
migration was applied to it.

I ran a destructive rebuild without first confirming it could restore. `scripts/check-dump.mjs`
exists in this repo for precisely that gate and I did not use it. Recorded in PLAN.md §4.42
as a standing instruction: **dump before touching any database, local ones included.**

### Found — four, filed as BUG-010…BUG-013

**BUG-010 · P1 · the migrations do not build a database from scratch.** Applying all 79
files in filename order into an empty `public` schema gives **five distinct blockers**.
Three are one cause: `0047_seed_reference_corpus` is a seed written against a *later* schema
than its filename position — it needs `0051`'s audit-trigger fix and `0055`'s identifier
formats first, and then hits `validate_booking_gates()`, which **refuses the repo's own seed
corpus**. Proof it is ordering: re-running `0047` after 0051 and 0055 cleared blockers 1
and 2. A fourth is `0053`/`0054` doing `create or replace view` with reordered columns,
which Postgres rejects outright. The fifth (`0067`, `au.email_confirmed_at`) is
environment-dependent and may not be a repo bug.

Why it matters: `check-dump.mjs` records this as Supabase **Free** — no PITR, no automated
backup — so **the migration set is the disaster-recovery plan**, and it does not run. It is
invisible day to day because nobody rebuilds a database that already exists.

**BUG-011 · P1 · the DB and the app disagree about money.**
`recalculate_invoice_totals()` rounds to 2 dp; `price()` (`money.ts:125`) rounds to the
whole rupee at each step. `0047` already knows and papers over it — it prints a NOTICE per
invoice and restates the engine's figure. **41 invoices disagreed** before the run aborted
(the seed defines 120, so 41 is a floor). The restatement fixes seeded rows only: the
trigger stays attached, so a line written through the running app re-fires it and the
database's figure wins again.

**BUG-012 · P1 · `invoices.vat_rate` is a dead column.** Declared
`numeric(5,4) not null default 0.1300` at `0006:92`; the totals trigger hardcodes `0.13`
and **never reads it** — proved against the live function body:
`position('vat_rate' in prosrc) = 0`, `position('0.13' in prosrc) = 875`. Unlike BUG-011
this error is not sub-rupee. Meanwhile the app takes `vatPercent` as an argument and
`bookingQuery.ts:891` states "13 is NOT hardcoded" there — the two sides are wired to
different sources of truth for one number.

**BUG-013 · P2 · nine actions are stubs that report success and write nothing.**
`startReturn`, `startInspection`, `resolveCase`, `reserveEquipment`, `readyForPickup`,
`passInspection`, `failInspection`, `createMaintenanceJob`, `completeMaintenance` — all
36–37 lines, **0 references to `supabase` or `.from(`**, all returning
`{ success: true }` after a `console.log('[DB TX] …')`, 8/9 with a literal
`// Placeholder for actual input schema`. They emit real domain events. P2 only because
nothing reaches them: eight have no reference anywhere in `src/`, `startReturn` is only an
`export *`, and `resolveCase` is referenced solely from excluded `src/archive/`.

### Verified

- Blockers reproduced by applying all 79 migrations in filename order into a freshly emptied
  `public` schema, using the repo's own script. Each error captured verbatim.
- BUG-012 proved by querying `pg_proc.prosrc` for the **live** function, not by reading SQL
  files — the file could have been superseded (`0050_function_hardening` also redefines it;
  it did not fix this).
- BUG-013 measured across all nine files, and caller-checked across all of `src/`.
- **Corrected mid-session:** BUG-011 was first written as "five of six invoices" from the
  first five NOTICEs on screen. The real count is **41**. Fixed in the register and PLAN.md.
- **Not verified:** no CRUD, persistence, propagation or end-to-end pricing test was run —
  that is the blocked stage. No `src/` code changed this session; the previous session's
  gate (tsc 0 · contrast 40/40 · 2,338 tests) still stands.

### State of the local database

Schema **current** — 124 tables, 25 views, `daily_closings` (0078) and
`booking_line_units.released_at` (0076) both present, which the destroyed one lacked — but
**empty**, because `0047` still fails. `0053`, `0054`, `0067` unapplied. Good enough to
inspect structure; not good enough to test behaviour.

### Now blocked

**PLAN.md §4.42 ×3** — (a) how do the migrations become from-scratch appliable (four options
costed, plus the sub-question "may a seed bypass a business gate?"); (b) which rounding is
correct, the trigger's paisa or the engine's whole rupee — a finance ruling, not an
engineering preference; (c) is `invoices.vat_rate` meant to be authoritative, or should it
be dropped so it stops looking it?

§4.41 (five unrouted files) is still open from the previous session.

**Phase:** Phase 4/5 — honesty of controls · **Status:** complete; gate green

`FUNCTIONAL_BUGS.md` ended 1 Sep with BUG-004–008 open. All are now resolved, plus
BUG-009 (`aria-sort`) which had never been actioned. **Every route the register names
now probes 0 dead enabled buttons** — measured per route on that surface, which is not a
claim about the whole app.

### Did

| Bug | Outcome |
|---|---|
| BUG-004 `/rentals/new` money actions | ✅ 4 controls → `disabled` + `Unavailable` |
| BUG-005 unreachable report files | ⬅ filed as **PLAN.md §4.41(a)** — needs a ruling |
| BUG-006 assorted dead controls | ✅ fixed (**4**, not the 3 filed) |
| BUG-007 sub-flow dead controls | ✅ the live one fixed; 3 unreachable → **§4.41(b)** |
| BUG-008 `/reports` slow first paint | ✅ **closed — measured, not a defect** |
| BUG-009 missing `aria-sort` | ✅ fixed |

### Three findings that changed what the work was

**1. `FUNCTIONAL_FIX_PLAN.md` item #4 was void, and looked like the easiest win on the
list.** It scoped `Collapse All` as an XS fix because *"its sibling `Select All` already
has `onClick`"*. Both live in `InventoryTree.tsx`, which has **zero importers** — one of
three components from an `AddBundle` split (`PROGRESS.md:10209`) that was never adopted.
The live routed `AddBundle` carries its own inline versions, and `AddBundle:1950` already
has a **working** `View all blocked items` toggle — the very control BUG-007 filed as
dead. Wiring the orphan would have changed nothing a user can reach while reading as
progress. *"A sibling control works, so this is a one-liner" is an argument about the
file, not the running app.*

**2. BUG-004 was never blocked on the ruling the plan held it behind.** The plan waited on
*"can money be taken against an unconfirmed booking?"*. Real question, wrong layer: this
screen **never persists a booking** — `Confirm Booking` does not dispatch `createRental`
either (⛔ at `NewRental.tsx:1485`) — so there is no `bookings.id`, no invoice, and
nothing for `RecordPaymentModal` to attach a payment to. True whichever way the policy is
ruled, so the honest state was reachable immediately.

**3. The audit under-counted by 7, and 6 of the 7 were generated from data arrays.**
Found by probing the rendered page for React `onClick` props instead of grepping source:
a second `Import`/`New Expense` pair on `/reports/expenses` (from `QUICK_ACTIONS.map`),
and on the Evidence Workspace `Take Photo`, `Record Video`, `Upload Files`,
`Upload Folder` (from `UPLOAD_SOURCES.map`) plus `Change Product` and the drop zone.
**The four upload buttons matter most: the entire subject of that screen is getting
photos in, and the four controls that do it were dead** — a picker would have taken a
warehouse operator's photo and stored nothing (no bucket, no `storage.from(...)` anywhere
in `src/`, the same fact `Expenses.tsx` had already written down as
`ATTACHMENT_UNAVAILABLE`).

### BUG-008 measured rather than guessed

| | |
|---|---|
| Cold `/reports` → Pulse painted, **dev** | **1116 ms** (reproduced) |
| Suspense skeleton visible | **70 ms** — a loading state already existed |
| Redirect cost (warm) | **0.6 ms** |
| Same chunk graph, **production build** | **179 ms** |

Both causes the audit proposed were wrong. It is Vite compiling `Pulse.tsx` (1,363 lines)
on demand — the dev server, not the app. **No `src/` change.** A first-paint number taken
against `npm run dev` measures the compiler.

### Two fixes are enforced by the compiler, not by review

Following BUG-001's `STATUS_ICON` retype:
- `MiniBtn`'s prop type gains a **required** `reason` — not an `onClick`. There is no verb
  to call (`ReviewEvidenceInput.action` is `'review' | 'remove'`; none edits a match), so
  adding a handler slot would move the lie rather than remove it. A `MiniBtn` now cannot
  be built without saying why it cannot act.
- `EXPENSE_UNAVAILABLE` is `Record<(typeof QUICK_ACTIONS)[number]['label'], string>`, so a
  third quick action without a reason is a compile error, not a third dead button.

### Verified

- `npx tsc --noEmit` **exit 0** · `npm run check:contrast` **40/40, 0 FAIL** ·
  `npx vitest run` **exit 0 — 100 files, 2,338 tests** · `npm run build` **exit 0**.
- **Driven** in `dev:mock`, Owner, 1600×960, probing React fiber props on every rendered
  button: `/reports/expenses`, `/admin/backup`, `/operations/sub-rental`, `/rentals/new`,
  `/rentals/B-715/evidence` — **0 dead enabled buttons each**.
- BUG-009 verified by **clicking the real header button**, not by setting state — this
  file records an incident where `pushState` verification hid a broken nav.
  `Client=ascending` → click Type → `Type=ascending` → click again → `Type=descending`.
- **Not verified:** nothing was run against the live DB; no migration was touched.

## 2026-09-01 — BUG-003 fixed: the Client Ledger pager is gone, because there was never a page 2
**Phase:** Phase 4/5 — honesty of controls · **Status:** fixed and driven; ⚠ repo typecheck is RED on another session's file

`FUNCTIONAL_BUGS.md` BUG-003 (P1): `/reports/clients` rendered a nine-control pager
(`« ‹ 1 2 3 4 … 209 ›`) with **no handler on any of it**, and the page-number buttons set
`aria-current="page"`, so assistive tech was told this was a working pager.

### The audit's diagnosis was close but wrong, and the fix turns on the difference
It read the symptom as *"records beyond page 1 are unreachable"*. **There are none.**
`data/clientReports.ts` `CLIENTS` holds **six rows**, `ClientReports.tsx:340` maps all six
unsliced, and both figures in the footer were literals: **1,248** is the seeded *Total Clients*
KPI (`clientReports.ts:8`), and **209** is that number divided by six. The data module says the
rows are "seed decor" outright.

So it was not a broken pager — it was **decoration advertising 1,242 records this screen has
never held**. Wiring it would have produced a pager that pages through exactly one page.

### Did
- **Deleted the pager**, following this file's own precedent: a `PeriodPill` on nine cards with no
  handler was already resolved here as *"gone rather than wired"*.
- **Footer now states the truth** — `Showing all {CLIENTS.length} rows` (derived, not a literal),
  plus *"A seeded sample, not a client-register query — the full directory is at Clients"*, linking
  to `/clients`, which is the DB-backed, genuinely paginated list.
- The `aria-current="page"` lie goes with the pager.

### Verified (DOM assertions, not a screenshot — the pane would not frame the footer)
Driven in `dev:mock`, logged in, at `/reports/clients`: **6** table rows · footer reads
`Showing all 6 rows` · the seeded-sample note and the `/clients` link both present · **0** pager
buttons · no `1,248`, no `209`. The one surviving `aria-current="page"` is the sidebar marking
"Client Ledger" — checked, it is nav, not a pager remnant.
`npx vitest run` **exit 0 — 99 files, 2,321 tests**.

### ⚠ Gate status — honest
`npx tsc --noEmit` is **RED**, and it is **not this change**:
`src/actions/finance/approveDailyClosing.ts(149,11) TS2353 'clientUuid' does not exist in type
'InsertOptions'`. That file is **untracked and new** (written 20:16, ~3h after this edit), beside
modified `actions/core.ts`, `events/eventBus.ts` and `lib/rbac.ts` — a concurrent session mid-
feature. No error names any file in this change. **Not fixed here: editing another session's
in-flight work would collide.**

### Still open
Making `/reports/*` query the register is a separate job — every one of the ten report screens is
seed-only (`LAYER-D-VERIFICATION.md`). BUG-004/005/006 remain.

## 2026-09-01 — BUG-002 fixed as far as it can be without a ruling: the fake "12 unread" is gone, both dead controls now say why
**Phase:** Phase 4/5 — honesty of controls · **Status:** the bug is fixed; the **feature** is filed, not built

`FUNCTIONAL_BUGS.md` BUG-002 (P1): the header's notification bell and Help button had **no
`onClick` on any of the 56 routes**, and the bell carried a **hardcoded unread badge of 12**.

### Established first — there is no notification feature to wire to
- `notifications` exists live (12 columns) and holds **zero rows**.
- **Nothing in `src/` writes one.** The only inbox UI is
  `src/archive/notifications/UnifiedInbox.tsx` — archived, no route, no importer outside its own
  test.
- No `/notifications` or `/help` route exists in `App.tsx`.

So the badge was advertising twelve pieces of pending work that did not exist and could not be
opened — and it rendered in the **danger pair**, so it read as urgent. That is a fabricated figure
of exactly the kind the no-fabrication register exists to stop, and it needed no ruling to remove.

### Did
- **Deleted the hardcoded `12`** and its badge, and the `aria-label="Notifications, 12 unread"` —
  the label lied to screen readers specifically, which is worse than the visual because there is no
  second channel to correct it.
- **Both controls are now `Unavailable` + `disabled`**, the house pattern already used by
  RentalsList's "Save View" and Inventory's "Bulk Actions". `Unavailable` states the reason on hover
  **and on a 500 ms long-press**, so the warehouse tablet gets the explanation too — a bare `title`
  would have left touch users with nothing.
- Reasons name the open decision rather than the implementation: *"Notifications are not built yet
  — nothing writes one, so there is nothing to open."* / *"Help is not built yet — no destination is
  settled: in-app guide, docs site, or a support contact."*

### Deliberately NOT "absent, not disabled"
That rule is Law 6 — hiding money from money-blind roles, so a greyed control cannot advertise that
money exists. These two are unbuilt **for everyone**, which is a different fact and is worth saying
out loud rather than hiding. Removing them would also have quietly deleted the only affordance
where notifications will eventually live.

### Verified
- `npx tsc --noEmit` **exit 0** · `npx vitest run` **exit 0 — 99 files, 2,321 tests**.
- **Driven in `dev:mock`, logged in, at 1440×900:** both buttons report `disabled: true` with their
  reason on the wrapper; the header contains no `12`; no `aria-label` containing "unread" survives
  anywhere. Screenshot taken — the bell renders with no red badge.

### Still open — needs Babin, and this is the feature half
Building the notification centre is unruled on three points: **what generates a notification**,
**what "unread" means per user**, and **where a click lands**. Help needs one decision: destination.
Until those are answered the controls stay honest rather than dead. BUG-003 (inert Client Reports
pagination, 11 dead controls) is untouched and still open.

## 2026-09-01 — BUG-001 fixed: red `[Icon:…]` debug text is gone from client-facing UI, and the type now forbids it
**Phase:** Phase 4/5 — design-system enforcement · **Status:** fixed, driven, gate green

`FUNCTIONAL_BUGS.md` BUG-001 (P1, from the concurrent session's functional audit): **51 pieces of
red developer text were rendering inside status chips** — 25 on `/clients`, 13 on `/crew`, 13 on
`/operations/crew`. Every "Academy" membership chip read `[Icon:circle_dashed] Academy` in bold red.

### Root cause — a `string` where an `IconName` belonged
`lib/status.ts`'s `STATUS_ICON` was typed `Record<StatusKey, string>`, so nothing checked its values
against the `Icon` REGISTRY and every call site had to cast `as IconName`. Three of eight values
named glyphs that do not exist: `neutral`/`dim` → `circle_dashed`, `progress` → `progress`.
`Icon.tsx`'s miss branch then rendered them **unconditionally** as
`<span style="color:red;font-weight:bold">[Icon:…]</span>`.

`RentalsList.tsx:101` and `CrewBooking.tsx:893` had each already written a paragraph warning about
this exact hazard and dropped their own usages — the two remaining live sites were missed. The
warnings were right and the type was still wrong, which is why this recurred.

### Did — three layers, so it cannot come back
1. **`STATUS_ICON` is now `Record<StatusKey, IconName>`** (`import type` from `components/ui/Icon`,
   the same edge `lib/queries/useFilters.ts:12` already uses). A glyph the REGISTRY lacks is now a
   **compile error at the one place the map is written**. `data/warehouse.ts` and `Maintenance.tsx`
   already typed their equivalent maps this way; `lib/status.ts` was the outlier.
2. **The three names now resolve**, using existing REGISTRY glyphs — **no glyph was added**.
   `progress → timer` follows established house usage for a waiting state (`warehouse.ts`
   `Pending: 'timer'`, `BranchesWarehouses.tsx` `'Under Setup': 'timer'`). `neutral` and `dim` keep a
   **shared** glyph (`dot`), exactly as they shared `circle_dashed` — colour and word already
   separate them, and giving them distinct icons would be a design change, not a bug fix.
3. **`Icon.tsx`'s miss branch no longer leaks to production.** The red marker is kept under
   `import.meta.env.DEV` and returns `null` in the build. Safe because Law 11 (§7.4) guarantees the
   label always renders beside the icon, so a missing glyph costs decoration, never meaning.
4. **All five `as IconName` casts removed** (`ClientsDirectory.tsx:252`, `CrewBooking.tsx` ×4). The
   cast is precisely how the broken names reached the screen; deleting it is what makes (1) bite.

### Verified
- `npx tsc --noEmit` **exit 0** · `npx vitest run` **exit 0 — 99 files, 2,321 tests**.
  (⚠ tsc segfaulted once mid-run — transient, the concurrent session was building at the same time;
  clean on retry. Not a code fault.)
- **Driven in `dev:mock`, logged in:** `/clients`, `/crew` and `/operations/crew` each report
  **0** `[Icon:…]` matches in `body.innerText`, against 25/13/13 before. The Academy chips render a
  real `tabler-icon-circle-filled` glyph. Screenshot taken.

### Not touched
The audit's own `FUNCTIONAL_BUGS.md` still lists BUG-001 as open. It is **another session's
untracked, in-flight document**, so I did not edit it — this entry is the record. BUG-002 (dead
Notifications/Help on all 56 routes) and BUG-003 (inert Client Reports pagination) remain open and
need a ruling on what those controls should do.

## 2026-09-01 (cont. 2) — "finish all todos": the bare-status-ink sweep was incomplete; six more found and fixed
**Phase:** cross-phase close-out · **Status:** done, gate green

The standing list was already closed by an earlier entry today. What was left to take was
the **completeness of its own `--st-*-fg` sweep**, which reported "78 call sites classified,
9 bare". Re-derived that classification mechanically rather than re-reading the note, and
it was short: **six live bare sites survived**, three of them in files that sweep had
already edited.

### Why the miss was systematic, not careless
The previous sweep looked for bare **text**. The bug is not about text — it is that
`--st-*-fg` is *ink for a solid fill*, so it fails wherever it is spent on anything the
fill is not behind. Two whole shapes were therefore never in scope:
- a **border/ring** drawn against something other than its own fill, and
- a **`tone` prop** that a child component spends as a bare `color:` one file away.

Both shapes are represented below. The detector I used flags any `--st-*-fg` with no
`-bg`/`background` within its element window **plus every `border:` use regardless** —
that second clause is what caught the ring cases, and it is the clause a text-shaped
search cannot have.

### Fixed — six, each verified against the token table in `theme.css`
`--st-danger-fg`/`--st-in-fg` are `--on-danger`/`--on-success` = **`#ffffff` in BOTH
themes**; `--st-progress-fg` is `--on-ready` = **near-black (`#231a05`/`#1c1405`) in BOTH**.
So the first class disappears on the now-default LIGHT theme and the second on DARK.

1. **`shell/Header.tsx:229`** — the sync chip's *settled* branch. Its other four branches
   already named `--primary-text`/`--warn-text`/`--muted`/`--danger-text`; only "Synced"
   read `--st-in-fg`, against a `--surface-2` background. White on a light surface — the
   chip read as **empty** in its most common state. → `--success-text`. Note this is the
   same chip an earlier entry today had just edited for the error tooltip.
2. **`crew/CrewBooking.tsx:861`** — `MoneyStat`'s `tone` is spent as bare `color:` at
   `:872`. **Both** branches were fill-ink, so the Margin figure was white on the card
   **either side of zero** — profit and loss equally invisible. → `--danger-text` /
   `--success-text`.
3. **`crew/CrewBooking.tsx:1002`** — the conflict ring, drawn against `tone.bg`, i.e.
   whatever status fill the block already carries and never guaranteed to be the red one.
   White ring on a light chip = the conflict signal gone. → `--danger` (the line hue),
   matching `data/calendar.ts`, which already names `line: 'var(--danger)'` for this.
4. **`settings/sections/DevicePin.tsx:183`** — locked-out label; its own `else` branch was
   already `--success-text`. → `--danger-text`.
5. **`today/AlertsPanel.tsx:213`** — the CRITICAL priority word, sibling branch `--muted`.
   Its comment reads *"Law 11 — the priority … is a word on the row"*; the word was white
   on the card, so **Law 11 was breached at exactly the rows that most need it**.
   → `--danger-text`.
6. **`clients/Membership.tsx:194`** — the MIRROR direction: `--st-progress-fg` bare on a
   glyph is black-on-black in **dark**. Its two sibling branches were already text-safe.
   → `--ready-text`.

### Deliberately NOT fixed — triaged, not skipped
- **`stockCheck.ts:74/82/88`, `NewRental.tsx:1008`, `ResetWorkspace.tsx:1103`** — the
  border and its fill are on the *same element*, so the ring sits on the status colour it
  belongs to. Cosmetic at worst; the fill and word still carry the signal.
- **`NewRental.tsx:1984`** — looks bare (`background: 'transparent'`) but the enclosing
  `<li>` is `--st-danger-bg`, so the button genuinely sits on red. False positive.
- **`ResetWorkspace.tsx:1410/1419`** — a real inconsistency that the code **already
  documents in place** as cosmetic-and-not-fixed-here. Left as its author ruled it.
- **`archive/automation/EventTriggers.tsx`, `archive/notifications/UnifiedInbox.tsx`** —
  re-confirmed dead: the only non-archive mentions are prose in comments, no importers.

### Verified
- `npx tsc --noEmit` **exit 0** · `npm run check:contrast` **40/40, 0 FAIL** · `npx vitest
  run` **96 files, 2282 tests, all green**.
- Every token substituted in is gated by `check:contrast` in both themes — `danger-text`
  6.75:1 light, `success-text` 6.83:1, `ready-text` 6.05:1 on surface.
- The detector re-run is clean of all six; the 13 it still prints are the triaged set above.
- ⚠ **Not driven in a browser.** Another session holds this folder's dev-server port. These
  are token substitutions whose failure mode is a contrast ratio, and the ratios are gated
  above — but "gated" is not "seen". The six should be eyeballed on the next run that owns
  the port, `Membership` in **dark** specifically.

### ⚠ Working-tree hazard for whoever reads this next
A **concurrent session was editing this same tree during this one** — it landed `4696af8`
and prepended the Dashboard-sweep entry below while this pass was running, and left ~27
files uncommitted. My six edits are mixed in with its work and **nothing here is
committed**. Do not `git add -A` this tree without separating the two.

### Blocked — unchanged, all of it Babin's
The five standing items are untouched: token rotation, the `B-900…B-945` collision,
`full_sync.sql`, the three §4 rulings, and the ~30 money tables. None is an agent's to take.

## 2026-09-01 — Dashboard bug sweep (driven audit, no fixes applied)
**Phase:** cross-phase verification · **Status:** findings reported to owner, nothing changed

Drove every Dashboard control in mock mode (desktop/phone/tablet) plus a source pass over
`Today.tsx` / `MovementList.tsx` / `data/today.ts`. Findings, most severe first:

1. **Mock engine compares timestamps as strings** (`engine.ts` `cmp` → `String(a) < String(b)`).
   `operationalDayBounds` emits `+05:45`-offset ISO bounds; mock rows store `Z`-form —
   lexicographic comparison silently drops every row in the 00:00–06:00Z band, i.e. **the
   whole Nepal working morning (05:45–11:45 NPT)**, from every mock date-ranged read:
   Dashboard Outgoing/Incoming, Rentals pickups/returns KPIs, Operations day scope.
   Repro: pickups sandboxed at 10:00/11:00 NPT invisible; 12:00 NPT visible. Fix shape:
   `cmp` should `Date.parse` ISO-looking strings. **Mock-only, but it poisons every mock
   demo and every mock-mode verification of a day panel.**
2. **More Filters offers guaranteed-dead stage chips.** The Status group ships all six
   stages + Inspection(→Returned) to BOTH lists, but Outgoing intersects {Booked,Packed}
   and Incoming {On Rent} — five of seven live chips on Outgoing (six of seven on
   Incoming) can only ever render the empty state. Also cross-wired: the Return group's
   options appear on the Outgoing list's panel and vice versa.
3. **Row menu "Complete Pickup"/"Complete Return" look live but can never succeed**
   (stub / no-lines-by-construction). The file's own rule — "Entries that can act, act.
   The rest are explicitly unavailable" — is violated by exactly these two. Also offered
   stage-inappropriately (Complete Return on a not-yet-collected booking). The failure
   banner works (inline, role=alert, honest copy) but has no dismiss control.
4. **"Edit" navigates to the same route as "Open"** — a mislabelled duplicate.
5. **"Print Checklist" prints nothing** — navigates to Packing, identical to "Packing
   List". Two labels, one route.
6. **Hover card is `role="tooltip"` with four interactive buttons inside** — ARIA
   violation; a tooltip's controls are unreachable for keyboard/AT users. Needs a
   popover/non-modal-dialog pattern.
7. **Tomorrow-with-no-chips empty state reads "No pickups match these filters"** — the
   operator changed the day, not a filter (`outFiltered` conflates the two). The Clear
   affordance is right; the sentence blames filters that were never picked.

since 17 Aug (§4.34 DATED — the 2083 BS table); "Cash due · Not tracked yet" (§4 TODO).

**Not a bug after investigation:** layout failing to reflow on resize in the Claude

all carry reasons · menu unavailable items aria-disabled+title · Copy Booking Number ·

## 2026-09-02 — Phase 2, the client half: New Rental reads live clients and dispatches CREATE_RENTAL
**Phase:** Phase 2 — screens read the database · **Status:** client half live and green; equipment half re-scoped, NOT done

`/senior-architect next` picked this: `/rentals/new` never dispatched `createRental`, so the app
**could not create a booking** — every downstream flow (invoices, payments, the closing built
yesterday) sits on a primary write that was not wired. Verified before starting rather than
taken from `FUNCTIONAL_FIX_PLAN.md`, which had already been wrong twice.

### Did
1. **`ClientRecord.dbId`** — the real `clients.id` uuid, added ADDITIVELY beside `id`, which
   stays the `C-34` CODE every screen keys on and renders. Populated only by
   `queries/clients.ts:toClientRecord`, i.e. only by rows that came from the database, so a seed
   row is distinguishable from a bookable one by whether it has one at all.
2. **`clientPool` reads `listClientRecords()`** — filtered to rows carrying `dbId`, so a client
   that cannot be booked never looks selectable.
3. **A live product read** (`listInventory`) behind `catalogue` — 56 products in mock.
4. **`confirmBooking` dispatches for real**: `createRental` (which returns a Quote) then
   `confirmRental` with the id the database minted — never the old `bk-new` placeholder. Branch
   is read from `users.branch_id`, as `approveDailyClosing` does, because this screen has no
   branch picker and defaulting would file one branch’s booking under another.
5. **A new booking starts EMPTY.** It used to pre-pick three items from the demo catalogue.
   Once the screen writes for real that is not scaffolding but a trap: those rows carry product
   NAMES for ids, so every booking would open pre-loaded with three lines that can never save.
   `seedLine` went with them — a helper whose only job was manufacturing unsaveable rows.

### Found — my own scope estimate was wrong, and a bug in my own warning
- **The equipment half is a separate slice, not "one more data source".** I scoped this as two
   sources and one dispatch. The add path is `NewRental` → `AddItemPanel` →
   `booking/itemCatalogue.ts` (857 lines) → **five** seed modules (`data/inventory`,
   `data/addBundle`, `data/bundles`, `data/addEquipment`). My `catalogue` state is not what the
   panel serves. Stated rather than quietly half-done.
- **My first warning banner was gated on `catalogueIsLive`** — this screen’s own read, not the
   panel’s source. So it hid the warning exactly when it was still true. Now unconditional,
   which is what the panel’s actual state warrants.
- **`withMoney` would have emptied the catalogue.** `listInventory` returns `dailyRate` only
   when asked (Law 6), and my first filter required a rate > 0 — which would have handed a
   money-blind operator an empty catalogue, a Law 6 gate turning into a missing feature. Now
   filtered on `isActive` alone, with `withMoney` passed from the screen’s existing gate.

### Verified
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean for every file this session touched.
- `vitest run`: **101 files, 2341 tests, green.**
- **Driven** (mock, Owner, `/rentals/new`): the screen opens with **0 items** (was 3 demo
   lines), the client list loads live, and the banner reads *"56 real products are waiting on
   this panel’s conversion"* — the live read working and the panel’s gap stated in one line.
- ⚠ **NOT verified end to end.** A booking still cannot be completed, because the only way to
   add an item is the seed-backed panel and the new guard refuses those lines by name. So the
   dispatch itself has not run against a database. The guards are the thing standing between a
   press and a booking with products that do not exist; they are inline in a 2400-line
   component and are not unit-covered either. Both are the next slice’s job.

### Blocked / next
1. **Convert `booking/itemCatalogue.ts` to live products.** That is the remaining half of the
   identity path and it unblocks the app’s primary write end to end.
2. ⚠ **`src/modules/today/MovementList.tsx` is BROKEN in the working tree** — `MovementDispatch`
   and `MovementActionFailure` are undefined, so `tsc` is red on that file. It is the parallel
   session’s uncommitted work, was not touched here, and is deliberately not committed.

## 2026-09-01 (cont. 7) — The closing write path: APPROVE persists. Proven live, both ways
**Phase:** Phase 6 + actions · **Status:** built, driven, gate green

Babin: "build the write path". 0078 landed the table last entry; this is the action that fills
it and the button that calls it.

### Did
1. **`rbac.canApproveDailyClosing`** — §4.20’s method. It mirrors
   `daily_closings_finance_insert`’s predicate `auth_is_finance_or_admin()` (Owner · Admin ·
   Manager · Coordinator · Accounts), read from `pg_get_functiondef` on the live project rather
   than from a migration file. Offline refused, like every other money write.
2. **`closing.approve`** in `actions/core.ts`. Its OWN rule rather than one of the existing
   sets, because none carries that exact five — `canRecordPayment` is Owner/Coordinator/
   Accounts and `canPerformOperations` is a floor set. Mirroring a policy means mirroring it.
3. **`actions/finance/approveDailyClosing.ts`** — validate, resolve branch, insert, verify.
4. **The screen’s APPROVE is live**, its stale "there is no closing table" reason removed, and
   an inline error surface added (Law 12 — never a toast for a failure).

### Found — the read-back would have broken this silently
0078 revoked table-level SELECT and granted back only the 13 non-money columns. PostgREST runs
`RETURNING` **as the same role**, so `idempotentInsert`’s default read-back (`select()`,
unqualified) would have been denied on `counted_cash` — **the row commits and the write looks
like a failure.** That is the two-permissions trap `InsertOptions` already documents against
`audit_events` (§4.36 / `R3-5`), hit a second time by a different table.

Fixed by naming `returningColumns: 'id, approved_at'`, both inside the grant. **Proven, not
reasoned:** as `authenticated`, the insert returns both columns, and a raw `counted_cash`
read-back on the same row raises **42501**. The trap is real; the fix closes it.

### Two design choices, stated
- **The figures travel with the press.** The action does not re-read the day. If it did, a
  payment landing between the render and the press would mean the approver signed one statement
  and stored another. `variance` is passed and 0078’s CHECK re-derives it, so bad arithmetic is
  refused by Postgres rather than quietly stored. Law 2 is satisfied upstream — the screen did
  not compute them either, `lib/queries/closing.ts` read them.
- **The button is ABSENT, not disabled, for a role the database would refuse.** A

**Phase:** Phase 1 schema · **Status:** draft written and pre-flighted; **needs Babin to apply**

never apply a migration to the live project without explicit approval, and "add the migration"

  `invoices`/`clients` — `lib/queries/closing.ts` derives exactly them. A closing is a
  statement somebody SIGNED, and recomputing a March closing from today’s ledger would
  silently restate it every time a late correction landed. Same reasoning `invoices` stores its
  own totals instead of summing lines on read.

  `service_role`) permits exactly one transition — live → voided, touching only the three void

  void plus a new closing; a partial unique index keeps one LIVE closing per branch per day and
  lets the replacement through.

  `authenticated` loses the blanket SELECT and gets back only the non-money half; the amounts
  live behind `daily_closings_v`. A Warehouse session can see THAT a day closed and by whom
  without seeing a rupee — which is operationally useful and is why the counts stay ungated.
- Post-conditions in the file re-check every one of those at apply time.

## 2026-09-01 (cont. 4) — Daily Closing screen built · §5.4 digest shipped · driven in the browser
**Phase:** Phase 6 (screens) · **Status:** built, driven, green. APPROVE is deliberately not built — reason below

Babin: "build the daily closing screen". It was the last blocker on
`WHATSAPP_LINKS_SPEC v1.0` §5.4, so the digest ships with it.

### Did
1. **`lib/queries/closing.ts`** — `fetchDailyClosing(dayAd)` gathers all eight figures the
   digest states, in ONE place, so the screen a person signs off and the message that leaves
   the building cannot disagree. Six queries in parallel; every figure a sum of columns the
   database already maintains (`invoices.outstanding_amount`, `clients.deposit_held_amount`).
   Nothing re-prices. A single query failure rejects the whole read rather than returning a
   partial closing — a silent zero is indistinguishable from a real quiet day.
2. **`modules/finance/DailyClosing.tsx`** at **`/finance/closing`**, reached from a link in the
   Finance header. **A route, not a tab and not a nav entry:** the nav is the ruled 11 and
   `09_FINANCE.md` line 4 rules Finance’s six tabs, so neither list could grow for this.
3. **§5.4 — "Send digest on WhatsApp"**, composed from the same figures, gated on the count.

### Found — three things the spec did not answer, none invented
1. **APPROVE has nowhere to write, so it is not built.** Checked against the live database:
   no table matching clos/cash/till/reconcil/shift exists. `LOCAL_FIRST_CORE_SPEC` §6, which
   §5.4 defers to for this ritual, **is not in this repo** — so whether a closing persists, who
   may approve one, whether a day can be re-opened and what an unexplained variance costs are
   ALL unruled. The button renders unavailable carrying that reason, and the digest is gated on
   the COUNT instead — the one act here that is real. A green "Approved" that vanished on
   reload is precisely what `SUCCESS_FABRICATION_REGISTER` exists to catch.
2. **The ruled digest has four money buckets; `payment_channel_group` has five.** Cash, Bank
   and Cards keep their lines; **Digital wallets folds into "other"** — and that hides
   something real, because eSewa/Khalti are a first-class channel in this market, not a
   remainder. Adding a fifth line would change a ruled message; dropping wallets would stop the
   four totals adding up to the day’s takings. So it folds, the SCREEN shows the split the
   message cannot, and it is filed for the spec’s §6. Payments with NO channel are counted and
   shown separately rather than guessed into a bucket.
3. **Two different days are in one object, deliberately.** Movement counts use the operational
   day (D4, 06:00); collections use the calendar day, because `operationalDay.ts`’s header
   rules finance and audit boundaries stay at midnight for VAT. Not an oversight and not to be
   "fixed" by moving one — it is stated on the screen instead, so nobody meets it first as a
   variance they cannot explain.

Also ruled by the shape of the problem: **the count compares against CASH only.** Bank, card
and wallet takings are not in a drawer, so folding them into an expected figure would produce a
variance nobody could act on.

### Verified
- `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0 · `npx vitest run`: **99 files, 2321 tests, all green** (17 new).
- **Driven in the browser** (mock corpus, signed in as Owner, `/finance/closing`): the screen
   loads real figures — deposits held **Rs 5,82,500** — a counted `2500` against `Rs 0` cash
   renders **"Rs 2,500 over"**, the disabled digest carries the exact owner-number reason, and
   with a number set the link composes to `wa.me/977…` whose decoded text is the §2 template
   verbatim, `target=_blank` with `noopener noreferrer`. Screenshot taken.
- The tests pin what a mock corpus cannot: five channel groups into four buckets, the four
   adding up to the total, a null-channel payment counted, voided invoices excluded, a null
   deposit read as nothing, and `varianceLine(null)` returning **"not counted"** rather than
   "balanced" — an uncounted drawer reported as balanced would claim a reconciliation that
   never happened.

### Blocked / next
- **The closing record itself.** If Babin wants an approved closing to persist, it needs a
   table and a ruling on the four questions above. Filed as the open item; a migration is one
   session once the ruling exists.
- **`LOCAL_FIRST_CORE_SPEC` is still not in the repo** — the same absence §4.38(b) records for
   the 20/24/29 Aug documents. Placement of this screen (Finance vs Tools vs its own surface)
   is the one part nobody has ruled; it is in Finance because a closing is money.

## 2026-09-01 (cont. 3) — §5.3 shipped: the toast can carry ONE action, and the receipt reads its balance back
**Phase:** Phase 6 (screens) + components · **Status:** §5.3 done and green. §5.4 blocked on a screen that does not exist

Babin: "build 5. and toast action". §5.3 is the toast action, so this is that item and the
component change it needed.

### Did
1. **`components/ui/Toast.tsx` gains an optional `action`** — `{ label, href }`, rendered as a
   real `<a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">`. Law 12 is intact: the action is a
   follow-on to something that already SUCCEEDED, never a retry for a failure.
   **It is an href and not a callback on purpose.** The caller has to await a query before it
   can compose the link, and a `window.open` fired after an await has left its user gesture
   behind — browsers block it. An anchor cannot be blocked. That one constraint is what forces
   the caller to compose the URL BEFORE raising the toast, which is what makes the figures in
   it real (see 2).
2. **Dwell: 12s with an action, 4s without.** Four seconds is right for "that worked". It is
   about the time it takes to read a line, decide, and move a pointer — so an actionable toast
   at 4s vanishes under the cursor roughly as often as it is caught. Toasts with no action are
   untouched, so nothing else in the product got slower.
3. **§5.3 — "Send receipt on WhatsApp" on the Record Payment success**
   (`BookingDetail.tsx`). Money-gated and phone-gated: no `canBookingMoney`, no phone, or no
   composable link ⇒ the plain confirmation toast, with no action offered.

### Found — the receipt would have stated the wrong balance, and the fix is an ordering
`paymentReceipt` prints a remaining balance. Inside the `onSuccess` closure
`totals.outstanding` is the **PRE-payment** figure — the refetch fired on the line above has
not landed — so composing there tells a client they still owe the money they just handed over.
The other obvious route, subtracting the amount, is the UI doing money arithmetic that
`sync_payment_to_invoice()` owns (Law 2).

So the balance is **read back**: the handler awaits a fresh `listInvoices(invoicesForBooking)`,
sums the live rows, and only then raises the toast with the composed link. The ~100ms is
invisible next to a wrong figure in writing to a client. A failed read loses the OFFER, not the
confirmation — the payment is recorded either way, and a success never turns into an error.

### Verified
- `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0 · full suite green (see the run in this entry’s session).
- **6 new tests** in `components/ui/__tests__/toastAction.test.tsx`, driven through a real
   `ToastProvider`: the action is an anchor, `href` is the composed link, `target=_blank` with
   BOTH `noopener` and `noreferrer` (wa.me is a third-party origin and could otherwise reach
   back through `window.opener`), the row keeps a 44px target (Law 15), and the two dwells are
   asserted with fake timers — the actionable toast survives 4.5s and is gone by 12.5s, while a
   plain one is gone by 4.5s.
- **NOT verified by driving:** the receipt path end to end needs a booking with a live invoice,
   a client phone and a recorded payment; another session holds this folder’s dev-server port.
   The composition, the gates and the toast rendering are unit-covered; what is unproven is the
   real click opening WhatsApp.

### Blocked — §5.4, and it is not close
The daily digest needs a **Daily Closing screen, which does not exist**: grepped `src/` and
`docs/` for closing / cash-count / variance surfaces and found only this spec’s own mention.
`LOCAL_FIRST_CORE_SPEC`, which §5.4 defers to, **is not in this repo either** — `docs/` has
`LOCAL_DATABASE.md` and nothing else local-first. Building the digest would mean inventing the
closing workflow it reports on (cash counts, variance, an approval step), which is a product
decision this session does not get to make (`CLAUDE.md`). `dailyDigest()` and
`ownerWhatsappNumber` are built, tested and waiting; the button is one call when the screen
lands.

## 2026-09-01 — DESIGN_DIRECTION_SPEC v4.2 (Miraz feel) applied end to end
**Phase:** design system · **Status:** applied and verified in the running app

`docs/DESIGN_DIRECTION_SPEC_v4.2.md` (31 Aug ruling) is now fully applied. Most of the
token work had already landed in the tree (canvas gradients, shadow scale, card glass
vars, soft-chip tokens, theme.tsx light default); this session closed the gaps and
removed two spec violations that had ridden in with it.

### Defects found and fixed
- **`--ease` was read in 4 places and defined nowhere** (theme.css body + `.card`,
  `Page.tsx`, `Card.tsx`). An undefined custom property invalidates the whole
  declaration at computed-value time, so those transitions were silently dead — the
  same bug class theme.css's alias registry documents. Defined in `:root` (§5).
- **Miraz orange had crept back onto actions**: `--theme`/`--brand-accent`/friends
  (`#F4911E`) in both theme blocks, and Button's `brand`/`action` variants painting an
  orange button (zero call sites). All removed — §2.3: orange is a status hue only,
  never on buttons.
- **index.html still resolved an unset user to dark** (`data-theme="dark"`, fallback
  `'dark'`) while theme.tsx resolved to light — a guaranteed wrong-theme first paint
  for new users. Flipped to light + `theme-color` → `#fdefdc` (§2.1).
- **Gold on cream fails, as §3 warned**: light `--ext-line` `#af903a` measured
  **2.70:1** on `#FDEFDC` (floor is 3:1). Moved to `#8f7526` → 3.91:1 on cream,
  4.43:1 on white. `check:contrast` now gates `--ext-line` against
  `--bg-gradient-1` in both themes (dark navy stop passes at 3.37:1 — that also
  answers open item §9.1 with a measurement).
- **The canvas was invisible**: `App.tsx` shell and `AuthCard.tsx` painted opaque
  `var(--app)` over the whole viewport, hiding the body gradient and giving glass
  nothing to blur. Both wrappers are now transparent (§3).
- **KpiCard trend used `--st-in-fg`** (white ink for solid fills) on a white card —
  invisible in light theme. Moved to `--success-text`/`--ready-text`.

### Spec items landed this session
- `--r-card` 8px → **14px** (§2.4 radius map 6/8/14/999; §6 "Radius stays 14").
- Keyframes `fadeIn`/`slideUp`/`toastIn`/`pop` ported on our duration scale (§5).
- Sidebar collapse now transitions `width 240ms var(--ease)` (§5); the global
  `prefers-reduced-motion` block already kills it.
- Glass kill-switches (§4): `prefers-reduced-transparency` / `prefers-contrast: more`
  / `[data-floor]` repoint `--card`/`--surface-card`/`--sidebar` at solid surfaces and
  set `backdrop-filter: none !important` on `*` (beats the inline blurs).
- Chrome glass completed: sticky Header + phone BottomBar were 0.88 tints with **no
  blur** (content smears through a tint that doesn't blur); both now blur(20px).
  FilterDrawer panel gets the 16px sheet step.
- `scripts/check-contrast.cjs` retargeted to the light-first selector shape (it was
  already broken by the flip — it looked for `:root,\n:root[data-theme='dark']`).

### Wave 0 (§7) — verified already merged, not redone
`lib/breakpoints.ts` + `lib/device.ts` + `styles/responsive.css` (imported in
main.tsx) + the index.html pre-paint band script, with `breakpoints.test.ts` guarding
the 768/1280 duplication. Nothing to do.

### Verified
- `check:contrast`: **40/40 pass** (including the two new gold-on-canvas gates).
- `vitest run`: **94 files, 2224 tests, all pass**.
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean for every file this session touched (remaining errors are in
  another session's untracked `syncEngine.ts`/`syncContext.tsx`/`posEngines.test.ts`).
- **Driven in the app** (mock mode, fresh profile): opens LIGHT with the cream
  gradient canvas behind the auth card; signed in as owner — dashboard on the warm
  canvas, 14px cards, blue primary; toggled dark — navy gradient
  (`#050B12→#0B1622`), sidebar computed transition shows
  `width 0.24s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` (i.e. `--ease` resolves).

### Second pass — what an adversarial review of the above found
A four-lens review (CSS cascade · radius blast-radius · theme-flip consistency ·
backdrop-filter stacking) was run over the diff, each finding then handed to an
independent agent told to refute it. It caught six real defects the first pass
missed — four of them **caused by the flip itself**:

- **`--st-*-fg` used as bare text.** The fg half of a status pair is ink for a
  SOLID fill: `--st-danger-fg` is `#ffffff` in *both* themes. Bare on a light
  card that is white-on-white. A mechanical sweep classified all **78** call
  sites — 69 correctly paired with a fill, **9 bare**. Fixed the live ones to
  the gated text-safe pair (`--danger-text` / `--ready-text`): Today's Quick
  Info overdue figure, MovementList's overdue note (whose own comment cited a
  *dark-theme* measurement), both BookingDetail Notes errors, both ScreenLock
  PIN alerts, PinPad's rejection ring, PackingWorkspace's tree glyph. Two are
  deliberate non-fixes: `HandoverWorkspace:1063` is a false positive (it sits
  inside a ternary-filled yellow block) and `archive/automation/EventTriggers`
  is dead code with no importers. The mirror bug also existed —
  `--st-progress-fg` is near-black in both themes, so those sites were invisible
  in DARK. Both directions are now gated.
  Note the Today/BookingDetail/PinPad/System findings show as "refuted" in the
  review output only because I had already fixed them while it ran.
- **Body ink lagged its own canvas.** Defining `--ease` switched ON a body
  `transition: background …, color …` that had been dead (an unresolvable var
  invalidates the shorthand). Measured: the gradient cannot interpolate so it
  snaps, while `color` took 200ms — text crossing to the new theme over a canvas
  that already arrived. In dev it was caught frozen at black on the navy canvas.
  The transition is now removed and canvas + ink change in one frame (verified
  by sampling both 32ms after a toggle).
- **PWA manifest still shipped the dark canvas.** `vite.config.ts` kept
  `background_color`/`theme_color: '#0F1420'` while index.html flipped to
  `#fdefdc` — an installed cold launch would paint a full-screen dark splash and
  permanently mismatched window chrome. (`#0F1420` matched *neither* theme.)
- **`--r-card` 8 → 14 squared off four cards' corners.** A child with an opaque
  background flush inside a padding-0 card paints over the parent's rounded
  corner; at 14px the overhang is ~4.1px, plainly visible. Verified empirically
  in the browser (hit-testing the corner pixel) rather than by eye. Fixed by
  giving the flush child the card's radius — **not** `overflow: hidden` on the
  card, which would have clipped ClientsDirectory's absolutely-positioned
  row-action menu. Membership, ClientsDirectory, Maintenance, Bundles (top) and
  AddBundle's totals `tfoot` (bottom). Maintenance/Bundles bottoms were checked
  and are fine — their footer strips carry no background.
- **A modal was living inside the new glass chrome.** `HandoverSheet` renders a
  `Modal` (`position: fixed; inset: 0`, and this codebase uses no portals) from
  *inside* `<header>`, which I had just given `backdrop-filter`. Measured on
  Chromium 148: `filter` and `transform` do trap a fixed child, `backdrop-filter`
  does not — but WebKit treats it as a containing block, which would collapse a
  full-screen modal into the 59px header strip on iPad. Moved out to a sibling,
  matching `BottomBar.tsx:128`, which already renders `MoreSheet` outside its own
  glass `<nav>`.
- **Two more undefined tokens**, same class as the alias registry: `--t-caption`
  (6 call sites across three modals) and `--text-dim` (2 in Tools) were read but
  defined nowhere, so those labels silently inherited body size/colour. Probed
  live to confirm before aliasing.

Also removed `--ease-bounce`/`--ease-spring` (zero readers; a bounce curve
contradicts §5's single-curve rule), and corrected Settings' Theme note, which
still told operators "dark uses gold" — a palette retired on 25 Aug.

**Verified after the second pass:** `check:contrast` 40/40 · `vitest` 95 files /
2241 tests, exit 0 · `tsc --noEmit` clean · driven in the app (light default on
the cream canvas, dark toggle intact, the Overdue figure now legible where it
had been invisible). One earlier run reported a transient error that did not
reproduce — the concurrent session was editing files mid-run.

⚠ The `prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce` media query is ACTIVE in this
machine's browser, so the glass was exercised via its opaque fallback for most
of the session. The kill-switch is therefore well proven (blur `none`, tokens
solid, beating the inline `backdropFilter`); the glass path was verified
separately by removing that rule at runtime (chrome blur 20px, tokens at the
0.88 floor). Glass has **not** been eyeballed on a display without that setting.

### Blocked / for Babin
- **§8's same-pass downstream updates cannot be done from this machine**: no
  `DESIGN_DIRECTION_SPEC_v4.1.md`, `UI_UX_SPEC`, `CLAUDE_DESIGN_INSTRUCTIONS`,

## 2026-09-01 (cont. 3) — BS dates stop hiding: the em dash is gone from eight sites · the month-length table stays open
**Phase:** Phase 4/5 — date engine consumers · **Status:** fixed and verified in the running app;
the underlying BS table is **still open and needs Babin**

Since 17 Aug 2026 the app had been rendering `—` where it held a perfectly good date. `lib/bs.ts`
can only name days inside Shrawan 2083 (anchor 16 Jul + 32 days), and eight call sites wrote
`bs ? formatBs(bs) : '—'`. On the Dashboard and Finance pills the dash took the **bold** line while
the real English date sat muted beneath it — the app hiding a date it knows, and the thing the
31 Aug walk saw and misfiled as "Finance period control shows a blank start date".

### Did — no new date arithmetic, no invented calendar data
1. **Adopted `lib/bs.ts:135 formatBsOrAd()`**, which already existed for exactly this ("Never null,
   never an em dash, never a guessed BS day") and had **zero importers**. Now used by
   `CasesWorkspace`, `queries/clients.ts`, `ReturnWorkspace`, `ResetWorkspace`, `PackingWorkspace`.
   `toBs`/`formatBs` dropped from those five import lists (they became unused).
2. **The two date pills** (`data/today.ts` `TODAY_DATE`, `Finance.tsx` `AS_OF`) now carry
   `bs: string | null` instead of a pre-baked `'—'`, and the renderers promote the AD date to the
   lead line, printing "Nepali date unavailable" beneath with `BS_UNSUPPORTED_NOTE` as its `title`.
   Law 9's BS-above-AD ordering is untouched wherever BS *can* be named.
3. **`Warehouses.tsx`** ×2 — the transfer cell promotes AD to the lead line; the activity line drops
   the orphan `—  ·` separator. `archive/wall/WallDisplay.tsx` updated for the null.
4. **The `!iso` dash is deliberately kept** in the three floor workspaces — no instant really is no
   date. Only the second branch (a known instant with no BS name) changed.
5. **Four tests added** to `lib/__tests__/bs.test.ts` for `formatBsOrAd`, including a sweep asserting
   no day across ±400 days returns `—` or empty, and a Kathmandu-civil check on the fallback path.

### Verified
- `npx tsc --noEmit` **exit 0**; `npx vitest run` **exit 0 — 96 files, 2,282 tests**.
- **Driven in the mock app** (`dev:mock`, real clock = 1 Sep 2026, i.e. outside the BS window):
  the Dashboard pill reads **"1 Sept 2026 / Nepali date unavailable"** where it previously read
  **"— / 1 Sept 2026"**; `/finance` shows the same. Screenshot taken.
- ⚠ One test expectation of mine was wrong and the code was right: en-GB's short month for
  September is **"Sept"**, not "Sep". Corrected the assertion, not the renderer.

### ⛔ Still open — and NOT an agent's call
`toBs` still answers only inside **Shrawan 2083**, so BS dates are now *absent* (English shown)
rather than *hidden*. Closing that needs the **2080–2090 BS month-length table**. A BS month is
29/30/31/32 days with no derivable rule, `bs.ts:50-65` explicitly forbids extrapolating, and no such
table exists anywhere in this workspace (searched, including the spec library). **I did not invent
one** — a wrong month length silently shifts every subsequent date, which is `Calendar.md` §4.2's
highest-priority correctness bug in a new costume. Babin supplies or approves a source.

## 2026-09-01 (cont. 2) — The gap check's 38 P1/P2 claims verified against source: 4 false, 17 partial · eight new defects found, one of them a live law breach
**Phase:** verification · **Status:** done, read-only. Record:
[`docs/booqable/GAP-CHECK-VERIFICATION.md`](docs/booqable/GAP-CHECK-VERIFICATION.md)

I had turned the gap check's P1/P2 items into backlog checkboxes on the walk's word alone. Ten
agents (five verifying clusters, five adversarially attacking every "X does not exist" verdict)
re-derived all 38 from source with `file:line`. **17 CONFIRMED · 17 PARTIAL · 4 FALSE · 0
UNVERIFIABLE.** No absence verdict survived unchanged.

**The repeated shape: built somewhere, missing here.** A UI walk cannot tell built from wired, or
here from anywhere — that is the structural limit this exercise measured.

### The four that were simply wrong
- **`FilterRail` exists** — `Inventory.tsx:925`, live, reflows below 1280, and predates the walk by
  three days. Three more pages carry a `SideRail label="Filters"`. The genuinely dead piece is
  `FilterOptionList` (zero production importers).
- **Facet counts exist** — wired on Rentals (`RentalsList.tsx:27,563,618`) behind the collapsed
  Status accordion (`enabled: open`). Also: **the "second `facetCounts.ts`" the layer-d pass
  reported is a git-worktree copy**, byte-identical — corrected in the backlog.
- **The FY 2083/84 + branch chip it praises does not exist.** `Header.tsx` has zero matches. It was
  likely seeded by doc rot: `ReportToolbar.tsx:75` asserts the header pill says FY 2083/84.
- **"Finance blank start date"** — misread; see the BS defect below.

### Both build-order assumptions are half wrong
- **Item 3:** `lib/workflow` has **no** single-stage next-verb function (only `canAdvance(from,to)`,
  `jobThatSets(to)`, `planTransition({from,to})`); the lookup exists three times elsewhere, and a
  "Reset" primary already renders on Operations Queues and Today — so the Booking Detail fix is a
  **label**. ⛔ **But there is no Close verb anywhere** (`Reset.sets` null, `closeGates` has no
  production caller, ResetWorkspace records a reset and does not close). Returned → Closed must be
  built from scratch; item 3's "Reset/Close" is unbuildable as written.
- **Item 4:** `periodRange` answers **6 of 16** presets and **ReportToolbar does not share it**.
  The item is "extend by ten cases and migrate ReportToolbar", not "wire to an existing engine".

### 🐞 Eight defects the walk missed — full list in the doc, the load-bearing ones here
1. **BS dates are broken for every date after 16 Aug 2026.** `lib/bs.ts` covers only Shrawan 2083
   (anchor 16 Jul + 32 days); `toBs` returns null beyond it, so the Finance header pill
   (`Finance.tsx:180`) and Dashboard date pill (`data/today.ts:76-80`) render `—`. **The
   BS-above-AD law is failing in production** — live only inside a window that closed a fortnight
   before the walk praised it. Fix exists as dead code: `bs.ts:135 formatBsOrAd()`, zero importers.
2. **`/rentals/B-701/evidence` refuses to load** — `EvidenceWorkspace.tsx:174-175` hard-gates on
   `BOOKING.no` (B-715). The constant is not gone; Booking Detail was fixed, Evidence was not.
3. **`LogCaseModal.tsx:90`** files a booking-less case against `'B-715'`.
4. **Operations bypasses `operationalDayBounds`** (`OperationsQueues.tsx:201-208`, raw midnights)
   while Today is 06:00-anchored — **two screens disagree about "today"**, undermining D4.

### Corrections that prevent damage
- **Payment Due grey is NOT a Law 6 breach** (settled from source, no Warehouse session needed).
  `chipsFor(canSeeMoney)` already strips the chip before render, test-locked. Re-enabling it would
  ship a money filter with no column behind it. **Box closed.**
- **The two "duplicate" More Filters are not duplicates** — different state, distinct accessible

## 2026-09-01 (cont.) — Scoping the gap check's P0 found a blocking numbering collision, two corrupting import scripts, and a committed API token
**Phase:** investigation · **Status:** findings recorded; **three items need Babin, none actionable by an agent**

Filing the gap check left "corpus import/bridge" as an open box. Scoping what it would actually
cost turned up four things, all measured 1 Sep against the live DB (MCP, read-only) and the tree.
Full writeup: [`docs/booqable/BRIDGE-AND-CORPUS-STATE.md`](docs/booqable/BRIDGE-AND-CORPUS-STATE.md).
**No sync was run, no migration applied, no Booqable API call made.**

### ⛔ 1. The applied 0076 seed corpus squats on live Booqable booking numbers
`bookings.booking_no` is **UNIQUE**. Booking numbers map 1:1 to Booqable order numbers — live
**`B-898` carries `return_at = 2026-08-31 06:00`, exactly the due-back the gap check reports for
Booqable #898.** The import covered orders **700–899** (`B-700…B-899`, 200 rows). Then
`0076_seed_operational_stage_corpus` inserted 46 synthetic rows numbered **`B-900…B-945`** — the
range the next real orders need (the capture probed Booqable **#906** live on 31 Aug).

Importing #900+ now fails on the unique index. **The blocking rows cannot be deleted** (Law 3 /
`trg_bookings_reject_delete`, every role incl. `service_role`), and **cancelling does not free the
number**. Options costed in §4; (a) renumbering 0076's rows via a new migration looks cheapest and
keeps the #N ↔ B-N convention — but it is a live write against an applied migration and is
**Babin's ruling**.

Knock-on: the gap check's own acceptance test names #898 and #903. B-898 is real; **B-903 is a
synthetic seed row wearing that number** (unrelated dates). Half that test currently reads a fake.

### 2. The bridge is built and off-line — this was never a build task
`src/lib/booqable/sync.ts` (109 KB, dependency-ordered pull phases, `external_refs` bookkeeping,
`sync_conflicts`, write-back allowlist) + seven mappers (~270 KB) +
`supabase/functions/booqable-proxy/index.ts` (**exists** — `client.ts`'s "proxy not written in
this pass" header is stale) + `scripts/run-full-sync.ts` calling `runFullPull`.
**Nothing under `src/` imports any of it** — every outside mention is prose in a module header or
an error string. Not dead: off-line.

Corpus: 246 bookings · 366 clients · 204 products · **0** payments/invoices/product_units/
stage_transitions. `external_refs` covers only `clients` (100) and `products` (71) — **zero
`orders` refs**, so no booking traces back to Booqable and a re-sync would **duplicate rather than
update**. A refs back-fill is a prerequisite to any re-sync.

### 3. Two import scripts would corrupt bookings if run today
`scripts/full_sync.sql` (223 KB) and `generated_import.sql` insert every booking with
`client_id = (SELECT id FROM public.clients LIMIT 1)` — arbitrary, no ORDER BY — and
`pickup_at = return_at = NOW()`. Their idempotency guard checks `external_refs` rows with
`entity='orders'` that **were never written**, so it suppresses nothing: a run inserts 100 (or 25)
mis-clientned zero-length bookings, permanently.

spread, zero zero-length rentals. **The live 200 came from a better path, not from these files.**

Hard-coded with a Supabase key in four git-tracked scripts (`import-booqable-direct.mjs`,
`import-via-mcp-sql.mjs`, `sync-all-booqable-data.mjs`, `sync-booqable-data.mjs`) since commit

## 2026-09-01 — Law 6 exercised per role at runtime: gate is correct; `clients` is a LIVE breach, not a latent one
**Phase:** cross-phase verification (**no code changed, no migration applied**) · **Status:** complete

### Did
Closed `DECISION-SHEET.md` §5's first item — *"the highest-value follow-up in the pack"* — by
**exercising** Law 6 rather than reading policies. Each probe: `begin; set local role authenticated;
set_config('app.current_user_id', …); … rollback;`. Written up in
[`docs/booqable/RLS-PER-ROLE-2026-08-31.md`](docs/booqable/RLS-PER-ROLE-2026-08-31.md).

### Verified
- **RLS provably filters at runtime** — same connection, Warehouse sees 246 bookings / 366 clients,
  Client sees **0 / 0**. Unknown uid fails closed to `Client`.
- **The gate is correct for all four money-blind roles.** Each money table carries two permissive
  SELECT policies which Postgres OR-combines; evaluated across the whole `system_role` enum the two
  predicates agree on all nine roles, so the OR is redundant today.
- **The `_v` masks work on live data** — `clients_v`, identical 366 rows: Owner reads
  `payment_terms` 366 times, Warehouse **0**.
- **`payments` immutability is enforced by the database** — no UPDATE and no DELETE policy exists,
  so both are denied. All three money tables have real `with_check` allowlists on INSERT, none null.
- **0062's mechanism works where it was applied** — a Warehouse read of `bookings.deposit_required`
  returns `ERROR 42501: permission denied for table bookings`.

### Found
**Base `clients` leaks what `clients_v` masks.** A Warehouse session reads `payment_terms` for all
**366** clients from the base table. `0062` armed the column mask for exactly four tables —
`bookings`, `booking_lines`, `products`, `product_units` — and **`clients` is not in it**;
`0038`'s column-revoke on `clients` is the shape `0062`'s own header calls ineffective.
`src/lib/queries/clients.ts:18-20` asserts the opposite as settled fact: *"selecting them from
`clients` fails outright for everyone."* It does not.

**This one is live, not latent — the distinction from I5.** 0077's four tables have no reader in
`src/` (its own §3). `clients` does, and it is reachable by every signed-in role:
`Header.tsx:45 triggerSync` → `syncContext.tsx:36 syncAll()` → `syncEngine.ts:166`
`.from('clients').select('*').limit(300)` → money into IndexedDB as a Warehouse session.
`App.tsx:96` mounts `SyncProvider` app-wide.

### Ruled
Nothing. Two options surfaced, neither taken: add `clients` to `0077` (same mechanism, same shape),
and/or narrow `syncEngine.ts:166` to an explicit non-money column list — a one-line change that
closes the live path immediately without `0062`'s ordering hazard. **A migration needs Babin's
approval (`CLAUDE.md`), and the call-site change must ship first.**

### Blocked
- `tsc --noEmit` not clean; errors move between runs and belong to another session's in-flight
  refactors. Not touched.

## 2026-09-01 — 0077 drafted: the four I5 breaches, armed the way 0062 actually works
**Phase:** Phase 1 schema · **Status:** draft written, **NOT APPLIED** — needs approval

I5 found four tables whose money columns are raw behind a row policy that admits a money-blind
role, and proposed a four-line fix. The fix as written would have closed nothing. New migration:
[`0077_law6_arm_the_four_unarmed_tables.sql`](supabase/migrations/0077_law6_arm_the_four_unarmed_tables.sql).

### ⚠ Two premises this session was given turned out to be false
Both were caught by reading the live ledger, and both would have shipped a broken file.

1. **"Live is at 0070; 0071–0073 are drafts awaiting approval."** Live is at **0076**.
   `schema_migrations` shows 0071 (31 Aug 11:57), 0072 (12:01), 0074_drop_discount_gate (12:42),
   **0075_drop_invoice_lines_discount_gate (13:19)** and **0076_seed_operational_stage_corpus
   (14:12)** all applied. Nothing is awaiting approval.
2. **Therefore this file could not be 0075.** It was written as 0075 and **renumbered to 0077**
   — 0075 and 0076 were both taken by the concurrent session *while it was being written*.
   Numbering moved four times in one session: `0073_discount_policies.sql` → 0074 at 17:33, then
   a second 0074 at 17:57, then 0075 at 18:59, 0076 at 19:58, another 0076 at 20:17.

⚠ **`0076_booking_line_units_release.sql` is on disk, is NOT in the ledger, and collides with the
applied `0076_seed_operational_stage_corpus`.** Same collision class as the 0017/0018 one 0019's
header records from 9 Aug. It needs renumbering before it can apply. Not touched — another
session's file. **Re-read the ledger before trusting any number in that directory.**

### Found — before writing a line
1. **I5 §3's one-liner is a no-op, and two of its four lines have already been issued once.**
   `revoke select (col) … from authenticated` cannot subtract from a table-level grant, and
   Supabase grants table-level SELECT on every `public` table to `authenticated`. This is the
   exact finding 0062's and 0048's headers both carry against the live DB (`pg_class.relacl` =
   `authenticated=arwDxtm/postgres`; `pg_attribute.attacl` null). **0035:38 already revokes
   `accessories.replacement_cost` and 0036:151 already revokes `vehicle_fuel_logs.cost_amount`** —
   and I5's own probe then read both columns as Warehouse. That is the mechanism being falsified
   on live data, not a theory. §3's claim that this is "the mechanism 0062 established" reads
   0062 backwards: 0062's mechanism is the reverse — `revoke select ON TABLE`, then
   `grant select (<non-money columns>)`. 0077 does that.
2. **Two of the four `_v` views do not exist.** §3 says each table "has a masked `_v` sibling
   (`accessories_v`, `vehicle_fuel_logs_v`, …)" — the ellipsis is wrong. `booking_transport_v`
   and `maintenance_records_v` have never been written in any file. `bookingQuery.ts:466` says so
   independently. A bare revoke would have left Owner/Admin/Coordinator with **no** path to
   `delivery_charge` / `fuel_charge` / `cost`, not a masked one. 0077 creates both, in the same
   file as the revoke — the 0019/0035/0036 convention.
3. **Nothing in `src/` reads any of the four tables.** Zero `.from('accessories' | 'booking_transport'
   | 'maintenance_records' | 'vehicle_fuel_logs')`, single- or double-quoted. Every column-name hit
   is generated types, one Law 6 forbidden-word list in `floorVerbs.test.ts:475`, or prose. No SQL
   function or trigger reads them either — the only `from <table>` anywhere in the tree is the two
   masking-view bodies. **So 0077 needs no call-site migration**, unlike 0062, which needed a
   74-site audit and 0065's two schema prerequisites. It is the cheapest of the pending drafts.

### Did
- Revoke + non-money grant for all four: accessories (12 cols, 11 granted), booking_transport
  (14/12), maintenance_records (21/20), vehicle_fuel_logs (11/10). Lists read from the `create
  table` blocks after confirming no `alter table … add/drop/rename column` touches any of the four
  in any migration; two counts corroborated by 0048's own asserted view counts. Grant lists and view
  column lists were then diffed against the DDL mechanically, not by eye.
- Created `booking_transport_v` and `maintenance_records_v`, definer-rights with the row predicate
  inlined (0048/0065 pattern). Predicates read off the policies: transport mirrors
  `booking_transport_driver_read` (0014) verbatim; maintenance is `auth_is_staff()`, since
  `maintenance_records_select` (0020) and `_all` (0018) are PERMISSIVE and OR together.
- Post-conditions that would have caught this bug class three migrations ago: the table grant is
  gone · each money column unreachable **and** a neighbouring operational column still readable
  (catches an over-broad revoke) · base-table column counts match what the grant lists assume ·
  all four views exist, carry a WHERE, and are **not** `security_invoker`.

### Verified against the live database (read-only, 1 Sep — nothing applied)
Every assumption in the file was first derived statically from the tree, then confirmed against
the live catalogue. All six checks agreed with the static reading:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Column names/order/counts (`pg_attribute`) | **exact match** — 12 · 14 · 21 · 11, same order as the grant lists |
| `has_table_privilege(authenticated,'SELECT')` on the four | **true** on all four — the breach is open |
| Column-level ACLs on the four (`attacl`) | **0** — 0035/0036's column revokes left no trace at all |
| Same two checks on `bookings` / `products` | **false**, with 27 / 35 column ACLs — **0062 is applied and working** |
| `pg_policies` on the four | all six predicates match what the new views inline, verbatim |
| `reloptions` on `accessories_v` / `vehicle_fuel_logs_v` | **(none)** → definer-rights; `booking_transport_v` / `maintenance_records_v` **absent** |
| Row counts | **0 · 0 · 0 · 0** — still empty, so applying changes no visible figure |

Two things that matter beyond this file. The `attacl = 0` row is the one-line fix being falsified
on live data rather than quoted from 0062's header — PostgreSQL did not record those revokes at
all. And the `bookings`/`products` row is the same defect **already fixed correctly**, which is
what makes 0077 a repeat of a proven change rather than a first attempt.

**No view breaks; no money-visible screen blanks.**

### Flagged, deliberately not fixed
- **`vehicle_fuel_logs_v`'s row predicate is broader than its own table's policy.** 0048's header
  says the view should carry the `vehicle_fuel_logs_all` list; the SQL it shipped (0048:731) says
  `where auth_is_staff()`, which also admits Accounts and Technician. 0077 does not widen it, but
  it becomes the sanctioned gate once the base table closes. Needs a ruling.
- **`booking_transport_driver_read` excludes Manager *and* Accounts.** Accounts is money-visible and
  still cannot read a transport row at all. Pre-existing; the new view mirrors the policy rather
  than quietly widening it.
- **`vehicle_fuel_logs.receipt_url` stays granted.** A receipt image obviously shows the amount —
  that is a storage-bucket question (I5 §4), and a column grant does not answer it.
- `anon` keeps its table grant, matching 0062. It is denied by RLS on all four (resolves to
  `Client`), so the columns are unreachable — but by a **row** denial, not a grant denial.

### Blocked / next
**Not applied, per CLAUDE.md — awaiting approval.** Everything that would normally gate it is now
settled rather than assumed: 0062/0065 are confirmed applied (0065 first, as its header requires),
the pattern is confirmed working on `bookings`/`products`, the four tables are confirmed empty, and
0077 has no ordering dependency on 0071/0072/0074/0075/0076 — disjoint tables. The remaining gate
is a decision, not a check.

Two things to carry forward:
- **Stop diagnosing from migration headers.** 0062's own file still reads ⛔ DO NOT APPLY and has
  been applied since 28 Aug. The ledger is the authority; this is now the fourth time that
  confusion has cost a session.
- **Forward obligation once applied:** the first write path built against any of these four tables
  must send `Prefer: return=minimal` or name granted columns — PostgREST's unqualified `RETURNING`
  will 42501 otherwise (0065's hazard, future here rather than live, since nothing writes them yet).

## 2026-08-31 — facetCounts wired to /rentals: the Status accordion shows §10 option counts
**Phase:** Phase 6 wiring (no schema/engine changes) · **Status:** complete

The 31 Aug Layer D pass named this "the best next piece of code": `facetCounts.ts` was
built and tested with zero callers, so no screen showed an option count. `useFacetCounts`
(and through it `countFacet`) now has its first live caller.

### Did
1. **`StatusFilterGroup` (RentalsList.tsx) renders a count beside each of the six stages**,
   following `FilterOptionList`'s §10 rendering rule verbatim: dash while loading/failed,
   `0` only as a computed fact. `enabled: open` — the six `count=exact` probes run only
   while the accordion is showing them.
2. **The page-injected counter respects the chip intersection.** This group could not use
   `countFacet`'s default base-strip: `chips.stage` on this page is the quick chip's
   structural set INTERSECTED with the Status picks (`narrowStages`), so stripping it would
   count `Quote` under an `Active` chip as "all quotes". The probe travels under a column
   name the server never sees (`status`), and `statusCountRows` rebuilds the real query via
   `rentalsQuery(chip, dates, [probe], NOW_AD, sub)` — `impossible` from a stage the chip
   does not carry returns a computed 0; Sub-Rental-unanswered (`bookingIds === null`)
   returns null → dash, never a fake 0. The chip's structural stages stay in the hook's
   base filters, which is what keys a re-count when only the chip changes (two chips that
   differ solely in stage set would otherwise produce identical keys → stale counts).
3. Neither call passes `withDeposit` (Law 6) — a count carries no money.

### Verified (mock app, driven)

  Closed 16 — sums to the list's own "120 Rentals found".
- §10 own-group strip: ticking Quote narrows the list to "18 Rentals found" while every
  sibling count HOLDS (31/17/24/14/16) — the group can still be widened.
- Chip intersection: under quick chip On Rent, list reads 24 and the accordion reads
  0/0/0/24/0/0 — the impossible intersections are computed zeros, not stripped-base lies.
- Switching back to All re-fires: counts return to 18/31/17/24/14/16. Console clean.
- `vitest run` facetCounts + FilterDrawer suites: 29/29 pass.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — the ONLY errors are in another session's in-flight discount work
  (`discount.test.ts` / `money.test.ts` reference `applyPolicy` / `DISCOUNT_APPROVAL_THRESHOLD`,
  unstaged edits to `lib/discount.ts` + `lib/money.ts` not from this session); zero errors
  in the files this session touched.

`FilterOptionList` itself remains mounted only in its own test — the /rentals rail's

> exactly as `seed.ts`'s frozen anchor did — just from a later start. When Going out empties again
