  longer hand-writes Devanagari BS strings — `BOOKING.pickup`/`ret` now compute through
  `toBs()`/`formatBs()`/`formatAd()` from two `Date.UTC` constants. `BookingDetail.tsx`'s
  Pickup/Return `Fact` now renders BS bold/primary above AD+time secondary, matching
  Foundation's locked BS-over-AD order (was reversed).
- **F3**: added an optional `days` field to `LineItem` and set `days: '3'` on every
  `ITEMS` row that carries a `total` (9 of 12 rows; the 3 pure grouping rows get neither).
  Added a `Days` column to the equipment table between Location and Rate/Day. Deliberately
  did **not** multiply any row's `total` by days — this dataset is a flat-priced 18-item
  bundle (`FX3 Documentary Package`, Rs 60,750 for the whole 3-day package), not the
  spec's simpler flat per-day-line example, and multiplying the child breakdown rows
  would have double-counted against the bundle's own already-correct total. Documented
  the reasoning inline so a future reader doesn't "fix" it into a real bug.
- **F6**: `ALERTS`'s low-stock entry (`'NISI Athena set...'`) changed from
  `tone: 'danger'` to `'progress'`, matching the other two alerts. Had to also add an
  explicit `{ tone: 'danger' | 'progress' }[]` type annotation to `ALERTS` — without it,
  removing the array's only `'danger'` entry narrows the inferred type to a single
  literal, which broke `BookingDetail.tsx`'s `a.tone === 'danger'` comparison with a
  `tsc` "no overlap" error (caught by running `tsc --noEmit` after the first pass, before
  calling the fix done).
- **F4** (VAT rounding): already correct at the engine level; `data/booking.ts`'s
  `TOTALS`/`RENTAL_TOTAL`/`CHARGES` hardcoded strings already matched the engine's output
  exactly, so left untouched rather than refactoring something that wasn't wrong.
- **F5**: deliberately **not** fixed, per the spec's own instruction — crew billing
  stays Rs 72,000 (no silent +800). Verified no code path reintroduces 72,800.
- **F7**: found already resolved, by a different and more thorough mechanism than the
  spec assumed. `BOOKING.status` is `'Booked'` (not a hardcoded `'Draft'` string) — a
  prior session concluded the render's "Draft chip + fully packed items" was internally
  inconsistent (Packing only runs at status Booked per `lib/workflow.ts` §1.5) and fixed
  the underlying status rather than just relabeling the chip. `'Draft'` isn't even a
  valid `BookingStatus` anymore (moved to `Flag`, and `BOOKING.flags` is empty). Left
  alone — changing it to `'Quote'` per the spec's literal text would have contradicted
  the packing evidence and been a regression.
- Left the five-section layout, right rail and header action set untouched per the
  spec's explicit "No redesign" scope note, even though the reference photo
  (`New_booking_light_mode_with_crew_and_documents_expanded.PNG`) shows a differently
  laid out right rail — the photo is documented in-code (`money.ts`'s own
  `REFERENCE_CASE` comment) as showing superseded seed numbers, so it was treated as a
  visual/contextual reference, not a layout spec to match pixel-for-pixel.

### Verified
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors, whole repo, both before and after the post-hoc
  `RENTAL_PAYMENTS` fix (two separate runs).
- Independent adversarial verification: ran a 5-agent workflow, each re-deriving one
  defect's fix from the actual current file contents (not trusting my own summary) —
  hand-traced `toBs()`'s arithmetic for both dates, hand-traced `price()`'s rounding
  chain against the reference case, re-counted every `ITEMS` row's `total`/`days`
  pairing and confirmed no row's total was multiplied, confirmed the `ALERTS` type fix,
  confirmed `BOOKING.status`/`Flag` typing. Caught the `RENTAL_PAYMENTS` hardcoding gap
  this way — fixed immediately after.
- Drove the app directly (own dev server, auto-assigned port — this repo has a
  concurrent session's server already running elsewhere): loaded `/rentals/BK-2026-0715`
  and read the rendered text. Confirmed "Pickup / 1 Shrawan 2083 BS / 16 Jul 2026 · 06:00
  AM", "Return / 4 Shrawan 2083 BS / 19 Jul 2026 · 06:00 AM", a Days column reading `3`
  on every priced equipment row with Equipment Subtotal still Rs 60,750, "Payment History
  (Rental)" showing exactly the one Advance row, Rental Outstanding Rs 1,24,506
  everywhere it appears, Crew Subtotal 72,000, and the NISI Athena alert's DOM background
  computed to `var(--st-progress-bg)` (not danger). The default seeded role
  (`lib/auth.tsx`, a concurrent session's own Warehouse-role test toggle) hides the whole
  money-gated Pricing & Payments block by design (Law 6) — temporarily flipped it to
  `'Owner'` in my own dev server instance to see that block, confirmed the render, then
  reverted the line exactly (`git diff` shows only the concurrent session's own
  Warehouse-vs-committed-Owner change, nothing net-new from me).

### Found
- The MD spec's F3 worked example (Sony FX6/Sigma/DJI, flat per-day lines) doesn't match
  this codebase's actual seed data (an 18-item flat-priced bundle) — applied the
  *principle* (days explicit on every priced line, Law 9) rather than the literal
  numeric example, to avoid a double-counting regression.
- `RENTAL_PAYMENTS` in `data/booking.ts` was still hardcoding two values `MONEY` already
  computed — the exact class of drift-risk F1 exists to close. Fixed (see Did).

  Devanagari string as a historical reference (not live data) — left as-is, it's
  documentation, not a rendered value.

## 2026-08-09 — Hover Intel System v2.1, wave 2: Bundle/Maintenance/Document/Cases + Booking-Payment/Invoice/Crew/Supplier

**Phase:** cross-cutting feature (ahead of Phase 1/2) · **Status:** 8 of the 13 condensed-spec
cards done (Quote/Production/Rack/a real Supplier profile still don't exist as data concepts —
see the first HIS v2.1 entry's Blocked/next). All built by an 8-agent workflow against the
Client/Equipment cards as the reference pattern, one entity/file-group per agent to keep the
parallel edits collision-free.

### Scoping, decided before building
Surveyed all 13 condensed entities first and found they aren't uniform: three (Bundle,
Maintenance, Document) plus Damage/Missing already sit on correctly money-gated screens; five
(Booking's *detail* page, Payment, Invoice, Crew, Supplier) sit on screens with **zero** money
gating at all — a real, independently-confirmed Law 6 gap (`CrewBooking.tsx`/`SubRental.tsx`
were already flagged in `AUDIT_FINDINGS.md`/this log before today); and four (Quote, Production,
a Supplier *profile*, Rack) don't exist as their own data/screen concept at all — Quote is a
`BookingStatus` value, Production is an explicit `<Placeholder>` stub, Rack has no queryable
"this rack's contents" object anywhere. On explicit direction: built the first two tiers this
pass (fixing the gating gap before wiring the card, not after), left the third for later since it
means modeling new features, not wiring cards onto existing ones. Damage/Missing specifically:
two disjoint implementations exist (`CasesQueue.tsx`+`data/cases.ts`, correct and gated; the
duplicate `CasesWorkspace.tsx`, stale inline dataset, ungated, reachable from two routes) — built
against `CasesQueue.tsx` only, on explicit direction, leaving the duplicate un-reconciled (already
tracked as a known bug).

### What shipped, per entity
- **Bundle** (`data/bundleIntel.ts`, `data/bundles.ts`, `Bundles.tsx`) — physical/virtual lock
  mode, mandatory/replaceable/substitute flags on 2 real bundles. No `primaryAction` on the
  glance — Bundle detail has no screen yet, so a link there would have been fabricated.
- **Maintenance** (`data/maintenanceIntel.ts`, `Maintenance.tsx`) — parts + downtime seeded on 2
  of 3 real jobs; cost group gated `asset-finance`. Found: `MaintenanceRecord` lives inline in the
  page rather than in `data/`, unlike every other entity here — flagged for a future extraction,
  not fixed this pass (`maintenanceIntel.ts`'s header documents it).
- **Document** (`data/documentIntel.ts`, `data/documents.ts`, `Documents.tsx`) — signer/versions

## 2026-08-09 — App-wide cross-page link audit: 7-cluster discovery, 20 fixes applied
**Phase:** ad hoc (navigation completeness pass, user request: "link every page and function to
each other") · **Status:** done for the confirmed, in-scope findings; two structural gaps found
and deliberately deferred rather than fixed blind (see Next)

### Did
Ran this as a two-phase workflow rather than guessing at scope: a 7-agent discovery pass audited
every module in the app (Rentals, Clients, Inventory, Operations, Finance/Reports,
Notifications/Admin/System, Today/Calendar/Documents — all ~50 routes, every file behind each
one) for two specific patterns: an entity name/ID (client, booking, asset) shown as inert text
where that entity's own page exists, and a button whose label promises navigation but has no
handler. Findings came back structured (file, exact location, current text, target route,
confidence) — 37 candidates total.

Triaged before fixing: fixed every high/medium-confidence finding where the target route
genuinely exists and the needed id/param was already in scope (20 fix groups); explicitly

(logged as background tasks, not silently done or silently dropped — see Next). A second

## 2026-08-09 — Phase 1: first reviewed batch of the 92-table RLS gap (4 tables), rest categorised
**Phase:** 1 (schema) · **Status:** partial — see PLAN.md §6.10 for the full still-open list

### Did
Continued the RLS-gap work from the prior Phase 1 entry (§6.9: 111 tables have RLS enabled, only
19 had a real policy — 92 fail-closed). That entry deliberately stopped short of writing any of
the 92 policies, recommending "categorize by domain/sensitivity first, then write in reviewed
batches." This entry does the categorization and the first batch.

Re-derived the 92 independently rather than trust the prior count: a plain-text grep for
`create policy ... on <table>` undercounts, because two policies in `0014` are generated inside
`execute format(...)` loops over a Postgres array variable, not literal text. Resolved both loops
against their actual array contents (`['vehicle_trips', 'trips', 'booking_transport']` — only
`booking_transport` is real; `['invoices', 'payments', 'security_deposits', 'deposit_movements',
'expenses']` — all five real) and discounted `0014`'s dead `maintenance_tickets` conditional
(that table doesn't exist). Result: 19 tables with real coverage, 111 real tables total — both
match §6.9's numbers, confirmed independently instead of carried forward on trust.

Ran an automated first-pass sweep (column names matching `_amount`/`_price`/`_rate`/`_cost`/
`_value`/`_fee`, typed `numeric`/`bigint`/`integer`) across the 92 to split money-adjacent from
plain tables, then manually corrected two the sweep got wrong: `number_sequences` (flagged MONEY
by the sweep on `current_value bigint`, but it's a document-numbering counter, not money — moved
to "plain") and `user_approval_authorities` (NOT flagged — its `max_amount_limit`/
`max_discount_pct` columns don't match the sweep's suffix list, but are money-adjacent by any
real reading — moved to "money"). Also flagged `bank_accounts` as sensitive by content (holds the
business's own `account_number`) despite having no money-amount column the sweep could catch.

Wrote `supabase/migrations/0022_branch_zone_role_lookup_policies.sql`, covering 4 of the 5 tables
§6.9 named as highest-leverage (they're what any future branch/zone/approval row-scoping policy
would itself need to read): `branches`/`warehouses`/`storage_zones` get `auth_is_staff()` SELECT
(pure reference data every internal role needs) and `('Owner', 'Admin', 'Manager')` for structural
writes — the same tier `audit_settings` (0018) already uses, not invented here. `user_roles` gets
that same tier for **both** read and write, since it's access-control metadata (who holds which
role), not operational reference data, so it doesn't get the other three's broad staff-read.
Confirmed `user_roles` isn't what `auth_user_role()` itself reads (that function reads
`users.primary_role` directly) — no auth-bootstrapping risk from gating it, unlike `users` in
`0020`. The fifth table §6.9 named, `user_approval_authorities`, is deliberately **not** included
— its money columns put it in the masking-review bucket, not this one.

  assumed — consistent with this thread's established practice after the `inventory_units`/

HIS v2.1's gating tables list Owner/Admin/Manager/Accounts as four distinct roles. The
business-8 ruling (0013, 8 Aug) had folded Manager into Admin by renaming the enum label in
place. Reopened on explicit user instruction, additively rather than by editing Admin's
meaning: `0017_reopen_manager_role.sql` adds a genuine new `'Manager'` enum value (the old
label was consumed by 0013's rename, not preserved), `0018_manager_role_policies.sql`
restates the ~20 policies/helpers that used to say `Manager` pre-0013 (now reading `Admin`)
to include `Manager` alongside `Admin` everywhere, since HIS v2.1 states no rule where the
two diverge. `SystemRole` (`types/database.ts`), `rbac.ts`, `data/nav.ts`'s
`BOTTOM_BAR_ROUTES`, and the two exhaustive `ROLES` arrays (`Settings.tsx`,
`CasesQueue.tsx`) all updated — `noUnusedLocals`/exhaustive `Record<SystemRole,...>` caught
every call site that needed it. **Migrations are new files only, not applied to any
Supabase project** (CLAUDE.md's hard rule) — mechanically correct on read, unverified
against a live database.

### Built: a reusable Glance/Detail card, not another one-off
No reusable hover-card component existed — the only prior one (`MovementList.tsx`'s
`HoverCard`) is entity-specific, has no `onFocus` handling despite this file previously
claiming otherwise, and doesn't check `useCapability().hasHover` at all. `Unavailable.tsx`
turned out to be the app's one genuinely correct capability-aware pattern (hover / focus /
long-press, gated on `hasHover`, with the touch-emits-a-click suppression SCREENS.md logs as
a real defect class). `components/ui/IntelCard.tsx` generalizes that pattern: a Glance

**Phase:** cross-cutting fix · **Status:** done

### Did
- Both `NewRental.tsx`'s §5.2 summary bar and `BookingDetail.tsx`'s Facts strip used the
  same hardcoded `gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(4, minmax(0,1fr)) minmax(0,1.1fr)'` with no

  and deliberately not fixed inline there since the pattern is shared with `BookingDetail.tsx`.
  At phone width every field's value (`whiteSpace: nowrap` + ellipsis) truncated to a few
  characters — including the Client name and the Outstanding figure, the page's most
  important number.
- Added `useViewport()` (Law 14) to both files. Grid now branches: desktop unchanged
  (5 unequal columns), tablet collapses to `repeat(2, minmax(0,1fr))`, phone collapses to a
  single stacked column (`1fr`). The Outstanding block spans the full row
  (`gridColumn: '1 / -1'`) on both non-desktop tiers instead of sitting orphaned in one
  column. Divider style switches from `borderRight` (desktop) to `borderBottom`
  (phone/tablet). In `BookingDetail.tsx` the `Fact` sub-component now takes a `viewport` prop
  to make the same divider switch, since it renders three of the five strip cells.

### Verified
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean, no errors, from a fresh full run (not the transient
  `summaryCols`/`summaryDivider` "unused variable" state a concurrent session caught
  mid-edit in the entry below — that was this change still in progress, not a real bug).
- Drove both pages live (own dev server on a separate port, since another session already
  had one running on 5173 — connected to that one directly to avoid the 5-dev-server-per-folder
  cap). Confirmed via computed styles at three widths on both pages:
  - Phone tier (window inner-width in the 570s under this environment's mobile emulation,
    still `< 768` so `useViewport()` correctly reads `'phone'`): grid is a single
    ~333px column, Outstanding spans it, **zero elements with `scrollWidth > clientWidth`**
    among all `nowrap`+`ellipsis` fields (Client "Himalayan Films Pvt. Ltd." and Outstanding
    "Rs 1,19,069"/"Rs 1,24,506" render in full).
  - Tablet tier (900px): 2 equal ~314px columns, Outstanding spans both, zero truncation.
  - Desktop tier (1280px): unchanged 5-column asymmetric grid
    (`197.6px × 4 + 217.4px`), Outstanding back to `gridColumn: auto` with its original
    right-side border radius — confirms no regression above the breakpoint.

### Found
- This environment's mobile viewport emulation (375×812 preset) reports
  `window.innerWidth` around 571–579, not 375 — the app has no `<meta name="viewport">`
  forcing `width=device-width`, so Chrome's mobile emulation falls back to a wider virtual
  layout viewport that's then scaled to fit. Harmless for this fix since 571 is still
  `< 768` and lands in the same `'phone'` bucket, but worth knowing before trusting a raw
  `window.innerWidth` reading at the 375 preset for anything closer to the 768 boundary.

## 2026-08-09 — Forward-only stage-transition trigger built; found the RLS gap is systemic
(92 of 111 tables have zero policy), not just the few named in the prior entry
**Phase:** 1 (schema) · **Status:** partial — see PLAN.md §6.9 for the full still-open list

### Did
Continued from the prior entry ("next" after the foundational-bug/typo fixes). Implemented the
"forward-only stages" item from the Phase 1 checklist in
`supabase/migrations/0021_forward_only_stage_transitions.sql`: an AFTER INSERT trigger on
`booking_stage_transitions` (`security definer`, same precedent as `log_audit_event()`) that
validates from_stage matches the booking's real current stage, forward-only/no-skip unless an
already-CHECK-enforced approved reversal, causal order against the booking's prior transition,
and that a Closed booking accepts nothing further — then writes `bookings.stage`/`closed_at`
itself. Revoked direct `UPDATE (stage, closed_at)` on `bookings` from `authenticated`, so this
trigger is the only path — making `bookings.stage`'s own column comment ("Written ONLY by that
table's trigger; a direct UPDATE is rejected") true instead of aspirational for the first time.
Deliberately scoped to just the checklist's "forward-only stages" + "causal order" items, not the
other four `0002`-commented `TRIGGER REQUIRED` items on this table (inventory release on cancel,
the full Confirm-transaction bundle, the Critical-condition gate) — those need real Phase 3
engine logic this migration has no business inventing; see `0021`'s header for the exact line.

**Caught before shipping, not after:** `booking_stage_transitions` itself had RLS enabled with
zero policies — the trigger's own dependency would have been unreachable, freezing every
booking's stage at Quote forever. Added an INSERT policy (same five roles `bookings_update`
already allows, actor_id pinned to the session) and a SELECT policy (`auth_is_staff()`) in the
same migration before calling it done.

**That near-miss is what prompted the bigger check.** Diffed every `enable row level security`
statement against every `create policy` statement across all 21 migration files: **111 tables
have RLS enabled; 19 have ever had a policy. 92 — the large majority of the schema — are
fail-closed with no policy at all**, including `branches`, `warehouses`, `crew_members`,
`vehicles`, `expenses`, `suppliers`, every `booking_*` line/flag table, and the entire
client-portal auth path (`portal_users`/`portal_auth_challenges`/`portal_sessions`). This is
larger and more basic than the "branch/zone/approval dimension is missing" gap named in the prior
entry — those tables at least have a role-only policy to extend; these have nothing.

### Verified
- `next_booking_stage()`'s case map checked against `0015`'s actual canonical six-stage
  declaration order (Quote → Booked → Packed → On Rent → Returned → Closed), not assumed.
- Traced the interaction between this trigger and the `validate_booking_gates()` fix from the
  prior entry by reading both function bodies together: the new trigger's own `UPDATE bookings`
  still fires `bookings`' existing BEFORE UPDATE trigger exactly as a direct client UPDATE would,
  so a gate failure still rolls back the whole transition (the inserted `booking_stage_
  transitions` row included) rather than silently succeeding.
- The 92-table gap count is a mechanical diff (`comm` between two sorted greps), re-run once to
  confirm the count before writing it down.
- **Not verified by execution** — same as prior entries, nothing applied to any live project.

### Explicitly still open
The 92-table RLS gap is **deliberately not attempted** — writing real policies for 92 tables
needs per-table judgment (role set, row-scoping, money-column masking, and `portal_*`'s auth path
is likely not `system_role`-based at all), not a rushed same-session pass. See PLAN.md §6.9 for
the full remaining list (this gap now first, ahead of the branch/zone/approval dimension work,

## 2026-08-09 — Phase 1 follow-up audit: a foundational RLS bug, two migration-breaking typos,
one file-numbering collision with the concurrent session — all fixed (local files only)
**Phase:** 1 (schema) · **Status:** partial — see PLAN.md §6.8 for the full still-open list

### Did
Continued straight from the prior entry's Phase 1 audit (user: "Continue Phase 1 schema gaps").
Dispatched a 4-agent research workflow — full re-read of every policy in `0011`
(not a sample: 32 found, not the ~22 both `0014`'s and my own prior `0017`'s comments
estimated), the `0015` stage-transition trigger claim, the `invoices` money columns and their
write paths, and what branch/warehouse/approval-limit infrastructure already exists — then
verified the two most consequential findings directly myself before touching anything:

1. **`auth_user_role()` (the function every single RLS policy in this schema calls) cannot
   actually read `users`.** It's `language sql stable`, not `security definer`, so its internal
   `select primary_role from users where id = ...` runs as the calling role — and `users` has
   RLS enabled with zero policies anywhere in `0001`-`0019` (confirmed by exhaustive grep, not
   inference). Postgres returns zero rows, not an error, so the function's `coalesce()` falls
   through to `'Client'` for every user, Owner included. Since `'Client'` is correctly excluded
   from every staff allow-list elsewhere, this means **every role-gated policy in the entire
   database would have denied everyone**, the moment any of this was applied to a live project —
   a total, silent outage, not a leak. Ironically the only policies that would have worked are
   the exact `using (true)` ones this session has been trying to close.
2. Confirmed two migration-breaking typos the research agents flagged: `0010`'s audit trigger
   and three of `0011`'s policies targeted a table called `inventory_units`, which has never
   existed (`product_units` is the real table — grep confirms no rename statement, so this is an
   unpropagated drafting-time rename); and `validate_booking_gates()` (`0010`) branched on
   `NEW.stage_number`/`OLD.stage_number`, a column from the retired 13-stage model that was
   never a real column in this schema. Both would have aborted migration application outright —
   the first at `0010`, before any of the money-relevant policy fixes in `0011` even ran.

Fixed all three directly at their source (`0010`, `0011`, `0018` — none of these have ever been
applied anywhere, so editing in place is cleaner than patching around them):
- `0010`: renamed the audit trigger's target `inventory_units` → `product_units`; rewrote
  `validate_booking_gates()` to branch on `bookings.stage`'s real enum values (old Stage
  6/Handover → `'On Rent'`, old Stage 10/Closed → `'Closed'`, using the same ordinal-comparison
  idiom `0015` already established) — gate logic itself unchanged, only the broken column ref.
- `0011` and `0018`: renamed all five remaining `inventory_units_*` policy statements to target
  `product_units`.
- New `supabase/migrations/0020_role_lookup_and_staff_retrofit.sql`: adds `users_select_own`
  (a session may read its own row — the minimum fix for the foundational bug, deliberately not
  a broad "staff can list all users" grant, which is a separate, later decision) and retrofits
  the four remaining `using (true)` SELECT policies (`bookings_select`,
  `maintenance_records_select`, `operation_sessions_select`, `clients_select`) to
  `auth_is_staff()`.

Also found and resolved a **file-numbering collision**: the concurrent session's own
`0017_reopen_manager_role.sql` / `0018_manager_role_policies.sql` (reopening Manager as its own
role, separate from Admin) landed on the same `0017` I'd used for the prior entry's money-masking
migration. Renamed mine to `0019_column_level_money_masking.sql` rather than touch their two
files, and updated its header — the `product_units` gap it described as "zero policies" was
actually the `inventory_units` typo above, not a true gap; corrected for accuracy.

### Verified
- Every renamed table/column reference re-checked against an actual `grep`/`create table`
  confirmation, not memory: `product_units` exists (`0004`), `inventory_units` does not and has
  no rename statement anywhere; `bookings.stage_number` does not exist anywhere outside the two
  buggy lines; `maintenance_records` confirmed real (`0004:433`) before writing a policy against
  it, precisely because `inventory_units` turning out to be phantom raised the bar for trusting
  a table name without checking.
- **Not verified by execution** — same as the prior entry, no local Postgres instance available
  and nothing applied to either Supabase project, per CLAUDE.md's hard rule.

### Explicitly still open
See PLAN.md §6.8 for the full current list (branch/warehouse-zone/approval-limit RLS still
entirely missing — and now known to be blocked by the *same* zero-policy pattern as the `users`
bug, on `branches`/`warehouses`/`storage_zones`/`user_roles`/`user_approval_authorities`; the
forward-only stage-transition trigger still doesn't exist; the invoices integrity trigger needs
a formula decision first, since the two existing triggers that write `outstanding_amount`
disagree on flooring and neither accounts for `payment_reversals`; 21 of 32 policies in `0011`
still not retrofitted).

not just theoretically at risk — `ClientReports.tsx`, `ProductReports.tsx`, `CasesWorkspace.tsx`,
`CrewBooking.tsx`, and `SubRental.tsx` all render real money (revenue, outstanding, payroll,
sub-rental cost/margin) with zero `canViewMoney` gate, to every role including Client. **Two
migrations cannot deploy as written**: `0009_crew_vehicles.sql` redefines `crew_members` (already

dangling foreign keys to tables (`assets`, `documents`, `cases`, `charges`) that don't exist
anywhere in the schema — which would also silently prevent every trigger in `0010` and every RLS
policy in `0011` from ever being created. **Invoice immutability is stated but unenforced** —
`0006_finance.sql`'s header promises Void+Credit-Note-only, but `invoices` was never added to the
REVOKE UPDATE list. **The discount law has two DB-level gaps**: invoices can carry a >10% discount
with no required reason/approver, and stacked sub-10% discount rows can exceed the 25%/10%
caps in aggregate since only a per-row check exists. Plus ~10 dead-navigation/orphaned-screen
bugs (Command Palette, Operations Queues' Pack job, Stock Check, Purchase Requests, Add
Equipment) and a shift-handover logout that never actually logs out.

## 2026-08-09 — Phase 1 schema audit: one live Law-6 violation found and fixed (local file only)
**Phase:** 1 (schema) · **Status:** partial — one migration written, four related gaps still open

### Did
User chose "Start Phase 1 — schema" at a fork once Phase 6 polish work ran out of queued items.
Read all 16 existing migrations against PLAN.md's own Phase 1 checklist and gate ("no path lets
Warehouse read a money column"), starting with a 5-agent audit workflow, then direct reads of
`0011`, `0013`, `0014`, `0002` (`booking_lines`), `0004` (`products`, `product_units`) to confirm
findings against actual column lists rather than the audit's summary.

Found the gate was not just unverified but actively violated:
- `booking_lines_select` (`0011_rls_policies.sql:137`) was `using (true)` — no role check.
  `booking_lines` carries `rate`, `discount_amount`, `supplier_cost`, `markup_amount`; every
  money-blind floor role (Warehouse, Technician, Driver) could read all four today.
- `products` and `product_units` (`0004_inventory.sql`) have RLS enabled but had **zero policies**
  anywhere in `0001`–`0016` (confirmed by `grep -rn "products_select\|product_units_select\|on
  products\b\|on product_units\b"` — only index-creation lines matched). Fail-closed, so safe but
  functionally broken: nobody, including Owner, could read the fleet catalogue at all.

Wrote `supabase/migrations/0017_column_level_money_masking.sql`:
- New `products_select` / `product_units_select` policies using the already-defined-but-unwired
  `auth_is_staff()` (`0014`) — the first real caller of that function.
- Replaced `booking_lines_select`'s `using (true)` with `using (auth_is_staff())`.
- `revoke select (<money columns>) on <table> from authenticated` on all three base tables, plus
  three new masking views (`products_v`, `product_units_v`, `booking_lines_v`) that return the
  real value only `when auth_can_view_money()` (`0014`, already in force) and `null` otherwise —
  the standard Postgres/Supabase view-owner-privilege masking idiom, not a new mechanism.
- File header documents the reasoning (why a view and not a row policy — these three tables mix
  money and operational columns in the same row) and explicitly lists what it does **not** cover.
- Updated `PLAN.md` §6.7 (new) with the full finding and the still-open items; left the Phase 1
  checklist's "Column-level money hiding" line unchecked with a "partial, see §6.7" note rather
  than checking it — three tables covered, several more (`invoice_lines` etc.) are not.

### Verified
- Every column name in the three new views checked against the actual `create table` statements
  in `0004_inventory.sql` and `0002_bookings.sql` (re-read in full after writing the migration,
  not trusted from memory) — all names match exactly, no typos.
- `auth_is_staff()` and `auth_can_view_money()` signatures re-confirmed against `0014` (both
  `returns boolean`, zero arguments) — the calls in `0017` match.
- **Not** verified by execution — no local Postgres instance was available and, per CLAUDE.md's
  hard rule and the user's own framing when choosing this task ("I'd stop and ask before applying
  any migration"), this was **not applied to either Supabase project** on the account. This is a

  in any of `0001`–`0017`.
- No forward-only booking-stage-transition trigger exists, despite `0015`'s own column comment
  claiming one does.

## 2026-08-09 — Operations Popup Shell: adversarial-review fix pass
**Phase:** 4.6 (Operations Popup Shell, mock-data build) · **Status:** done — every
adversarially-confirmed finding from the review workflow is fixed; two structural gaps the review
also flagged (open decision, seed data can't reach every state) are disclosed below, not hidden.

### Did
The shell (`OperationsShell.tsx` + 4 step panels + `EvidencePanel.tsx`, built earlier this
session on mock data per the user's own "build the shell UI now" call) went through an
adversarial multi-dimension `Workflow` review. The workflow hit a session usage limit mid-run
(26 of 31 agents failed with "session limit"), so most raw findings were never independently
re-verified by a second agent — recovered the full candidate list from the run's `journal.jsonl`
directly and self-verified each by reading the flagged code myself before fixing, rather than
shipping either an unverified fix or no fix. Fixed, file by file:
- **`HandoverStep.tsx`** — the single largest write-gate gap: 5 of 7 write controls (Outbound
  evidence, Edit-locked toggle, correction-qty/-reason inputs, Submit-correction) had no
  `disabled={readOnly}` at all, meaning a viewer at a blocked stage could still submit a
  correction. Gated all 5. Also: the correction-qty `<input type="number" min={0}>` never
  actually blocked negative/decimal input (`min` only affects the native stepper, not typed
  characters) — combined with `effectiveDispatchedQty`'s `/^(\d+)/` regex silently falling back
  to the stale value on a negative string, a bad correction could look like it saved while being
  a no-op. Added an explicit `Number.isInteger(n) && n >= 0` gate on the Submit button instead of
  touching the regex, since the UI is the only caller.
- **`ReturnStep.tsx`** — count-tracked outstanding lines always received the *full* expected
  quantity; there was no control to enter less, so `receiveReturn`'s own "Missing" (partial
  return) state was unreachable through the built UI for anything but serial items. Added a
  per-line qty input (0..expected, integer-validated) that feeds the real quantity through. Added
  an "Inbound evidence" button + `<EvidencePanel direction="in">` — previously the only evidence
  entry point anywhere in the shell was Handover's outbound one.
- **`EvidencePanel.tsx`** — added a `readOnly` prop gating "Add a condition photo" (had none).
  Its own Escape handling was a separate concern in the review; left unfixed here on purpose —
  `evidenceOpen` is now lifted to `OperationsShell`, whose window-level handler already checks it
  before closing the whole shell, so a second local handler would just race the first.
- **`PackingStep.tsx`** — the substitute-serial input and "Confirm substitution" button were the
  one inconsistency in an otherwise fully-gated file; added `disabled={readOnly}`.
- **`BookingDetail.tsx`** — `OperationsLauncher`'s progress subtitle read the frozen module-level
  `SEED_ITEMS` constant, which the shell's own state never touches — it was permanently stuck at
  "0/8" regardless of what was actually packed. Wired `OperationsShell`'s `onProgressChange`
  callback into local state instead. Separately, the disabled-reason `title` attribute on the
  launcher was inert for keyboard/touch (native `disabled` removes an element from the tab order,
  and `title` never fires on touch) — replaced with the shared `Unavailable` component another
  concurrent session had already centralized this same session for exactly this pattern.
- **`ResetStep.tsx`** — its checklist state was a local `useState`, lost every time another rail
  tab was selected (`{step === 'Reset' && <ResetStep .../>}` unmounts it). Lifted `resetDone` to
  `OperationsShell` beside `items`/`corrections`. Also fixed `progressFor('Reset')`, which had
  been measuring `returnState === 'Returned'` — the rail dot could show "done" the instant Return
  finished, before a single checklist box was ticked; now measures `resetDone` against the
  returned set.
- Lower-priority a11y sweep, folded in while already in these files: `aria-expanded` added to the
  two inline-disclosure toggles (Edit-locked, Substitute); touch targets bumped to 44×44 across
  `PackingStep`/`ReturnStep`/`HandoverStep`/`EvidencePanel` controls that were sitting at 30–34px.

### Verified
`npx tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors, run twice (once after the core fixes, again after the touch-target
pass). Live in the browser against `BK-2026-0715` (status `Booked`):
- Packed all 8 seed items, including one real substitution (DJI RS3 Gimbal → `RS4-0042`) — the
  launcher subtitle updated live at every step, `Operations · Packing 0/8` → `1/8` → ... → `8/8`,
  confirmed via the actual rendered button text, not an assumption.
- Typed `SN102` into the scan field character-by-character (via real per-keystroke `type`, not
  programmatic value-setting — the exact gap that let the original digit-hijack bug through my
  own testing last time) and confirmed the step rail did **not** jump on the embedded `1`/`0`/`2`
  digits, and the field held `"SN102"` intact afterward.
- Switched to Handover and Return tabs (both correctly still-blocked at `Booked` status) and
  read every button/input's `disabled` state directly from the DOM: signer-name input, Sign
  button, Outbound-evidence button, all 4 condition buttons × 8 outstanding lines, all 4 qty
  inputs, and Inbound-evidence — every one `disabled: true`, with the inline blocked-reason
  banner present and `role="alert"`.
- Reset tab rendered "Still with the client (8)" with no console error, confirming the lifted
  `resetDone` state doesn't break the panel when nothing has returned yet.

**Not verified live, disclosed rather than assumed:** the write-*enabled* paths of Handover,
Return, and Reset (submitting a correction, receiving a partial return, ticking a reset checkbox)

ship those as unverified, I personally re-checked all four by direct file read/grep after the

inconsistent.

### Found
Full table with impact/fix/severity is in `AUDIT_FINDINGS.md`. Highlights: **P0** — Pulse's
"Net cash" figure includes refundable client deposits (Law 5 violation, visible to the Owner on
the business-at-a-glance dashboard). **P0** — New Rental computes VAT/pricing locally instead of
through the Financial Engine, so a Settings VAT change silently stops applying to new bookings
made from this screen. **P1** — a not-yet-applied migration trigger (`validate_booking_gates`)
references a `stage_number` column that was never added to the schema, which would make every
`UPDATE` to `bookings` error out the moment migrations are ever applied live. **P1** —
`bookingQuery.ts` (the Single-Query-Rule engine) and the hand-authored `database.ts` types don't

**Phase:** build-every-page · **Status:** partial

### Found and fixed — the important one
- **Reports ▸ Pulse, Foundation's designated "owner's business view," was printing a fabricated
  P&L.** A headline of ~Rs 59.6L revenue / ~Rs 39.1L profit (a ~66% net margin nobody supplied)
  came from wholly invented business ratios (`SERVICES_RATIO`, `EXPENSE_FIXED`,
  `COLLECT_SAME_DAY`, etc.), and its Top Equipment panel showed several models at 100%
  utilization against fleet unit counts that **contradicted `data/inventory.ts`'s own seed on
  the same screen** — exactly the "Reports must not be the system's fifth opinion" defect
  `pulse.ts`'s own header claims to prevent, except `RECONCILIATION` never actually checked the
  fleet.

    "Ronin 4D 6K" at 3 units → the real model at 2), both now matching `inventory.ts` exactly.

    day rate). Picking a number would be a different fabrication, not a fix — `TODO(decision)`,
    tied to `GUIDE/OPEN-DECISIONS.md` item 5 (data import).

    banner between the header and the first figure, so an owner reading this page cannot
    mistake a placeholder shape for a real number.

  `if (!money) return`, crashing the app — "Rendered fewer hooks than expected" — whenever the
  session's money-visibility flipped while the component stayed mounted), and **a hardcoded
  25% discount-approval ceiling was applied to every line regardless of that line's actual
  discount %**, wrongly denying Admins approval on discounts their own role should clear.

### Verified

  `theme.css`-custom-property system (matching `cardStyle`, `STATUS` tokens, `Icon`,
  `Button` from `Page.tsx`), preserving every existing prop shape exactly so none of the 32
  `EmptyState` call sites needed to change. Dropped the dead duplicate `OfflineBanner` export

  Added a `pulse` keyframe to `theme.css` for the new `LoadingSkeleton`, and a `lock` icon to

  `Shell`, which every route passes through:

    §2.1's "never a bare spinner, never a blank container." Replaced with
    `<LoadingSkeleton type="card" label="Loading…" />`.

    render-time crash anywhere in the tree.** `main.tsx` only guards the §2.8 reference-case

    </Suspense>` specifically (not the whole Shell), so Sidebar/Header/BottomBar stay usable
    and a user can navigate away even if one page's render throws. Shows `ErrorBanner` with a
    reload-triggered retry.

    `RestrictedState` instead of a hand-rolled `<h1>`/`<p>` pair — same message, on-system
    styling.

  `Bundles.tsx`, `Maintenance.tsx`, `Inventory.tsx`, `Warehouses.tsx`, `RentalsList.tsx`,
  `Documents.tsx`, `NumberingSequences.tsx` (this last one had a `block` display-mode prop
  the shared component doesn't carry — replaced its two call sites, not the one originally

  and `CommunicationSettings.tsx` (brand-new files another concurrent session is actively
  building — a "not built yet" badge with no `children` prop, also a different shape); the
  remaining ~560 scattered raw `title=` attributes elsewhere in the app that aren't this
  specific pattern — a much larger, lower-value tail not attempted here.

### Verified
- `npx tsc --noEmit` filtered to `Unavailable.tsx` and all 11 migrated files: 0 errors.
- Drove the app at desktop width: every migrated screen's disabled controls still carry the
  correct `title` attribute with the exact reason text (checked via `document.querySelectorAll
  ('[title]')` on the Clients directory — 14 matching spans, each `aria-disabled="true"` with
  its reason as both `title` and `aria-label`) — the hover path is confirmed unchanged.
- **Not dynamically confirmed: the long-press timer path itself.** Emulated a touch/coarse
  device (`resize_window` mobile preset — confirmed `hasHover` false and `title` correctly
  omitted in that mode) and tried to trigger the 500ms long-press via synthetic `TouchEvent`/
  `Touch` objects and via `.focus()`; the popover never appeared. Isolated this as an
  environment limitation, not a confirmed defect: native `addEventListener('touchstart', …)`
  on a throwaway element fires from the same synthetic dispatch, plain `setTimeout` fires
  correctly in this backgrounded tab, and React's own synthetic `onClick` does fire from a
  dispatched `MouseEvent` on a real button in this app — but React's synthetic touch/focus
  handling specifically did not visibly respond to script-dispatched (untrusted) events here,
  and the `computer` tool's real-input path (which the mobile preset's own mouse-to-touch
  translation would make reliable) timed out because this session's Browser pane is not
  visually composited (the same limitation documented earlier this session for screenshots).
  The component's logic was reviewed by hand and matches a standard, low-risk React long-press
  pattern (`setTimeout` in an event handler calling `setState`); it should be spot-checked on

var(--nav-active-accent)` + `color: #fff`. In dark theme `--nav-active-accent` is the brand
gold (`#d8a93a`), and white-on-gold measures **2.17:1** — under WCAG AA's 3:1 floor for
bold/large text, the same class of bug `theme.css` documents already fixing once for
`--progress`'s amber. Fixed by switching to `--btn-primary-bg` / `--btn-primary-fg`, the pair
`Button` already resolves correctly per theme (black-on-gold in dark, 9.66:1; white-on-blue
in light, 5.17:1) — reused an existing correct token pair instead of inventing a new one.

  `useViewport() === 'phone'`, replacing the Sidebar entirely at that width rather than
  squeezing an icon rail in alongside it. Shows the first 3 `permittedNav()` items plus
  `Settings` as a fixed 4th slot (Settings sits outside the permission-filtered NAV array by
  design, and needed a way to stay reachable once the Sidebar — which normally carries it —
  is hidden).

  locks this: "Scanner — a FAB at every width (§5.5), never a nav item." The existing

  forbid.

  bottom padding grows by `BOTTOM_BAR_HEIGHT` on phone so page content isn't hidden behind
  the fixed bar.

## 2026-08-06 — Complete Phase 1 Database Schema Migrations (0001–0012)
**Phase:** 1 · **Status:** done

### Did
- **Completed full production PostgreSQL schema migrations (0001 through 0012) under `supabase/migrations/`:**
  - `0001_enums.sql`: 290 canonical lifecycle and domain enums with forward-only order.
  - `0002_bookings.sql`: Bookings, booking lines, discount approvals, and 12-stage state machine constraints.
  - `0003_operations.sql`: Operations sessions, packing/handover/return lines, checklists, and signatures.
  - `0004_inventory.sql`: 17 tables for product tracking (serialised, quantity, consumable), units, containers, accessories, bundles, sub-rentals, and maintenance.
  - `0005_clients.sql`: Client profiles (organisations & individuals), contacts, credit overrides, documents, and marketing consents.
  - `0006_finance.sql`: Invoices, line items (mandatory `days`), immutable `payments`, `payment_reversals`, isolated `security_deposits`, `deposit_movements`, `expenses`, `expense_reversals`, `coupons`, and `tax_ledgers`.
  - `0007_admin_security.sql`: Branches, warehouses, storage zones, users, 6 canonical RBAC roles (`Owner`, `Manager`, `Warehouse`, `Billing`, `Accounts`, `Viewer`), shifts, timesheets, immutable `audit_events`, backup logs, system settings, and atomic `number_sequences`.
  - `0008_automation_comms.sql`: Notification templates, notifications, delivery logs, broadcast batches, automation rules, SMS gateways, and webhooks.
  - `0009_crew_vehicles.sql`: Crew members, skills, assignments, fleet vehicles, trip logs, fuel logs, central `document_registry`, and deliveries.
  - `0010_triggers_functions.sql`: Universal audit trigger, pricing engine auto-recalculation (Subtotal -> Discount -> Taxable -> VAT 13% -> Total -> Outstanding), security deposit balance auto-sync, payment receipt sync, and handover/closure gate validation triggers.
  - `0011_rls_policies.sql`: Row Level Security policies enforcing RBAC roles and zero monetary visibility for Warehouse role.
  - `0012_seed_data.sql`: Seed data for branches (Kathmandu HQ & Pokhara), warehouses, initial users, Nepali fiscal year (`FY 2083/84`), bank accounts, expense categories, and equipment categories.

### Verified
- Enforced all 10 core architectural laws in SQL:
  1. No hard `DELETE` allowed — `REVOKE DELETE` applied to every table; terminal states are state changes.
  2. Every user-written table carries `client_uuid uuid not null unique` for idempotency.
  3. Payments and Audit Logs are strictly immutable with `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE`.
  4. Deposits are isolated as separate liability balances from invoices and rental revenue.
  5. Pricing engine enforces mandatory `days >= 1`, 25% hard discount cap, and half-up rounding.
  6. All 12 migrations syntactically structured in transactional blocks (`begin; ... commit;`) with explicit foreign key indexing and composite checks.

### Found
- Audit log triggers and pricing recalculation triggers eliminate any frontend state-drift risks.
- Warehouse staff role is barred from selecting monetary columns and invoice ledgers via RLS.

    List also used "Returning" and "Overdue", neither of which is a stage.

    *cannot* render an invented status. Verified in the browser — every status pill on
    every built screen resolves to a valid stage.

Fifteen renders sampled; every one lands in Reports, Finance, Administration, Automation
or Communication. **None** covers Operations Queues, Calendar, Inventory, Finance
dashboard or Documents — exactly the sections still empty. Those are now being built from

issue in the product.** `Calendar.md` §4.2 records three conflicting BS offsets across
pages; Today had one of them — `TODAY_DATE` read *17 Shrawan* for 31 Jul 2026, where the
correct anchor (16 Jul = 1 Shrawan) makes it the **16th**. A Nepali client reading a
delivery date one day out is the first thing anyone notices. `lib/bs.ts` is now the one
Date Engine and nothing hand-writes a BS date; verified in the browser that the date pill,
the mini-calendar and the Calendar columns all agree.

layouts so far (8 in Foundation §5.1, 13, 15, 16, and a 17-item variant with a duplicated

Every sidebar link was `<a href>` + `preventDefault()`, so **no nav click navigated**. The
browser sweeps had driven routes with `history.pushState`, which bypasses click handlers,
so 21 routes were confirmed "working" without a single link ever being clicked. Replaced
with router `<Link>`s and re-verified by **clicking** all 15 sections and all 21 children.
Lesson for later phases: exercise the control, not the route.

the Rentals table are now real links to Booking Detail; the `New Rental` buttons on Today
and Rentals now open the new booking workspace.

sections are not a wizard"; §0 lists "'Previous' implying a wizard" as a corrected defect).
Rebuilt as the **Booking Workspace**: five collapsible sections in any order, one Confirm,
no Previous. Verified: 5 sections, 1 Confirm button, no Back/Next in the DOM.

Money is derived, never typed, following §10.1's calculation order with half-up rounding at
each displayed step. §9.2 (Customer Pickup forces transport to zero), §10.3 (deposits never

(unset values render "—", never zero) and §12 (Critical blocks Confirm, Warning blocks
Handover) are enforced, not described.

alert · a short reason still blocks · a long reason without an approver still blocks · both
present clears it. No bypass, including Owner.

`Packing Workflow.md` v2.1 §0 lists eight defects in the reference screenshots, so the

**§10 completion gate verified through all four states:** bulk scan leaves 1 required item

clears it. Row actions had to be added for this: without them a Required line blocked by

### The reference figures were wrong — corrected to §10.2
Three sources disagreed about BK-2026-0715. The render's numbers are impossible
(1,39,505 − 15,000 ≠ 93,548) and Foundation §02's discount is labelled 7% but is 7.2%
(9,558 of 1,32,750). Booking Workflow §10.2 is the only internally consistent set and says

1,39,506 · 1,24,506.

### A verification race, found and fixed
A contrast sweep reported ~400 failures across pages that had passed minutes earlier. The
cause was my own harness: it scanned during the 200 ms theme transition, so it measured
dark text against a still-light body. Sampling at 50 ms after a toggle shows exactly that —
`data-theme` already flipped, background not yet repainted. The sweep now **polls until the
painted body background equals the theme's `--app`** before measuring. Re-run clean.

## 2026-08-05 — Whole-app design (14 agents); two dead purple tokens removed

**Phase:** 1 · **Status:** design delivered, not yet acted on — see the three fixes below

Ran the biggest workflow yet: 10 parallel readers across all 17 spec sections → three
synthesis passes (screen inventory/IA, component/engine architecture, build order) → one
adversarial challenge of the whole thing. ~2.5M tokens, 347 tool calls, ~64 minutes. The
result is roughly 200K characters and is saved to the scratchpad rather than pasted whole;
citations below are pulled from it.

**The challenge is unusually sharp and mostly correct.** It found, among ~40 findings ranked
by cost: §12's seven business-gap specs (Rate Cards, Security Held, Vehicles & Trips, Direct
Transfer, Consumables & Media, Quote Lifecycle & Agreement Versions, Write-off & Disposal)
missing from a 149-row screen inventory that claimed to be exhaustive — five of them have no
document anywhere in the library except the sentence in Foundation that scopes them; the
whole EN/NE localization layer (§3.5, §4.3.5) absent from all three parts; a Foundation quote
truncated mid-sentence then a module cited against the truncation it produced; money still
appearing on Warehouse-facing KPI cards as "(masked)" when §8.3 requires the field **absent**,
not shown-with-no-value; a chart smuggled past §5.2's "no charts" via a "throughput strip";
`Net Profit` shipped as a KPI with no formula anywhere in Foundation; and a build order where
Handover ships in Phase 5 gated on Record Payment, which the same plan schedules for Phase 7
— a warehouse permanently blocked by a balance nobody in the product can take.

**Structural finding, and the one worth remembering:** the design's own decision queue is
roughly twice its true size because it conflates two different things — *"Foundation says X,
a module spec says Y"* (already decided; §0: *"the screen or spec is wrong"*) with *"Foundation
itself declines to answer"* (genuinely Babin's). About half the open items it carried forward
are the first kind and should have been closed as corrections, not queued as decisions.

- ⛔ `--purple-text` (both themes) had no consumer anywhere in `src/`. It was orphaned when
  Today's Utilization card was removed in the §5.2 count-strip rewrite; §4.2 bans the hue
  outright regardless. Deleted from both theme blocks.
- ⛔ The `[data-page='today']` override block referenced `--st-inspection-bg`/`-fg` — tokens
  that stopped existing when v2.0 replaced the eight-token status system with §4.2's five. The
  override had been silently doing nothing since that rewrite. Removed; the comment explains
  why no page-scoped exception is legal under v2.2 regardless.

Verified: `--purple-text` no longer resolves (falls back to inherited colour) · `tsc` clean ·
`npm run build` passes · app mounts and renders.

### Not yet acted on — needs your call before I touch code

The review's "three things to fix before anyone writes a line of code" all require either a
Babin ruling or non-trivial rework, so they're reported, not applied:

1. Re-file roughly half the "open decisions" as already-decided corrections (closes Q1/Q2/Q5/
   Q8/Q9 and the purple/§4.2 class of item in one pass).

## 2026-08-05 — Bug hunt (12 agents); the dead-control class, found again

**Phase:** 1 · **Status:** dead-controls lens fixed; five other lenses triaged

The hunt's `verify:dead-controls` agent died on a session limit, so those 15 findings arrived
**unverified**. I verified them by hand against the code rather than either trusting or
discarding them. Four were real, and one was systemic and mine.

### Fixed

- ⛔ **Nothing in the entire application read the query string.** `grep useSearchParams |
  location.search | URLSearchParams` returned **zero hits**, while I had recently added
  `?queue=` to all five Operations sidebar children, `?queue=`/`?flag=` to Today's four count
  tiles, and `?filter=`/`?when=`/`?view=` to Pulse's four cards. Every one of them navigated,
  highlighted, and **scoped nothing** — the chip lit up and the table below it never moved.
  Operations now derives its filter from the URL, so a queue is linkable, shareable, survives
  a reload, and the sidebar child and the chip cannot disagree. Verified: `?queue=return` deep
  links to 3 rows, sidebar Packing → 2, Cases → 0 (nothing seeded, shown honestly).
- ⛔ **`BookingDetail` ignored `:bookingNo`.** It took no params and rendered the module-level
  `BOOKING` constant, so all 120 rows in the rentals list opened the same record *under that
  record's title*. It now reads the param for its identity, and states plainly when the URL
  names a booking the seed does not have — rather than silently serving another booking's
  money. Verified: `/rentals/BK-2026-0709` titles BK-2026-0709 and says so.
- ⛔ **52 dead `href="#"` links across 13 screens** — the exact class reported as
  *"side bar some pages are not working"*, which had regrown everywhere else. Two had a real
  destination sitting in the same file and are now `<Link>`s: the Operations job table's
  booking numbers (→ `/rentals/:no`, verified) and Packing's Evidence *View All* (→ the
  evidence route its own card already linked 39 lines below). The other 50 point at unbuilt
  screens and are now **stated unavailable** — `aria-disabled` with a reason — matching the
  row-menu pattern. **Zero `href="#"` left anywhere.**

### Note on method

Five lenses had their skeptic; this one did not, and it was the highest-yield of the six. The
findings were specific enough to check in minutes — file, line, and the grep that proves it —
which is what made hand-verification cheap. A finding that cannot be checked that fast is not
worth reporting.

## 2026-08-05 — Base-layer design (15 agents); three real defects found and fixed

**Phase:** 1 · **Status:** designs done, not yet implemented

Ran a 15-agent workflow over `00 Getting Started` to design the five missing engines — Date &
Localization, Validation, Notification, Audit, capability checks. Five readers first, then a
design per engine, then a skeptic per design. **83 of the designs' own decisions were
refuted**, which is the point: the designs that survived are the ones that withstood an
adversarial read against the spec and the existing code.

### Fixed — three defects the workflow found in *shipped* work

- ⛔ **`lib/bs.ts` truncated instants in UTC.** NPT is **UTC+05:45**, so every instant from
  18:15 UTC onward is already tomorrow in Kathmandu — the BS day, the AD day and anything
  derived from them rendered **one day early for 5h45m of every day**. It looked correct only
  because every seeded timestamp is midnight UTC (05:45 NPT), so the window was never crossed;
  it would have started failing the moment real `timestamptz` values arrived. `formatAd` had
  the same defect via `timeZone: 'UTC'`, so the AD line would have disagreed with the BS line
  directly above it. Both now resolve in Asia/Kathmandu.
- ⛔ **`lib/money.ts` blanked the whole app on failure.** Its §2.8 assertion threw at *module
  evaluation* — before `main.tsx` runs, so no ErrorBoundary exists and React never mounts.
  §6 rules that out twice: *"A blank page is never acceptable. 'Something went wrong' is never
  acceptable."* **This happened for real earlier today** — the paisa/rupee rounding bug
  produced an empty `#root` and no message. The check now reports instead of throwing, and
  `main.tsx` renders a stated screen naming the step that broke. The failure is still fatal,
  because §2.8 makes a wrong figure a defect — it is just no longer silent.
- ⛔ **The migrations named one table two ways.** `0002_bookings.sql` had six references to
  `audit_log`, `0003_operations.sql` five to `audit_events`, and **neither file creates it** —
  so the foreign keys could not both resolve. Normalised to `audit_events` (`audit_log_id` →
  `audit_event_id`), matching the later file and the Audit Engine design.

### Found — a spec defect, verified arithmetically

⚠ **`Date Engine.md` §2.1's illustrative row is impossible.** `2083: 31 32 31 32 31 30 30 30
29 30 29 31` sums to **366** and gives Baishakh+Jestha+Ashadh = **94** days. That document's
own §3.2 anchors — 1 Baishakh 2083 = 14 Apr 2026, 1 Shrawan 2083 = 16 Jul 2026 — are exactly
**93** days apart, and BS 2083 totals **365**. The row fails §3.3's own validator on two of
four rules. Seeding it would put every BS date from Shrawan onward one day out — the same
off-by-one `Calendar.md` §4.2 calls the highest-priority correctness bug in the product. The
row is now annotated **DO NOT SEED** in place.

### Open — 58 questions the designs refused to answer for you

Two are contradictions **inside Foundation itself**, not gaps:

- **Does Overdue block Close?** §1.7 lists four close conditions and Overdue is not among
  them; §1.9 says Overdue "blocks Close". Both are in the same document.
- **§1.9's four flag *types* vs §11's three *severities*.** Both encode blocking, no document
  maps one to the other, and they disagree: `Deposit Pending` is type `Attention` but blocks
  Handover, which is Warning severity's job.

The rest cluster on: which published BS table is authoritative and who reloads it each
Baishakh; BS 2078–2095 or 2000–2100; whether BS is materialised as a second column; the
06:00-boundary rule for a delivery note; and the §8.2 role set, which every capability
question is downstream of.

## 2026-08-05 — v2.2 §4.3 revision: fluid scale, three type roles, text-size setting

**Phase:** 1 · **Status:** done

### Did

**The three type roles are now enforced, not just declared.** `.mono` used to mean "every
number" — the pre-v2.2 rule — and applied JetBrains Mono to money, counts, dates and
percentages alike. §4.3.4 narrows the identifier face to *"serials, booking IDs, QR payloads
and PAN… and only they do."* So:

| Class | Face | For |
|---|---|---|
| `.identifier` | JetBrains Mono | serials, booking numbers, VAT/PAN — 17 sites |
| `.figure` | Source Sans 3 + `tabular-nums` | money, counts, times — 314 sites renamed from `.mono` |
| `.kpi-value` | Outfit 700 tabular | headline figures only |

§4.3.2 bars Outfit below 16px, so an inline 12–15px figure keeps the body face and takes only
tabular figures; the display face is reserved for the KPI band. The wordmark and the branch
monogram were caught by the rename and moved to `.title` — they are brand voice, not figures.

**§4.3.6's revised fluid scale.** The fixed ladder is gone. `html` now carries
`clamp(0.9375rem, 0.6875rem + 0.3125vw, 1.0625rem) * var(--ui-scale)`, and all 779 inline
sizes became `rem` tokens, so one variable moves the whole application.

**§4.3.11 text-size setting** — Settings ▸ Appearance ▸ Text size, three options writing
`--ui-scale`, persisted, and applied by an inline script in `index.html` *before first paint*
so nothing reflows on load.

### Verified

- **Root measures 15px at 1280 and 17px at 1920**, exactly as the §4.3.6 table specifies, and
  every token lands on its stated value: h1 31.5 · h2 21.75 · h3 18 · kpi 24 · body 15 ·
  ui 13.95 · meta 12.75 · th 11.25.
- **The root is not a fixed px** — checked explicitly, because `html { font-size: 16px }`
  would override the user's OS/browser text size, and the `rem + vw` middle term is what
  keeps Ctrl+ working (WCAG 1.4.4).
- Text size: Compact 15.3px · Default 17px · Large 19.55px at 1920. Multiplies with the
  viewport clamp rather than replacing it.
- Floor screens measure **exactly 1.10×** on every token.
- **No page-level horizontal scroll on any route**, at any of the three scales.
- **Contrast: 10 routes × 2 themes at 1280, 0 failures.**
- §4.3.7 budget re-measured: **349 KB** against 400 KB.

### Found

- ⛔ **`--ui-scale: 1.1` on a floor screen looked right and moved nothing.** `rem` always
  resolves against the root, and `--ui-scale` is only read by `html { font-size: … }`, so
  setting it on a subtree is inert. The floor step now re-declares the eight `--t-*` tokens
  multiplied by `--floor-step`, which the components actually read. **A CSS variable that
  only one rule consumes cannot be overridden anywhere else** — worth remembering, because
  the wrong version typechecks, renders and silently does nothing.
- **Wide-table overflow is not page overflow.** A first pass flagged 173 elements past the
  viewport on `/rentals` at 1280. Every one was inside an `overflow-x: auto` wrapper — the
  correct pattern. Measuring `documentElement.scrollWidth` and filtering out anything inside
  a scroller gives the real answer: zero.

## 2026-08-05 — v2.0 migration finished; v2.2 typography adopted

**Phase:** 1 · **Status:** done for the v2.0 app migration

### Did

**Every screen is off the migration shim.** `booking.ts`, `rentals.ts`, `operations.ts` and
all five workspace components now hold a `BookingStatus` and a `Flag[]`. The `@deprecated`
`Stage` / `STAGES` / `stageToken` scaffolding is **deleted** from `lib/workflow.ts`; only
`fromRetiredStage` remains, for the schema migration and the §9.6 go-live import.

- **§1.5 — Cleaning is gone as a fifth verb.** The Operations menu is four: Packing ·
  Handover · Return & Inspection · Reset, each gated on the single status §1.5's table gives
  it. The queue list went from six stage-keyed queues — including a "Prep Bay" that §5.1
  deletes outright — to the five that match the sidebar children exactly, keyed on **job**.
  A `Job` now carries a job *and* a status, which is §1.1's three layers made concrete.
- **§2.3 — `lib/money.ts`.** Integer paisa with a branded `Paisa` type, `formatMoney` /
  `parseMoney`, §2.1's calculation order, §2.4 half-up (including negatives, which
  `Math.round` gets wrong for reversals), §2.5's discount gate, and lakh grouping computed
  rather than delegated to `toLocaleString('en-IN')`, which is ICU-build dependent.
  `booking.ts` no longer runs its own arithmetic — §11: "no module recomputes."
- **§5.3 — Reports ▸ Pulse**, four cards in the locked order (Revenue · Cash · Utilization ·
  Exceptions) and one chart. `/reports` now lands here. This is where §5.2's money KPIs went.
- **§5.5 — Scanner FAB**, bottom-right at every width, in the shell rather than `NAV`.
  Six contexts, continuous mode, and **wrong-job modelled as its own state** with haptic
  feedback fired before the banner renders.
- **v2.2 §4.3 typography.** Written into the spec (version bumped to 2.2, §13.2 extended),
  then applied: Outfit 600/700 for headings and figures, **Source Sans 3** 400/600 for body,
  JetBrains Mono for identifiers only, `tabular-nums` on every figure, and Asar/Hind declared
  but **not loaded** so English users never download 1,146 Devanagari glyphs per weight.

### Verified

`tsc` clean · `npm run build` passes · **contrast 10 routes × 2 themes, 0 failures**.

- Fonts resolve as specified: body Source Sans 3 at 15px/22px, headings Outfit 700,
  identifiers JetBrains Mono with `tabular-nums`. Exactly three families loaded — no Asar,
  no Hind.
- **§4.3.6 ladder holds.** Every rendered size across 9 routes is now one of
  12 / 15 / 16 / 20 / 22 / 24 / 26. **Nothing below 12px, no 13px** — down from 625 text
  nodes under 12px and 279 at the banned 13.
- **§4.3.7 budget measured**, because the spec says a target nobody measures is a target
  nobody meets: **348 KB** for JS + CSS + latin-subset fonts against the 400 KB budget.
  (Cyrillic/Greek/Vietnamese subsets ship but are `unicode-range`-gated and never fetched.)
- Pulse renders four cards with lakh grouping; the Scanner FAB is present on every route.

### Found

- ⛔ **The §2.8 reference case failed on the first run, and the assertion caught it.** The app
  refused to mount. In paisa, 1,32,750 × 7% is 9,29,250 paisa exactly — Rs 9,292.50, no
  rounding — so the chain produced a total of **1,39,507**, one rupee above the reference.
  §2.4's "half up at each displayed step" means each step rounds to a **whole rupee**; that
  is the only reading under which §2.8's chain reconciles. Fixed, documented, and the
  assertion stays.
- ⚠ **§4.3.6's ladder is a re-layout, not a find-and-replace.** Snapping 706 sizes moved
  11.5px labels to 12 and 12.5px labels to 15. At the 1920px target this is clean — no
  horizontal overflow, no clipping. It cascaded once: avatar monograms were two stacked
  7.5px lines, and two 12px lines do not fit a 34px circle, so they are one token now.
- ⚠ **I briefly mismeasured this as catastrophic.** A fresh preview tab opened at 648px and
  the first pass reported 152 clipped elements and horizontal page scroll. That was a
  desktop-first app measured at phone width, not the resize breaking it. **Check the viewport
  before believing a layout regression.** The real §7 gap stands separately: mobile 0–767
  needs card-row equivalents for every table, and those are not built.
- **§1.4's mapping is not always the most faithful translation.** Two *completed* deliveries
  carried the retired `Dispatched`, which §1.4 maps to Packed + Partial Pickup — but §1.5
  says the final handover session sets **On Rent**. Followed §1.5. Likewise `Cancelled` maps
  to a flag, and since no seed row records *where* the booking died, it lands on Quote and
  says so rather than inventing a status.

  *derived* from it. Nothing on the page is typed twice.
- **Made every KPI actionable (§5.8).** Six cards, each landing on a pre-filtered view; each
  risk line is a second button with its own destination — §5.2's goes to the **item** list,
  not the booking list. Hover or focus shows the card's **formula, period and source**, and
  Revenue's shows the three at-risk buckets itemised.
- **Built the three things that were simply absent**: the §12 hover card (520px, eleven
  fields, long-press equivalent), the §13 row menu (twelve entries), and the §11 More Filters
  panel behind one entry point with the four locked groups.
- **Restored §6's six-row minimum** and compacted the row so six fit; derived the "+ N more"
  count from the same list.
- **Scoped purple away from everything but Utilization (§14).**
- Added `grouped()` / `rs()` to `lib/format.ts` — South Asian lakh grouping computed, not
  delegated to `toLocaleString('en-IN')`, which is ICU-build dependent.

### Verified

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Driven in the browser at 1920×1080, not read:

- **§4's hard gate, visibly.** ABC Films / BK-2026-0715 reads **09:00 AM · RED Komodo X
  Package · Ready** in the Pickups column *and* on the Timeline. It cannot do otherwise —
  both render the same object, and a loop throws if a booking ever describes itself twice.
- **Counts reconcile.** Pickups 14 = 6 rows + "8 more"; Returns 11 = 6 rows + "5 more";
  Alerts column 5 = Critical Alerts KPI 5; throughput "6 of 25".
- **KPI card → `/operations?queue=pickups&when=today`; risk line →
  `/inventory?status=not-ready&scope=today-pickups`.** Two different destinations from one
  card, as §5.2 requires.
- **Formula card** opens on hover *and* on `focusin`, closes on `focusout`.
- **Hover card measured 520px**, carries all eleven §12 fields, and opens on a 450ms
  long-press.
- **Row menu**: 12 items, exactly §13's list, in order.
- **More Filters**: all four groups, VIP / Deposit Pending / Broadcaster / Consumables
  present, selection count reflected in the bar.
- **Calendar day → `/calendar?d=2026-07-22`**, with the cell labelled "7 Shrawan 2083 —
  22 July 2026, has movements" (BS leads, Latin digits).
- **Purple appears exactly once** on the page — the Utilization icon.
- **Three columns equal height: 686 / 686 / 686.** No clipped text at 1920.
- **Contrast: four consecutive passes alternating light/dark, zero failures.**
- No "customer" anywhere in the DOM; one booking ID format; no star glyphs; six KPI cards.

### Found

- ⛔ **The reference render breaks §4 in the open.** ABC Films' pickup of BK-2026-0715 sits at
  09:00 AM / Ready in the Pickups column and 06:00 AM / Completed on the Timeline — one
  booking, two times, two statuses, on a page whose §4 is titled a hard acceptance gate. The
  old build had copied both.
- ⛔ **The render breaks §5.8 three times.** Pickups 14 over 3 rows + "5 more"; Returns 11
  over 3 rows + "4 more"; Critical Alerts 5 beside 5 alerts + "2 more".
- ⛔ **Purple was leaking through the status token.** `--st-inspection-*` is purple, which is
  correct on Inventory and in the Operations queues but put purple on an inspection return
  and on the Inspection Pending alert here. Scoped per page rather than changed globally.
- **⚠ §5.7 does not reconcile with §5.2/§5.3.** "12 of 25": the 25 is exactly 14 + 11, but
  the 12 is not derivable — 6 pickups are completed and all 11 returns are open. Derived to
  6 and logged. **TODO(decision), PLAN.md §4.**
- **⚠ §2 asks for two incompatible things** — "minimum 6 rows per column" and "no scrolling
  on desktop". The 6-row minimum wins; the page runs ~1471px at 1080.
- **§17 says radius 14px.** The app is 16px everywhere via Theme Design System v1.0. Kept at
  16 — a one-page radius would break shell consistency, and the design system outranks a
  module page spec.
### A 12-agent spec audit caught four things I had verified wrong

Ran the finished page back through a parallel audit (six auditors by spec section, each
adversarially verified). 42 gaps survived verification; most were against the pre-rewrite
file — the verifiers refuted all 9 "columns" findings as already fixed. Four were real
against the shipped code, and one of them my own browser check had passed:

- ⛔ **§12's long-press was unreachable on touch — and my test said it worked.** I had
  dispatched `touchstart` alone. A real touch also emits a synthetic click on lift, and the
  row's `onClick` navigated to the booking the instant the card appeared. There was also no
  drag-cancel and no way to dismiss (a touch user gets no `mouseleave`). Fixed with a
  `suppress` ref that swallows exactly that click, `onTouchMove`/`onTouchCancel`, and an
  outside-tap + Escape dismissal. **Re-verified with the full sequence:** hold → card opens;
  lift → stays on `/today` with the card open; drag → cancels; short tap → still navigates.
  *Lesson: a synthetic event that skips the gesture's own side effects proves nothing.*
- ⛔ **Purple was still on the page as a raw hex.** Four rows carried `avatarBg: '#4c1d95'`.
  My purple check compared against `--purple` (`rgb(124,58,237)`) and `#4c1d95` is a
  different violet, so it passed. Avatar fills are now named constants, and the check is a
  **violet-family** test (blue leads green by >45 and red leads green) rather than one exact
  token. Exactly one violet remains: the Utilization icon.
- **§5.8's monospace rule was half-applied.** The headline figures were `.mono`; the risk
  lines, the secondary lines and the throughput strip were not — two currency figures on one
  card in two faces.
- **§11's filters looked live and moved nothing** — the same defect class as the sidebar
  links that did not navigate. The chips now scope both columns, unsupported options are
  inert with a stated reason, and a period with no seeded data says so instead of silently
  showing everything.

Also from the audit: §11's **Status group** was missing — I had dropped it and written a
paragraph explaining why, when only its *values* were superseded. It is back, populated from
the twelve Foundation stages. §13's menu entries and §12's quick actions were dead; the ones
that need no engine are wired (Open, Edit, Print Checklist, Packing List, Invoice, Copy
Booking Number) and the rest are explicitly unavailable with a reason rather than silent
no-ops. §9's dot now reads the same stage category the badge does, so the two cannot disagree.

- **A much better contrast harness.** The old one polled until the painted body background
  matched the theme. That still produced ~220 phantom failures here, because the Browser pane
  throttles compositing between tool calls and a transition can sit mid-flight for *seconds* —
  even with `--dur-theme: 0ms`, which does not cancel an already-running transition. Injecting
  `*, *::before, *::after { transition: none !important }` before measuring cancels them
  outright. Four alternating passes then returned zero. **Use the kill-switch, not a wait.**

## 2026-08-05 — Evidence Workspace built; the mandatory-evidence gate closed and driven

**Phase:** 1 · **Status:** done

### Did

- **Ruling recorded and implemented — evidence is mandatory before Complete Packing.**
  `Evidence Workspace.md` §20 left it open. The answer is **yes**, at §14's granularity:
  *one photo per packed case, not per item.* A per-item rule would demand 18 photos for a
  single booking. `Unit` therefore carries a `case` (`Pelican 1610` · `Lens Case` ·
  `Accessories Case`) and `CASES` is derived from the unit list, like `GROUPS`.
- **`PackingWorkspace` gained a third gate branch.** Only cases *holding a packed item*
  need a photo, so an empty case can never block completion. The panel shows per-case
  coverage with its own `Take Photo` action and links to the Evidence Workspace.
- **Built `src/modules/rentals/EvidenceWorkspace.tsx`** at
  `/rentals/:bookingNo/evidence`, from v1.1's corrections rather than the render.
- **Fixed four contrast defects found by a stricter sweep** (below).

### Verified

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Driven in the browser, not read:

- **The gate, end to end.** Bulk Scan → `1 required item not yet packed` (the
  Cleaning-blocked 85mm) → mark it Missing → `1 missing item needs a reason of at least 10
  characters` → reason typed → **`3 packed cases need a photo — Pelican 1610, Lens Case,
  Accessories Case`** → one photo → `2 packed cases…` → all three → `Complete Packing`
  enables. Each step read off the live DOM.
- **Soft remove.** A 3-character reason is refused; a valid one archives the photo, Total
  falls 10 → 9, Matched 6 → 5, the `Archived (1)` card appears, and the §6 invariant
  (`Matched + Review + Unmatched = Total`) still holds.
- **Bulk bar.** Selecting two photos raises the bar reading `2 selected` with §9's seven
  actions; `Clear` dismisses it.
- **Contrast, 24 routes × 2 themes: clean.** The sweep was strengthened to resolve
  `background-image` gradients (taking the *lightest* stop as the worst case), which the
  previous colour-only walk skipped entirely.

### Found

- ⭐ **`Photo.product` is absent, not hidden, when unmatched.** §7.3 says an Unmatched card
  shows no product name and no serial; the render badged `Portkeys Monitor · PKM-001`
  **Unmatched**. Modelling the product as optional makes the contradiction unrepresentable,
  and `matchState()` derives the badge from the evidence so a card cannot argue with itself.
- **Four real contrast failures, all pre-existing, all now fixed:**
  · header avatar — white initials on `#475569→#94a3b8`; the light end measured **2.59:1**.
    Regraded to `#334155→#475569` (worst end 7.58:1). The old sweep never saw it because it
    ignored `background-image`.
  · notification badge — white on dark-theme `--danger` `#ef4444` = **3.76:1**. Now the
    AA-verified `--st-damage` pair.
  · `--disabled` `#9ca3af` used as *text* — calendar spill days, the `•` and `·`
    separators, the footer `|` — **2.54:1**. All moved to `--muted`; the two separators are
    now `aria-hidden` as well, since a screen reader was announcing them.
  · `--blue` as text on the dark card = **4.4996:1**, a thousandth under AA. `theme.css`
    already documents this exact case; `KpiRow` was simply still on the raw token.
- **A selected-row pattern that fails twice.** `--muted` on `--nav-active-bg` `#eef4ff` is
  **4.38:1**. It bit the Evidence Categories list and Numbering's Sequence Categories, both
  fixed to `--text2` when selected. Worth checking any future list that dims a count on a
  tinted active row.
- **One false positive worth remembering.** `/reports/inventory` reported five failures at
  4.39:1 on backgrounds like `rgb(242,244,247)` — values that are not tokens. It was the
  200 ms theme transition again, sampled on a slow page: the settle loop watched `body`
  while an inner surface was still interpolating. A 1,200 ms settle is clean. **Suspect the
  harness whenever a reported background is not a real token.**

  is not built. No dead links, and nothing pretends to be a finished empty screen.
